1.title: Ruling of Bishop Lee, Philippine Annual Conference
1.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that lay missionaries, even though designated as 'Associate Members' of an Annual Conference, cannot vote in elections for ministerial delegates to General Conference because they remain lay members.
1.keyHolding: Lay missionaries designated as 'Associate Members' of an Annual Conference retain their lay status and cannot vote in elections for ministerial delegates to General Conference.

2.title: In Re: A. Lincoln Shute
2.summary: A minister appealed a bishop's rulings about pension laws from before church unification. The Judicial Council dismissed the appeal as moot since new laws had been enacted and no rights were affected.
2.keyHolding: Appeals become moot when new legislation has superseded the issues in question and no vested rights of the appellant are affected.
2.outcome: Affirmed - appeal dismissed as moot, bishop's rulings upheld

3.title: Appeal of Willard L. Hadsell
3.summary: A minister who was properly located by his Annual Conference but then defied church authority by continuing to preach at his former charge for over a year forfeited his right to appeal, despite being improperly denied the right to speak at conference.
3.keyHolding: A member may forfeit his right of appeal by contumacious treatment of the Church and its authority, including deliberate defiance of conference actions.
3.outcome: Appeal dismissed - appellant forfeited right to appeal through misconduct

4.title: Tenure of Central Conference Bishops
4.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that Central Conferences have the constitutional authority to elect bishops for limited terms, not just for life tenure.
4.keyHolding: Central Conferences may constitutionally elect bishops for limited terms as this practice was part of the historic episcopacy of The Methodist Episcopal Church and is preserved in the current Constitution.
4.parties: majority of the Council of Bishops

5.title: Election of Delegates to Jurisdictional Conferences by Mission Conferences
5.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that Mission Conferences cannot elect delegates to Jurisdictional Conferences because only Annual Conferences have this constitutional right.
5.keyHolding: Mission Conferences do not have the constitutional authority to elect delegates to Jurisdictional Conferences, as this right is reserved exclusively to Annual Conferences.
5.parties: One fifth of the members of the General Conference
5.outcome: Unconstitutional - Mission Conference delegate election provision struck down

6.title: Election of Delegates to Central Conferences by Mission Conferences
6.summary: The General Conference passed legislation allowing Mission Conferences to elect delegates to Central Conferences, but the Judicial Council ruled this unconstitutional because only Annual Conferences have the right to elect delegates to these higher conferences.
6.keyHolding: Only Annual Conferences, as the basic body of the Church, have the constitutional right to elect delegates to Central Conferences, not Mission Conferences.
6.parties: One fifth of the members of the General Conference
6.outcome: Unconstitutional - Mission Conferences cannot elect delegates to Central Conferences

7.title: Constitutionality of Provision Fixing Retirement Age of Ministers
7.summary: The General Conference has the constitutional authority to set a mandatory retirement age of 72 for ministers. This ruling established that retirement age is a connectional matter under General Conference jurisdiction.
7.keyHolding: The General Conference has constitutional authority to legislate on ministerial retirement age as a connectional matter affecting uniform regulations throughout the Church.
7.parties: More than one-fifth of General Conference members appealing the constitutionality
7.outcome: Constitutional - General Conference authority to set mandatory retirement age at 72 upheld

8.title: Status of Ministers of Former Methodist Protestant Church Left Permanently Without Appointment
8.summary: The Judicial Council determined that ordained ministers from the former Methodist Protestant Church who were left permanently without appointments have the same status as "located" ministers in The Methodist Church.
8.keyHolding: Unstationed ministers from the former Methodist Protestant Church hold the same relation to Annual Conference as located ministers under The Methodist Church Discipline.
8.parties: G. E. Williams requesting ruling from Bishop Edwin H. Hughes at Baltimore Annual Conference
8.outcome: Affirmed - Bishop's ruling that such ministers hold the relation of located preachers was affirmed

9.title: Compensation of Retired Minister Serving as Supply Pastor
9.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that an Annual Conference cannot make a blanket rule limiting pension payments to retired ministers serving as supply pastors without following proper procedures for individual claim reviews.
9.keyHolding: Annual Conferences must follow Disciplinary procedures requiring individual review, opportunity for claimant response, and two-thirds vote approval when disallowing or reducing annuity claims.
9.parties: Rev. C. Oscar Ford requesting ruling on New England Conference action
9.outcome: Affirmed bishop's ruling that the conference rule was illegal for violating Disciplinary procedures

10.title: Eligibility of Member of Annual Conference Board of Lay Activities to Membership on Annual Conference Commission on World Service and Finance
10.summary: District Lay Leaders cannot serve on the Annual Conference Commission on World Service and Finance because they are members of the Board of Lay Activities, which requests funding from that Commission.
10.keyHolding: Members of boards that request appropriations from the Annual Conference Commission on World Service and Finance are ineligible to serve on that Commission to prevent conflicts of interest.
10.parties: Conference Lay Leader requesting ruling on District Lay Leader eligibility
10.outcome: Reversed - Bishop's decision was in error; District Lay Leaders are ineligible for Commission membership

11.title: In Re: Board of Trustees, Missouri Annual Conference
11.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that Missouri Annual Conference trustees need not be incorporated due to state constitutional restrictions, but can still function as an unincorporated board to handle abandoned church property.
11.keyHolding: Annual Conference trustees may operate as an unincorporated board when state law prohibits religious corporations, and such unincorporated trustees have authority to recover possession of abandoned church property.
11.parties: Board of Trustees, Missouri Annual Conference
11.outcome: Affirmed bishop's ruling that trustees need not be incorporated but can perform duties as unincorporated board

12.title: Authority of a Joint Distributing Committee Appointed Under the Provisions of Paragraph 1312 of the Discipline of 1939
12.summary: When Methodist conferences merged in Kansas in 1939, a Joint Distributing Committee was created to allocate pension funds and claimants between the new conference boundaries. The Judicial Council ruled that this committee's decisions are binding on the affected conferences.
12.keyHolding: Decisions of a Joint Distributing Committee properly constituted under Paragraph 1312 are binding upon all conferences affected by merger and boundary changes.
12.parties: Kansas Conference and Central Kansas Conference of The Methodist Church
12.outcome: Joint Distributing Committee decisions upheld as binding and within proper authority

13.title: Recommendations for Apportionments for Conference Claimants by Annual Conference Board of Conference Claimants
13.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that Conference Claimants boards can recommend their financial apportionments directly to Annual Conference without going through the Commission on World Service and Finance first.
13.keyHolding: When interpreting conflicting disciplinary provisions, the entire legislation must be considered as a whole to determine legislative intent, not just isolated paragraphs.
13.parties: Wyoming Annual Conference Commission on World Service and Finance
13.outcome: Affirmed - Bishop's ruling upheld that Conference Claimants boards report directly to Annual Conference

14.title: Appeal of Board of Missions and Church Extension on Question of Responsibility of Pension of D. W. Nichols, et al.
14.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that an Annual Conference is not responsible for pension payments covering years a minister served in a Mission Conference, even if the minister later retired from that Annual Conference.
14.keyHolding: Annual Conferences are only responsible for pension annuities for years of service performed within their own conference boundaries, not for service in Mission Conferences.
14.parties: Board of Missions and Church Extension
14.outcome: The Southern California-Arizona Conference was not liable for D. W. Nichols' pension for years served in Mission Conference from 1888-1904

15.title: Constitutionality of Paragraph 231, Discipline 1940
15.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed that the mandatory retirement of ministers at age 72 under Paragraph 231 is constitutional and binding on Annual Conferences.
15.keyHolding: Annual Conferences must comply with the mandatory retirement age provisions of Paragraph 231, as the Judicial Council has sole authority to determine constitutionality and previously ruled this provision constitutional.
15.parties: Paul Barton requesting ruling on behalf of three retired ministers (W. C. Franasco, H. T. McGrew, and E. J. Speer)
15.outcome: Bishop's ruling affirmed - mandatory retirement at age 72 is constitutional and binding

16.title: Status of T. H. Osborne, North Texas Annual Conference
16.summary: A former Methodist minister who withdrew and became a Baptist minister could legally be considered for readmission as a minister from another church, even with unresolved complaints from his previous Methodist ministry. The Annual Conference retained final authority to accept or reject such admission.
16.keyHolding: A minister who withdraws from The Methodist Church and joins another denomination may legally apply for readmission under provisions for ministers from other churches, regardless of unresolved complaints from their previous Methodist ministry.
16.parties: T. H. Osborne and North Texas Annual Conference
16.outcome: Bishop's ruling affirmed that the minister could legally be considered for admission from another church

17.title: Costs of Jurisdictional Committee of Appeals
17.summary: A Jurisdictional Conference requested that the General Commission on World Service and Finance pay expenses for a Committee of Appeals hearing, but the Judicial Council ruled the General Administration Fund cannot pay these costs because no specific provision exists in church law.
17.keyHolding: The General Commission on World Service and Finance has no authority to pay expenses of Jurisdictional Committees of Appeals from the General Administration Fund because no specific provision exists in church law authorizing such payment.
17.parties: College of Bishops of the Northeastern Jurisdiction
17.outcome: Appeal not sustained - General Administration Fund cannot pay jurisdictional appeal expenses

18.title: C. M. Tyndal
18.summary: A minister who surrendered his credentials under complaint cannot have them restored by Annual Conference until he first obtains a local preacher's license and follows proper restoration procedures.
18.keyHolding: An Annual Conference cannot restore ministerial credentials to someone who is not licensed to preach, as it can only restore rights and privileges it originally bestowed.
18.outcome: Bishop's ruling affirmed - restoration cannot proceed until proper prerequisites are met

19.title: Distributions from Endowment Fund for Superannuates, Held by the Missouri Corporation
19.summary: Retired ministers who served in the Methodist Episcopal Church, South before 1939 unification are entitled to pension benefits from the Missouri Corporation fund based on their pre-unification service, even if they later served in conferences assigned to the Illinois Corporation. However, ministers have no vested legal rights to these pension funds.
19.keyHolding: Ministers retain entitlement to pension benefits from the Missouri Corporation's Endowment Fund for pre-unification service in the Methodist Episcopal Church, South, but have no vested contractual rights to such funds.
19.parties: California Annual Conference ministers seeking pension distributions
19.outcome: Bishop's ruling affirmed except for finding that ministers have no vested equity rights in pension funds

20.title: Pension Claim, Mrs. A. S. Gregg
20.summary: A widow sought a pension based on her deceased husband's ministry years, but the Judicial Council ruled she could not claim pension rights that her voluntarily located husband never had.
20.keyHolding: A widow cannot claim pension rights that her deceased voluntarily located minister husband did not possess at the time of his death.
20.parties: Mrs. A. S. Gregg (widow) and North-East Ohio Conference
20.outcome: Bishop's ruling reversed - widow denied pension claim

21.title: Election of Missionary Bishops by General Conference
21.summary: The General Conference cannot elect Missionary Bishops because the Constitution only allows Jurisdictional and Central Conferences to elect bishops.
21.keyHolding: The General Conference lacks constitutional authority to elect bishops, as this power is exclusively granted to Jurisdictional and Central Conferences.
21.parties: Appeal by more than the necessary number from General Conference resolution

22.title: Membership of Bishops in Annual Conferences
22.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that bishops, whether active or retired, are not members of Annual Conferences and should not be counted for statistical or voting purposes.
22.keyHolding: Bishops, effective or retired, are not members of Annual Conferences and should not be counted in Conference membership statistics or voting calculations.
22.parties: Central New York Conference (requesting ruling on bishop membership status)
22.outcome: Affirmed the Bishop's ruling that bishops are not Annual Conference members

23.title: General Pension Regulations
23.summary: The Judicial Council declined to interpret pension regulations, stating that while General Conference is in session, it should clarify its own unclear legislation rather than leaving interpretation to the courts.
23.keyHolding: The Judicial Council does not have legislative power and cannot interpret General Conference legislation while the General Conference is still in session to clarify its own enactments.
23.parties: General Conference requesting interpretation of pension regulations
23.outcome: No Jurisdiction - request returned to General Conference for self-clarification

24.title: Constitutionality of Paragraph 924 as to Lay Missionaries
24.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that lay missionaries serving outside the United States cannot be given voting rights in Annual Conferences because the Constitution strictly limits conference membership to traveling preachers and lay members elected by pastoral charges.
24.keyHolding: Only laymen elected by pastoral charges are eligible for membership in Annual Conference, and membership alone determines the right to vote on matters before the conference.
24.parties: L. O. Hartman on behalf of General Conference
24.outcome: Unconstitutional - voting rights for lay missionaries struck down, seating privileges upheld

25.title: Conscientious Objectors
25.summary: The 1944 General Conference modified the church's peace statement, but this did not eliminate protection for Methodist conscientious objectors claiming military service exemption. The protection remains through another unchanged paragraph in the Social Creed.
25.keyHolding: Changes to one disciplinary paragraph do not affect identical provisions in another paragraph unless specifically repealed.
25.outcome: Conscientious objector protections remain in effect despite peace statement modifications

26.title: Meaning of 'Church Members'
26.summary: The Board of Publication asked the Judicial Council to define whether 'church members' includes both laymen and ministers for purposes of jurisdictional representation. The Council declined to interpret this term, stating it is a legislative matter for General Conference to define.
26.keyHolding: Defining the meaning of 'church members' in the Discipline is a legislative function of General Conference, not a judicial interpretation matter for the Judicial Council.
26.outcome: No Jurisdiction - referred matter back to General Conference as legislative function

27.title: Pension Case, Mississippi Conference
27.summary: A retired minister who served in multiple Methodist denominations before church unification in 1939 can count all his years of effective service toward his pension annuity calculation. The 1944 General Conference changed the pension rules to include service in predecessor Methodist churches.
27.keyHolding: Years of effective service in predecessor Methodist denominations prior to the 1939 Uniting Conference should be included in calculating a retired minister's annuity claim under the new Pension Code.
27.parties: General Conference requesting declaratory decision regarding Mississippi Conference retired minister
27.outcome: Minister entitled to include all years of effective service from predecessor Methodist churches in annuity calculation

28.title: Boundaries, Baltimore and Central Pennsylvania Annual Conferences
28.summary: The Northeastern Jurisdictional Conference attempted to delegate its constitutional power to determine conference boundaries to the Baltimore and Central Pennsylvania Annual Conferences, but the Judicial Council ruled this delegation unconstitutional.
28.keyHolding: Jurisdictional Conferences cannot delegate their constitutional power to determine Annual Conference boundaries to the Annual Conferences themselves.
28.parties: Norman M. Moss appealing action of Northeastern Jurisdictional Conference
28.outcome: Unconstitutional - delegation of boundary determination power ruled invalid

29.title: Powers of Trustees, Fourth Street First Methodist Church, Wheeling, W. Va.
29.summary: A local church board of trustees cannot directly petition the Judicial Council for a declaratory decision about their authority to establish a trust for church property received through a bequest.
29.keyHolding: Local church boards of trustees do not have the right to appeal directly to the Judicial Council and therefore cannot petition for declaratory decisions.
29.parties: Board of Trustees of Fourth Street First Methodist Church, Wheeling, W. Va.
29.outcome: No Jurisdiction - Board of Trustees lacks standing to petition Judicial Council directly

30.title: Apportionment for World Service - Holston Annual Conference
30.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that the General Conference has constitutional authority to set World Service apportionments, even if they seem unfair to particular conferences. The General Conference's request for annual contributions 10% above previous year's contributions was legal and binding.
30.keyHolding: The General Conference has constitutional power under Article IV, Section 9 to determine and provide for raising funds necessary for connectional work, including setting World Service apportionments.
30.outcome: Affirmed - Bishop's ruling that General Conference action was legal and binding was upheld

31.title: Interpretation of Paragraph 411, Discipline 1944
31.summary: All ministers coming from other churches must meet Methodist educational standards for ordination, regardless of which provision they apply under in the Discipline.
31.keyHolding: Ministers from other evangelical churches must meet the same educational standards required of Methodist ministers in all cases, without exception.
31.outcome: Affirmed - Bishop's ruling that all ministers from other churches must meet Methodist educational standards was upheld

32.title: Appeal of the Northeastern Jurisdictional Conference on Its Own Action Involving a Change in Jurisdictional Lines: Boundaries of Delaware Conference
32.summary: The Northeastern Jurisdictional Conference attempted to change conference boundaries affecting Negro work in multiple states, but the Judicial Council ruled they lacked authority since General Conference had only granted permission to the Central Jurisdiction to make such changes.
32.keyHolding: Jurisdictional Conference boundaries can only be changed by General Conference with consent of Annual Conferences in each affected jurisdiction, and authorization granted to one jurisdiction does not extend to another.
32.parties: Northeastern Jurisdictional Conference (appealing its own action); Dr. John B. F. Yoak, Jr. (appellant); Dr. Frederick B. Newell (respondent)
32.outcome: Conference action exceeded its authority under the General Conference enabling act

33.title: Ruling of Bishop G. Bromley Oxnam, in Response to a Request From Hallam Richardson During the New York East Annual Conference
33.summary: A church member requested the bishop to rule on hypothetical questions about Methodist doctrine regarding military service and conscientious objectors. The Judicial Council affirmed the bishop's refusal to answer, establishing that bishops cannot rule on hypothetical questions.
33.keyHolding: Bishops may only rule on legal questions arising from actual or proposed conference actions, not on hypothetical questions or requests for information.
33.parties: Hallam Richardson requesting ruling from Bishop G. Bromley Oxnam
33.outcome: Affirmed - Bishop's refusal to rule on hypothetical questions upheld

34.title: Ruling of Bishop Charles C. Selecman in North Texas Annual Conference as to Casting of Ballot by Secretary of a District Conference Under Paragraphs 670-673, Discipline 1944
34.summary: A District Conference cannot authorize its Secretary to cast a ballot on behalf of the entire conference for licensing preachers or recommending ordination candidates. When the Discipline requires voting by ballot, each member must cast their own secret ballot.
34.keyHolding: When the Discipline requires votes to be taken by ballot for licensing to preach or ordination recommendations, authorizing one person to cast the ballot for the entire District Conference is illegal and null and void.
34.parties: George C. French requesting ruling on Dallas District Conference actions
34.outcome: Affirmed - Bishop's ruling that District Conference actions were illegal was upheld

35.title: Voting of Retired Bishops
35.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that retired bishops may participate in the Council of Bishops but without voting rights, as authorized by the General Conference's constitutional power to define episcopal duties and privileges.
35.keyHolding: The General Conference has constitutional authority to restrict retired bishops' voting rights in the Council of Bishops under its power to define episcopal powers, duties, and privileges.
35.outcome: Constitutional - General Conference authority to restrict retired bishops' voting rights upheld

36.title: Ruling of Bishop G. Bromley Oxnam regarding legality of abbreviated New York Annual Conference session
36.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that a wartime abbreviated one-day Annual Conference session was legal even though attendance was discouraged, because Annual Conferences have no quorum requirement.
36.keyHolding: Annual Conferences have no quorum requirement and any number of members meeting at the officially appointed time and place can conduct legal business.
36.parties: Ross A. Cobb, a Lay Member of the New York Annual Conference
36.outcome: Bishop's ruling affirmed that the abbreviated conference session was legal

37.title: Executive Sessions of an Annual Conference Excluding Lay Members
37.summary: Lay members of an Annual Conference challenged their exclusion from executive sessions, questioning whether this violated the Constitution. The Judicial Council declined to rule, stating they lack jurisdiction to hear constitutional challenges initiated by Annual Conferences.
37.keyHolding: The Judicial Council lacks jurisdiction to rule on constitutional questions when the request originates solely from an Annual Conference.
37.parties: Nathan Newby and lay members of the Southern California-Arizona Annual Conference
37.outcome: No Jurisdiction - Judicial Council determined it lacked authority to rule on constitutional questions initiated by Annual Conferences

38.title: In Re: Corporate Meetings, Central Kansas Annual Conference
38.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that when an Annual Conference incorporates under state law, it must follow corporate procedures for meetings, but once properly convened, it retains all its original ecclesiastical powers including the ability to amend its corporate charter and bylaws.
38.keyHolding: An incorporated Annual Conference retains all its ecclesiastical powers and cannot delegate away its basic authority as the fundamental body of The Methodist Church, even through incorporation under state law.
38.parties: Central Kansas Annual Conference, Bishop William C. Martin
38.outcome: Affirmed with clarification regarding corporate procedures and ecclesiastical authority

39.title: Request by the Council of Bishops for a Declaratory Decision as to the Legality of the Resolution Adopted by the General Conference of 1944, Relative to the Origin of The Methodist Church
39.summary: The Judicial Council declined to rule on whether The Methodist Church should officially date its origin from 1784 or 1939, finding no constitutional issue at stake. However, they clarified that while organized Methodism began in 1784, the current Methodist Church organization was created in 1939 through union.
39.keyHolding: The Judicial Council lacks jurisdiction over non-constitutional questions, but the present organization of The Methodist Church began in 1939 under the Declaration of Union.
39.outcome: No Jurisdiction - not a constitutional question, but clarified that current Methodist Church organization began in 1939

40.title: Voting by Retired Bishops
40.summary: The Judicial Council reaffirmed its previous decision that retired bishops cannot vote, upholding the constitutionality of the rule limiting retired bishops' participation.
40.keyHolding: The constitutional limitation on voting rights of retired bishops as specified in Paragraph 437 of the 1944 Discipline is valid and enforceable.
40.parties: Bishop John M. Moore (petitioner for rehearing), with supporting briefs from Bishop A. Frank Smith and Bishop E. H. Hughes
40.outcome: Affirmed - previous decision upholding constitutionality of voting restrictions on retired bishops was reaffirmed without change

41.title: Footnote to Article XXIII Articles of Religion
41.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that a footnote about Christian obedience to civil authority attached to Article XXIII of the Articles of Religion was not part of the constitutional Articles of Religion, but was added only by legislative action.
41.keyHolding: The footnote to Article XXIII of the Articles of Religion is not a constitutional part of the Articles of Religion but was added by legislative act only.
41.outcome: Footnote ruled not constitutional part of Articles of Religion

42.title: Executive Sessions of Annual Conference Excluding Lay Members; Constitutionality of Paragraph 646, Discipline 1944
42.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that Annual Conferences can hold executive sessions limited to ministerial members when discussing ordination, character, and conference relations matters, even though this excludes lay members from participation.
42.keyHolding: Paragraph 646 of the 1944 Discipline allowing executive sessions of ministerial members only for matters of ordination, character, and conference relations is constitutional.
42.parties: Southern California-Arizona Conference via Council of Bishops

43.title: Bishop Costen J. Harrell's Decision at North Alabama Annual Conference on Whether or Not the Annual Conference May Exclude Retired Members From Service on Boards, Commissions and Committees
43.summary: The North Alabama Annual Conference can adopt rules preventing retired ministers from serving on boards and commissions because retirement means relief from active duties and responsibilities.
43.keyHolding: Annual Conferences have the authority under Paragraph 631 to adopt standing rules that exclude retired ministers from serving on boards and commissions, as such service constitutes active duty from which retired ministers are relieved.
43.parties: W. F. Price and others requesting episcopal ruling
43.outcome: Affirmed - Annual Conference rule excluding retired ministers from quadrennial boards and commissions is constitutional

44.title: Annual Recommendations for District Superintendents' Support, Paragraph 788
44.summary: The North Alabama Conference's standing rule setting district superintendents' salaries violated church law because superintendents' support must be recommended annually by the Conference Commission on World Service and Finance, not set by permanent conference rules.
44.keyHolding: District Superintendents' support must be estimated and recommended annually by the Conference Commission on World Service and Finance and cannot be predetermined by conference standing rules.
44.parties: Chairman of the North Alabama Conference Commission on World Service and Finance
44.outcome: Bishop ruled that the conference standing rule violated Paragraph 788 by predetermining superintendents' salaries instead of requiring annual recommendations

45.title: The Decision of Bishop Magee in the Illinois Annual Conference, on the Right of Annual Conference to Make Appropriations Out of Its Benevolence Funds to Organizations on the Governing Boards of which the Annual Conference Has No Representation
45.summary: The Illinois Annual Conference asked whether it could give benevolence funds to organizations where the conference had no representation on their governing boards. The Judicial Council affirmed that annual conferences may make such appropriations.
45.keyHolding: Annual conferences are not required to have representation on the governing boards of organizations to which they make appropriations from conference benevolence funds.
45.parties: Board of Education of Illinois Annual Conference

46.title: Ruling of Bishop Titus Lowe in Indiana Annual Conference as to Fractional Years of Service Under Pension Regulations Interpreting Paragraph 1618 Discipline 1944
46.summary: The Judicial Council reviewed a bishop's ruling on pension calculations when conference sessions changed timing, creating a shorter service year. The Council upheld the disciplinary formula for calculating fractional years of service for pension purposes.
46.keyHolding: The disciplinary formula for calculating fractional years of service applies universally to all pension calculations, including cases where conference session changes created shorter service years.
46.parties: Indiana Annual Conference through A. M. Brown, Chairman of the Board of Conference Claimants
46.outcome: Bishop's interpretation affirmed regarding the universal application of fractional year calculations for pension service credit

47.title: Appeal of Edwin L. Morgan From Judgment of Committee on Appeals, Southeastern Jurisdiction
47.summary: A minister found guilty of writing bad checks in 1941 tried to appeal to the Judicial Council in 1947, but the Council dismissed his appeal because new appeal rights created in 1944 could not be applied retroactively to his case.
47.keyHolding: Laws allowing appeals to the Judicial Council are prospective only and cannot be applied retroactively to cases decided before the law became effective.

48.title: Petition of Bishops of Western Jurisdiction as to Assignment of a Bishop to Supervision of Missions
48.summary: The Western Jurisdiction asked if they could assign a bishop to oversee missions and provisional conferences even if those areas overlap with other bishops' territories. The Judicial Council said yes, bishops can be assigned based on function rather than just geography.
48.keyHolding: Episcopal areas can be defined functionally rather than geographically, allowing jurisdictional conferences to assign bishops to supervise missions and provisional conferences regardless of territorial overlap.
48.parties: Bishops James C. Baker, Wilbur E. Hammaker and Bruce R. Baxter of the Western Jurisdiction
48.outcome: Jurisdictional Conference has the legal right to assign a bishop to supervision of missions and provisional conferences even with territorial overlap

49.title: Ruling of Bishop Arthur F. Wesley in the River Plate Annual Conference as to Time Requirements for Preachers on Trial Before Admission into Full Connection Interpreting Paragraph 341 Discipline 1944
49.summary: A bishop ruled that seminary students who served as pastors could be received on trial and into full membership at the same conference session, but the Judicial Council reversed this, requiring the full two-year trial period first.
49.keyHolding: Before a preacher may be admitted into full connection in the Annual Conference, they must first have been received on trial and have remained on trial for at least two successive years prior to admission into full connection.
49.parties: River Plate Annual Conference appealing Bishop Arthur F. Wesley's ruling
49.outcome: Reversed - Bishop's decision was not in accord with the Discipline

50.title: Ruling of Bishop C. C. Selecman in the North Texas Annual Conference Relating to Assessment of the Conference for Conference Claimants, Under Pars. 1618, 1623, and 1624 of the Discipline
50.summary: The North Texas Annual Conference set pension rates and collected more money than needed for that year's payments, intending to save the excess for future pension obligations. A member challenged whether the conference could withhold current excess funds from current retirees.
50.keyHolding: Annual Conferences have the authority to collect pension apportionments in excess of current year needs and create reserve funds for future pension obligations.
50.parties: George C. French challenging Bishop Selecman's ruling
50.outcome: Bishop's decision affirmed - conference acted within its rights to create pension reserve fund

51.title: Ruling of Bishop William C. Martin at 1947 Session of Nebraska Annual Conference Relating to Payment of Pastors' Expenses as Affected by Provisions of Par. 1624, Art. 11, Sec. 4 of the Discipline of The Methodist Church in the Year 1944
51.summary: The Nebraska Conference could provide travel expense allowances to pastors without violating proportional payment rules, as long as these were actual expenses and not disguised salary supplements.
51.keyHolding: Travel expense allowances to pastors do not constitute supplementary compensation that defeats proportional payment requirements if they represent actual expenses and are not used to conceal additional salary payments.

52.title: Appeal by Quarterly Conference of First Methodist Church of North Little Rock, Ark., As to Advancements from the Board of Church Extension
52.summary: A local church's Quarterly Conference tried to appeal to the Judicial Council about a property dispute with the Board of Church Extension. The Judicial Council ruled that Quarterly Conferences do not have the right to appeal to them.
52.keyHolding: A Quarterly Conference of a local church is not an authority in the church that has the right to appeal to the Judicial Council.
52.parties: Quarterly Conference of First Methodist Church of North Little Rock, Arkansas

53.title: Right of Central Conference Bishop to Vote In the Council of Bishops
53.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that Central Conference bishops can vote in the Council of Bishops when matters affect their conferences or all Central Conferences collectively.
53.keyHolding: Central Conference bishops have constitutional voting rights in the Council of Bishops on matters involving their own Central Conference or interests common to all Central Conferences.

54.title: Re-enactment of Enabling Acts Adopted By General Conference of 1940 and 1944
54.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that General Conference legislation remains in effect until specifically repealed or amended, so Enabling Acts from 1940 and 1944 did not need to be reenacted in 1948.
54.keyHolding: General Conference legislation, unless specifically limited as to time, remains in effect until repealed or amended.
54.parties: Committee on Enabling Acts and Legal Forms

55.title: Constitutionality of Report No. 6 of the Committee on Conferences, Calendar No. 115, General Conference 1948, As to Change of Jurisdictional Boundaries
55.summary: The General Conference constitutionally changed the boundaries between the Central and Northeastern Jurisdictions to allow certain conferences to organize new Negro work within their territories.
55.keyHolding: General Conference may constitutionally change jurisdictional boundaries when the required consent of a majority of Annual Conferences in each affected jurisdiction has been obtained.

56.title: Change of West Texas Annual Conference Boundaries, Constitutionality of Report No. 4 Committee on Conferences, General Conference 1948
56.summary: The General Conference attempted to change conference boundaries by removing Arizona from the West Texas Conference without following constitutional requirements for consent from affected jurisdictions. The Judicial Council ruled this action invalid.
56.keyHolding: General Conference cannot change jurisdictional conference boundaries without the constitutionally required consent of a majority of Annual Conferences in each affected jurisdiction.

57.title: Fixing Boundaries of Episcopal Areas, Constitutionality of Provision Requiring Consent of Jurisdictional Committee on Episcopacy
57.summary: The General Conference cannot require bishops to get approval from a jurisdictional committee before setting the boundaries of episcopal areas. This power belongs exclusively to bishops under the Constitution.
57.keyHolding: The constitutional authority to arrange episcopal supervision, including fixing boundaries of episcopal areas, is exclusively vested in bishops and cannot be subjected to jurisdictional committee consent requirements.
57.outcome: Unconstitutional - amendment requiring jurisdictional committee consent for episcopal area boundaries violates constitutional episcopal powers

58.title: Special Act of General Conference Concerning Ordination of Elders in Germany Central Conference
58.summary: The General Conference passed special legislation allowing the Germany Central Conference to ordain elders directly without first requiring ordination as deacons. The Judicial Council ruled this constitutional based on General Conference's authority over ministerial qualifications.
58.keyHolding: The General Conference has constitutional authority to define qualifications of elders and deacons, including allowing a Central Conference to omit deacon ordination and proceed directly to elder ordination.

59.title: Constitutionality of Affirmations of Faith
59.summary: The General Conference asked whether the 1944 approval of certain Affirmations of Faith violated the constitution. The Judicial Council ruled it has no authority to interpret doctrine, only law.
59.keyHolding: The Judicial Council interprets law from a strictly legal standpoint, not doctrine, and therefore has no jurisdiction over doctrinal matters like Affirmations of Faith.
59.parties: Chester A. Smith (on motion at General Conference)
59.outcome: No Jurisdiction - Judicial Council lacks authority over doctrinal interpretations

60.title: Constitutionality of Clause in Par. 607, Discipline 1944, As to Election of Delegates to Jurisdictional Conferences by Provisional Annual Conferences
60.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that Provisional Annual Conferences cannot elect delegates to Jurisdictional Conferences. This ruling made certain already-elected delegates ineligible to be seated at upcoming Jurisdictional Conferences.
60.keyHolding: Provisional Annual Conferences do not have the constitutional authority to elect delegates to Jurisdictional Conferences.

61.title: The Appeal of the Council of Bishops to the a Declaratory Decision as to the Status of a Central Conference Bishop Who Fails of Re-election
61.summary: When a Central Conference Bishop's term expires and they are not re-elected, they return to membership in their original Annual Conference and lose their episcopal status.
61.keyHolding: A Central Conference Bishop who fails re-election returns to membership in their original Annual Conference upon expiration of their episcopal term.
61.outcome: Bishop D. D. Alejandro returned to Annual Conference membership upon expiration of episcopal term

62.title: The Appeal of the Council of Bishops to the Judicial Council Concerning the Constitutionality of Paragraph 901, Article I of the 1948 Discipline Which Reads, "Provided However That as a Result of the Election Each Jurisdiction Shall Be Represented on the Council"
62.summary: The Council of Bishops challenged whether requiring each jurisdiction to be represented on the Judicial Council was constitutional. The Judicial Council ruled it was constitutional because it only relates to the election process, not making members representatives of their jurisdictions.
62.keyHolding: The requirement that each jurisdiction be represented on the Judicial Council is constitutional as it relates to the manner of election and does not make members representatives of particular jurisdictions, preserving the Council's role as an independent judicial tribunal.
62.outcome: Constitutional - the jurisdictional representation requirement was upheld as relating only to election methodology

63.title: Right of a Local Church to Designate All Funds Received on World Service and Annual Conference Benevolences to World Service Alone
63.summary: A local church cannot designate all of its benevolent giving to World Service agencies while excluding Annual Conference benevolences. Funds must first be divided according to the ratio set by the Annual Conference.
63.keyHolding: Local churches must distribute benevolent contributions between World Service and Conference Benevolences according to the established Conference ratio before making specific designations within each category.
63.parties: Third Avenue Methodist Church of Watervliet, New York and Harry N. Van Antwerp vs. Troy Annual Conference Treasurer
63.outcome: Affirmed - Bishop's ruling upheld that local church cannot designate all benevolent funds exclusively to World Service

64.title: Episcopal Decision By Bishop Clare Purcell Concerning Legality of Action of Upper South Carolina Annual Conference Relating to Transfer of Lander College to the Lander Foundation
64.summary: The Upper South Carolina Annual Conference was permitted to transfer Lander College to the Greenwood community as a gift, with conditions for continued educational use and potential return of ownership.
64.keyHolding: An Annual Conference has the authority to dispose of a college it owns and controls by gift to a non-denominational body, subject to property rights governed by civil law.
64.parties: B. L. Kilgo and E. R. Mason, ministerial members of the Upper South Carolina Annual Conference
64.outcome: Annual Conference action deemed legal with conditions regarding property rights

65.title: In Re: Decision of Hazen G. Werner Made in Lima District Conference
65.summary: The Judicial Council interpreted terminology in the 1948 Discipline regarding basic salary plans for pastors, clarifying that "regular active itinerants" refers only to pastors and not District Superintendents.
65.keyHolding: The term "regular active itinerants" in Paragraph 807 of the 1948 Discipline includes only effective members of the Annual Conference serving as pastors and does not include District Superintendents and members serving under special appointments.
65.parties: Lima District Conference through questions to Bishop Hazen G. Werner

66.title: Election of Conference Lay Leader
66.summary: The Judicial Council ruled it lacked jurisdiction to review a bishop's decision about the validity of electing a Conference Lay Leader because the decision was not made in open conference session as required by church law.
66.keyHolding: The Judicial Council lacks jurisdiction to review a bishop's decision that was not requested or made in open session of an Annual or District Conference.
66.parties: Kentucky Annual Conference lay members regarding Conference Lay Leader election

67.title: Appeal From South Central Jurisdictional Conference-Report of Board of Education
67.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that a jurisdictional conference has constitutional authority to recommend that annual conferences consult their boards of education before establishing conference encampments.
67.keyHolding: Jurisdictional Conferences have constitutional authority under Paragraph 15 to make rules and regulations for the administration of church work within their jurisdiction, including advisory recommendations about educational camping programs.
67.parties: Paul Holmes (Central Kansas) appealing action of South Central Jurisdictional Conference

68.title: Request of Board of Pensions for Declaratory Decision
68.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that when a minister becomes a bishop, they must leave the Ministers Reserve Pension Fund because the Constitution requires uniform pension rules for all bishops.
68.keyHolding: Bishops cannot remain in the Ministers Reserve Pension Fund after election because the Constitution mandates uniform pension provisions for the episcopacy through the Episcopal Fund.
68.outcome: Constitutional requirement for uniform episcopal pensions prevents bishops from remaining in Ministers Reserve Pension Fund

69.title: The Power of an Administrative Committee in a Central Conference
69.summary: The Germany Central Conference's Administrative Committee had authority to reverse the Conference's decision to reduce the Northeast Germany Annual Conference to provisional status after learning that General Conference had extended the deadline for maintaining Annual Conference status.
69.keyHolding: A Central Conference Administrative Committee has authority to conduct business between Central Conference sessions, including reversing previous Central Conference actions, but remains accountable to the Central Conference.
69.parties: Bishop J. W. E. Sommer requesting clarification on behalf of Germany Central Conference
69.outcome: Administrative Committee's action upheld as within its constitutional authority

70.title: Basic Salary Plan
70.summary: The Judicial Council clarified that District Superintendents must be included in the Basic Salary Plan only if their conference uses the World Service and Finance Commission method of support, not other support methods.
70.keyHolding: District Superintendents are included in the Basic Salary Plan only when their Annual Conference provides for their support through the Conference Commission on World Service and Finance under Paragraph 788.
70.parties: Bishop Hazen G. Werner's ruling in Lima District Conference
70.outcome: Modified - affirmed previous decision but clarified that District Superintendents are included in Basic Salary Plan only under specific support arrangements

71.title: Re-enactment of Enabling Act Adopted by General Conference of 1940
71.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that Enabling Acts from 1940 and 1944 that help church agencies continue operating remain in effect until officially repealed or changed. These acts don't need to be re-enacted unless they had specific time limits.
71.keyHolding: General Conference legislation, unless specifically limited as to time, remains in effect until repealed or amended by the General Conference.
71.outcome: Enabling Act remains in full force and effect

72.title: The Interpretation of Paragraph 347 of the 1948 Discipline
72.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that time limits for completing the four-year course of study do not apply to the additional two years of graduate study required for ministers admitted under special provisions.
72.keyHolding: Paragraph 347's time limits apply only to the four-year course of study, not to additional graduate study requirements for special admissions.
72.outcome: Annual Conference has authority to set time limits for graduate study completion separate from the four-year course requirements

73.title: Ruling of Bishop G. Bromley Oxnam in the Newark Annual Conference, May 24-28, 1950, in Bloomfield, New Jersey
73.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed that annual conferences can count years of full-time supply pastor service when calculating retirement benefits for ministers.
73.keyHolding: Annual conferences have authority to instruct their Board of Conference Claimants to include supply pastor years in computing annuity years for retired ministers.
73.parties: Reverend Hedding B. Leech, retired member of Newark Annual Conference
73.outcome: Affirmed - Annual conference has authority to include supply years in annuity calculations

74.title: In Re: Ruling of Bishop G. Bromley Oxnam Relating to the Legality of Lay Members Holding a Separate Business Session at the Annual Conference
74.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that lay members of an Annual Conference cannot hold separate business meetings unless specifically authorized by the General Conference, which only permits such meetings for electing delegates to General and Jurisdictional Conferences.
74.keyHolding: Annual Conferences lack authority to hold separate meetings of lay delegates except when specifically authorized by the General Conference for delegate elections.
74.parties: Hallam M. Richardson, lay member of New York East Annual Conference

75.title: Ruling of Bishop Hazen G. Werner in Ohio Annual Conference with Reference to Election of Trustees for White Cross Hospital
75.summary: The Judicial Council reviewed a bishop's ruling that allowed nominations from the floor for hospital trustees, even when the hospital's constitution specified that trustees should be nominated by the board and elected by the conference.
75.keyHolding: An Annual Conference has ultimate control over Methodist hospital corporations it sponsors and may exercise judgment in trustee elections, but remains bound by existing constitutional procedures until formally changed.
75.parties: Ohio Annual Conference and White Cross Hospital Association
75.outcome: Bishop's ruling reviewed regarding conference authority over hospital trustee elections

76.title: Request of Council of Bishops for Decision with Respect to Constitutionality of Par. 502, Sections 2 and 3
76.summary: The Council of Bishops asked whether Annual Conferences could have separate voting for delegates and whether spring conferences could elect delegates at a different time than required. The Judicial Council ruled that separate voting is allowed but delegates must be elected at the session immediately before General Conference.
76.keyHolding: Annual Conferences have flexibility in how they conduct delegate elections, but delegates to General and Jurisdictional Conferences must be elected at the session immediately preceding General Conference as required by the Constitution.
76.outcome: Section 2 ruled constitutional allowing separate voting procedures; portion of Section 3 ruled unconstitutional for allowing delegate election at wrong time

77.title: Rulings of Bishop William T. Watkins at the 1951 Session of the Kentucky Annual Conference
77.summary: The Judicial Council ruled on questions about financial report approval and Conference Lay Leader nominations at the Kentucky Annual Conference. Financial reports must be audited before approval, but oral nominations for Conference Lay Leader are acceptable without written certification of the nomination process.
77.keyHolding: Annual Conference financial reports must be audited before approval as required by the Discipline, but oral nominations for Conference Lay Leader are permissible without written certification of the nominating process.
77.parties: Marcus C. Redwine, a Lay Member of the Kentucky Annual Conference
77.outcome: Partially Affirmed - Bishop's ruling affirmed regarding nomination procedures but modified regarding financial report approval requirements

78.title: Ruling of Bishop Lloyd C. Wicke in Pittsburgh Annual Conference with Reference to Adoption of Ministers Reserve Pension Plan
78.summary: The Pittsburgh Annual Conference tried to let local Quarterly Conferences vote on whether to join a pension plan, but the Judicial Council ruled that Annual Conferences cannot delegate their decision-making authority to lower bodies unless specifically authorized.
78.keyHolding: Annual Conferences cannot delegate their constitutional powers and responsibilities to Quarterly Conferences unless explicitly authorized by General Conference to do so.
78.parties: Pittsburgh Annual Conference requesting review of Bishop Lloyd C. Wicke's ruling
78.outcome: Affirmed - Bishop's ruling that the delegation of authority was unlawful was upheld

79.title: Ruling of Bishop J. Ralph Magee in Illinois
79.summary: The Illinois Annual Conference tried to require approval from Quarterly Conferences before adopting a pension plan, but the Bishop ruled this was improper delegation of the Annual Conference's authority.
79.keyHolding: Annual Conferences cannot delegate their responsibilities and powers to Quarterly Conferences unless explicitly authorized by the General Conference.
79.parties: Illinois Annual Conference members seeking ruling on delegation authority
79.outcome: Affirmed - Bishop's ruling upheld that delegation to Quarterly Conferences was improper

80.title: Ruling of Bishop Jose L. Valencia in the Philippines Annual Conference Relative to the Conference Status of D. D. Alejandro, Whose Term as Bishop of a Central Conference Has Expired; and of D. D. Alejandro's Appeal Therefrom, and Petition for Rehearing
80.summary: A former Central Conference Bishop challenged his return to membership in an Annual Conference after his episcopal term expired, but the Judicial Council ruled he was bound by the original terms under which he was elected Bishop.
80.keyHolding: Central Conference Bishops are bound by the terms of their election and automatically return to Annual Conference membership when their episcopal term expires or is terminated.
80.outcome: Affirmed - petition for rehearing denied and Bishop's ruling upheld

81.title: Pension Claim of Walter L. French
81.summary: A retired minister challenged pension reductions made under 1944 church law, claiming he should receive the withheld amounts after the law was changed in 1948. The Judicial Council ruled he had no right to recover the previously withheld pension money.
81.keyHolding: Annual Conferences have sole authority to determine annuity claims, and retired ministers have no contractual rights to pension benefits beyond the right to make a claim.
81.parties: Walter L. French v. Board of Conference Claimants of the Wyoming State Conference

82.title: Ruling of Bishop Valencia in the Philippines Annual Conference with Respect to a Full-Time Ministry
82.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed a bishop's ruling that annual conferences don't need fixed rules to define "full-time ministry," but said the bishop was wrong to order conference actions expunged from records rather than rescinded.
82.keyHolding: Annual conferences need not adopt fixed rules to define "full-time ministry" as each case should be considered individually by the Committee on Conference Relations based on specific facts.
82.outcome: Modified - bishop's ruling generally affirmed but procedure for handling conference records corrected

83.title: The Continuation of a Central Conference Bishop in Effective Relation as a Bishop, He Having Reached His Seventieth Birthday Prior to the First Day of the Regular Session of His Central Conference
83.summary: Central Conference bishops may continue serving past age 70, unlike jurisdictional bishops who must retire at 70, because General Conference has not established a uniform retirement age for all bishops.
83.keyHolding: A Central Conference bishop may continue in effective relation after reaching age 70 because current Discipline provisions for mandatory retirement at 70 apply only to jurisdictional bishops, not Central Conference bishops.
83.parties: Commission on the Structure of Methodism Overseas
83.outcome: Central Conference bishops may continue serving past age 70, but General Conference has constitutional authority to establish uniform retirement rules for all bishops

84.title: Election of Bishops by Jurisdictional Conferences for a Specific Area
84.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that bishops elected by jurisdictional conferences have full episcopal authority and can be assigned to serve in mission fields outside their home jurisdiction's territory.
84.keyHolding: Bishops elected by Jurisdictional Conferences are Bishops of The Methodist Church with full episcopal powers, not merely bishops of their electing jurisdiction, and may be assigned to supervise missions outside their jurisdiction's boundaries.
84.outcome: Constitutional - General Conference has authority to authorize jurisdictions to elect bishops for mission supervision beyond territorial boundaries

85.title: General Legislation to Permit Individual Churches of the Central Jurisdiction to Become a Part of Any Other Jurisdiction
85.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that individual churches in the Central Jurisdiction cannot transfer to other jurisdictions through blanket legislation, but must follow constitutional procedures requiring General Conference action and approval by affected Annual and Jurisdictional Conferences.
85.keyHolding: Changes in jurisdictional boundaries, including racial boundaries affecting the Central Jurisdiction, must be handled case-by-case through constitutional procedures and cannot be accomplished through general blanket legislation.
85.parties: General Conference requesting declaratory decision on Committee on Conferences Report No. 1
85.outcome: Constitutional procedures required for jurisdictional transfers; blanket legislation approach rejected

86.title: Constitutionality of Proposed Legislation
86.summary: The Judicial Council ruled on two pieces of proposed legislation: one theological statement about the Church Universal was deemed too unclear to violate constitutional restrictions, while adding "is the creation of God and" to Article XIII was ruled unconstitutional as it improperly altered the Articles of Religion.
86.keyHolding: Adding words to the Articles of Religion constitutes an alteration that violates the First Restrictive Rule and is therefore unconstitutional.
86.parties: General Conference referring proposed legislation for constitutional review
86.outcome: One proposal ruled unconstitutional for violating First Restrictive Rule; Council declined jurisdiction on the other as not clearly unconstitutional

87.title: The Right of a Retired Traveling Preacher to Vote in Annual Conference
87.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that retired traveling preachers retain their full voting rights in Annual Conference, as retirement does not terminate their full connection status.
87.keyHolding: A retired traveling preacher retains his right to vote in the Annual Conference of which he is a member in full connection.
87.outcome: Retired traveling preachers retain voting rights in Annual Conference

88.title: Questions Proposed by Ruben V. Candelaria, Delegate from the Philippines Annual Conference
88.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that retired ministers serving as supply pastors can be elected as delegates to Central Conference if they meet the constitutional requirements for conference delegates.
88.keyHolding: Retired Annual Conference members appointed as supply pastors may be elected to Central Conference if they satisfy the constitutional qualifications for ministerial delegates.
88.parties: Ruben V. Candelaria, Delegate from the Philippines Annual Conference
88.outcome: Constitutional qualifications for retired ministers as Central Conference delegates clarified

89.title: Question Proposed by Ruben V. Candelaria, Delegate From the Philippines Annual Conference
89.summary: The Judicial Council clarified that Committees of Investigation can only determine if charges constitute valid offenses under church law, and must file formal charges if they find reasonable grounds, regardless of whether the accused admits guilt.
89.keyHolding: A Committee of Investigation cannot terminate a case and render a final decision, but must prepare formal charges if the evidence substantiates an accusation of an enumerated offense.
89.parties: Ruben V. Candelaria, Delegate from the Philippines Annual Conference
89.outcome: Clarified that Committees of Investigation must file charges when evidence substantiates accusations and cannot terminate cases independently

90.title: Ruling of Bishop G. Bromley Oxnam, at Newark Annual Conference, June 1, 1952, Interpreting the Effect of Section 4, Paragraph 806, of the Discipline of 1948
90.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed that Annual Conferences must establish minimum salary schedules for pastors and apportion the necessary funds to support them.
90.keyHolding: The provisions requiring Annual Conferences to establish and fund minimum salary schedules for pastors are mandatory, not optional.
90.parties: Reverend William McLean Twiddy, Chairman of the Commission on Ministerial Support of the Newark Annual Conference

91.title: Request of the Iowa-Des Moines Annual Conference for an Interpretation of Paragraph 308 of the 1948 Discipline as Amended by the 1952 General Conference
91.summary: Student pastors can be authorized to perform sacraments if they pass the basic Course of Study for Admission on Trial, and can be excused from advancing in regular conference courses while attending approved colleges or seminaries.
91.keyHolding: Unordained student pastors may administer sacraments after passing the Course of Study for Admission on Trial, with suspension of regular course advancement while pursuing approved academic studies.
91.outcome: Student pastors authorized to perform ministerial functions upon passing Course of Study for Admission on Trial, with examination suspension allowed for regular conference courses while attending approved institutions

92.title: Power of an Annual Conference to Authorize a Hospital Owned by the Conference to Borrow Money
92.summary: The Kentucky Annual Conference was legally permitted to authorize its hospital corporation to borrow up to 25% of the hospital's appraised property value for expansion purposes.
92.keyHolding: An Annual Conference has the authority to authorize a subsidiary corporation to incur limited indebtedness based on a percentage of appraised property value without surrendering its sovereign oversight power.
92.parties: Marcus C. Redwine (appellant) challenging the Kentucky Annual Conference's authorization for Good Samaritan Hospital
92.outcome: Affirmed - Bishop Watkins' ruling upholding the Conference's authority to authorize limited borrowing was sustained

93.title: Ruling of Bishop W. T. Watkins of the Kentucky Conference on Question of Quorum Necessary for Quarterly Conference Business
93.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that quarterly conferences do not need a minimum number of people present (quorum) to conduct business, and that a quarterly conference can reduce the number of church trustees to comply with state law requirements.
93.keyHolding: No quorum is required for a Quarterly Conference to transact business, and Quarterly Conferences have authority to modify trustee numbers to comply with state law.
93.parties: Mead Memorial Church, Russell, Kentucky appealing District Superintendent's ruling
93.outcome: Bishop's ruling affirmed - no quorum required for quarterly conferences and trustee reduction to comply with state law was proper

94.title: Successor to Dr. Charles B. Ketcham as Member of the Judicial Council
94.summary: When a Judicial Council member died, the Council determined that the first-elected ministerial alternate should fill the vacancy, clarifying that 'class' refers to ministerial vs. lay categories, not year of election.
94.keyHolding: Vacancies on the Judicial Council are filled by alternates of the same class (ministerial or lay) in order of their election, where 'class' refers to ministerial versus lay status rather than year of election.
94.parties: President of the Judicial Council and Secretary of the General Conference
94.outcome: Judicial Council affirmed that Dr. L. Dorsey Spaugy was the proper successor as first-elected ministerial alternate

95.title: Ruling of Bishop Paul N. Garber at Virginia Annual Conference, October 11, 1952, as to Paragraph 1618, Section 4, Relating to the Listing of Special Appointments in the Conference Journal
95.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that when listing special appointments and their annuity responsibilities in the Annual Conference Journal, conferences must list current year appointments, not those from the previous year.
95.keyHolding: Annual conferences must list special appointments with annuity claims in their current conference journal, not appointments from the preceding conference year.
95.parties: Virginia Annual Conference appealing Bishop Paul N. Garber's ruling
95.outcome: Bishop's decision reversed - special appointments must be listed for current conference year

96.title: Is the Discipline of The Methodist Church a Book of Law?
96.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed that The Methodist Church Discipline is indeed a book of law, not just spiritual guidance, after a civil court ruled otherwise in a New Hampshire property case.
96.keyHolding: The Discipline of The Methodist Church is a Book of Law and the only official and authoritative Book of Law governing every aspect of church life and property.
96.parties: Council of Bishops (submitted by Bishop G. Bromley Oxnam based on inquiry from Rev. Oscar M. Polhemus)
96.outcome: Constitutional - The Discipline is definitively established as the authoritative Book of Law for The Methodist Church

97.title: The Request of the Pacific Northwest Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision Concerning the Relationship of "Approved Full-time Supply Pastors" (Par. 315-c to Paragraph 320 of the 1952 Discipline)
97.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that all approved full-time supply pastors must either be ordained elders or be actively pursuing ordination through the required course of study, regardless of their age or years of service.
97.keyHolding: All Approved Full-time Supply Pastors must satisfy the requirements of Paragraph 320 of the 1952 Discipline by either being ordained as Elders or actively preparing for ordination.
97.outcome: All approved full-time supply pastors must meet ordination requirements or be preparing for ordination

98.title: Ruling of Bishop Roy H. Short Regarding the Legality of the 'Conference Council' as Adopted by the Tennessee Annual Conference
98.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that the Tennessee Annual Conference could legally create a 'Conference Council' to coordinate and promote the work of various conference boards and agencies, as long as it didn't have authority over existing boards whose duties are defined in the Discipline.
98.keyHolding: An Annual Conference has the right to create its own agencies for promoting church work within its bounds, provided such agencies do not contradict the powers of boards established by General Conference.
98.parties: W. O. Largen, Willard H. Blue, and Cullen T. Carter requesting ruling on Bishop Roy H. Short's decision
98.outcome: Affirmed - Conference Council ruled legal as promotional agency without authority over existing boards

99.title: Removal of Residence of Secretary of the Board of Church Extension of the Methodist Episcopal Church, South, from Louisville to Philadelphia
99.summary: The Board of Missions could not move the Secretary of a Kentucky corporation from Louisville to Philadelphia because the Secretary's residence was fixed by the corporation's constitution, which could only be changed by General Conference action.
99.keyHolding: General legislation giving control over a corporation's work does not automatically grant authority to override constitutional provisions of that corporation that can only be amended through specific constitutional amendment procedures.
99.outcome: Board of Missions lacks authority to relocate Secretary; only General Conference can amend the constitution to permit such change

100.title: Request of Louisiana Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision Interpreting the Provisions of the Discipline Relating to Licensing and Renewal of Licenses of Local Preachers
100.summary: The Judicial Council clarified the authority for licensing local preachers, determining that District Conferences have final authority where they exist, while District Committees on Ministerial Qualifications have sole authority where no District Conference exists.
100.keyHolding: Final authority for licensing and renewing local preacher licenses rests with the District Conference where one exists, otherwise with the District Committee on Ministerial Qualifications.
100.parties: Louisiana Annual Conference, South Central Jurisdiction
100.outcome: Declaratory decision issued clarifying licensing authority based on presence or absence of District Conference

101.title: Request of Western North Carolina Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision on the Meaning of the Word 'Consult' as Found in Paragraph 432(l) of the 1952 Discipline
101.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that district superintendents must actually discuss appointments with pastors before making them, not just inform them simultaneously with the final announcement.
101.keyHolding: Consultation requires an exchange of ideas between the District Superintendent and pastor about the proposed appointment before the final announcement, not merely simultaneous notification.
101.outcome: Declaratory decision issued defining consultation requirement for pastoral appointments

102.title: Action of the Second Quarterly Conference of Inglenook First Methodist Church Held May 13, 1953, in Adding Three New Members to the Board of Trustees and Reorganizing the Board
102.summary: The Judicial Council reviewed disputes over a quarterly conference meeting that added three new trustees to a local church board and authorized legal action against a former treasurer. The Council ruled that while the conference meeting was properly called, the addition of new trustees was invalid because proper procedures were not followed.
102.keyHolding: A Quarterly Conference cannot validly add new members to a Board of Trustees outside of the Fourth Quarterly Conference unless vacancies are properly declared, and nominations must be made by a committee chaired by the pastor as required by Discipline.
102.parties: Four members of the Quarterly Conference of Inglenook First Methodist Church, North Alabama Conference
102.outcome: Partially Affirmed - Quarterly Conference meeting was valid, but trustee elections were null and void

103.title: Appeal from Decision of District Superintendent regarding Removal of William Westbrook, Jr., as Steward and Trustee
103.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed that a Quarterly Conference has the authority to remove a Steward and Trustee who withholds church financial records and fails to fulfill their duties, without prior notice or formal charges.
103.keyHolding: The Quarterly Conference has inherent right and authority to remove a Steward or Trustee who acts contrary to their duties without prior notice or formal charges under the church trial process.
103.parties: William M. Westbrook, Jr. and associates appealing removal from Steward and Trustee positions

104.title: The Restoration of Credentials to a Minister Who Was Permitted to Withdraw From the Conference Under Charges
104.summary: A minister who withdrew from conference under charges five years earlier can have credentials restored without trial if proper requirements are met and the conference determines there has been complete amendment of life.
104.keyHolding: No trial is necessary on old charges for credential restoration under Paragraph 993 when proper requirements are met and sufficient time has passed since charges were lodged.
104.parties: Council of Bishops requesting decision on behalf of Bishop Garber regarding North Carolina Conference minister
104.outcome: Declaratory decision that no trial is required for credential restoration under specified circumstances

105.title: The Request of the Council of Bishops for Declaratory Decision Concerning the Meaning of the Words
105.summary: The Annual Conference has the constitutional right to vote on ministerial conference relations matters even when acting contrary to its Committee on Conference Relations' recommendation. The Conference cannot delegate away its basic voting power to a committee.
105.keyHolding: An Annual Conference retains the constitutional right to vote on all matters relating to ministerial character and conference relations, even when acting contrary to committee recommendations.
105.outcome: Annual Conference retains voting authority over supernumerary extensions regardless of committee recommendation

106.title: Request of Council on World Service and Finance for Declaratory Decision on Pension for Resigned Bishop or His Widow
106.summary: The Judicial Council declined to rule on whether a resigned bishop's widow could receive a pension because there was no law in the Discipline addressing pensions for resigned bishops.
106.keyHolding: The Judicial Council cannot make declaratory decisions where no legislation exists in the Discipline to interpret, as this would constitute legislative action beyond the Council's authority.
106.parties: Executive Committee of the Council on World Service and Finance
106.outcome: No Jurisdiction - declined to accept jurisdiction due to absence of relevant legislation

107.title: Request of Division of National Missions of the General Board of Missions for a Declaratory Decision on the Meaning of the Words "or Sub-divisions" in Paragraph 174 of Discipline of 1952
107.summary: The Judicial Council clarified that when church property deeds contain trust clauses, the exception for "subdivisions" refers only to governmental subdivisions, not private real estate developments.
107.keyHolding: The term "subdivisions" in Paragraph 174 refers exclusively to subdivisions of governmental agencies, not private real estate projects, and does not create an exception to the trust clause requirement for private developers.
107.parties: Division of National Missions of the General Board of Missions
107.outcome: Declaratory decision issued clarifying that trust clause exceptions apply only to governmental subdivisions

108.title: Request of the Council of Bishops Asking If An Annual Conference Incorporated in Accordance with Paragraph 625 of the 1952 Discipline Is Compelled to Incorporate Its Board of Trustees in Accordance with Paragraph 709 of the 1952 Discipline
108.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that when an Annual Conference is already incorporated, it does not need to separately incorporate its Board of Trustees if the existing corporate structure performs the same functions.
108.keyHolding: An incorporated Annual Conference that has trustees performing the functions of an incorporated Board of Trustees substantially complies with Disciplinary requirements without needing separate incorporation of the trustees.
108.outcome: Substantial compliance found; separate incorporation not necessary

109.title: Instruction of Lay and Reserve Members of an Annual Conference by an Official Board or a Quarterly Conference
109.summary: A church's Official Board cannot order its lay members to vote a certain way at Annual Conference. The Judicial Council affirmed that lay delegates must be free to make their own decisions based on conference discussions.
109.keyHolding: Official Boards and Quarterly Conferences lack authority to instruct or order lay members to vote in any specified manner on matters coming before Annual Conference.
109.parties: Central Texas Annual Conference requesting Episcopal Decision regarding Official Board of First Methodist Church, Coleman, Texas
109.outcome: Affirmed Bishop's decision that Official Boards lack authority to instruct lay delegates

110.title: Request of New England Southern Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision as to the Meaning, Application and Effect of Paragraphs 375 and 309 of Discipline of 1952 Referring to Termination of Annual Conference Membership by Voluntary Location
110.summary: When a minister voluntarily takes location (leaves active ministry), they automatically become a local preacher in their home church and don't need annual license renewal. They keep their status until they surrender credentials or lose them through a church trial.
110.keyHolding: A minister who voluntarily locates automatically becomes a local preacher in their home quarterly conference without need for annual license renewal and retains this status until voluntary surrender of credentials or deprivation through due process.
110.outcome: Declaratory decision issued clarifying that located ministers automatically become local preachers without annual license renewal requirements

111.title: Answer of a Candidate for the Traveling Ministry as to His Abstinence From the Use of Tobacco
111.summary: A candidate for ministry must give an unqualified 'yes' answer when asked about abstaining from tobacco use - they cannot object to tobacco being specifically mentioned while agreeing to avoid other harmful indulgences.
111.keyHolding: A satisfactory written answer to the disciplinary question about tobacco abstinence must be an unequivocal affirmative answer without equivocation or reservation.
111.outcome: The suggested qualified answer was ruled unsatisfactory; only an unequivocal affirmative answer is acceptable

112.title: Ruling by Bishop Watkins on Whether An Approved Supply Pastor Can Be Elected By His Charge as a Lay Member of the Annual Conference
112.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that an Approved Supply Pastor cannot be elected as a lay member to Annual Conference because they already serve as the pastoral representative of their charge, and serving in both roles would violate constitutional requirements for lay representation.
112.keyHolding: An Approved Supply Pastor cannot represent his charge in the dual capacity of both Pastor and Lay Member to Annual Conference as this would violate constitutional requirements for lay representation.
112.parties: Wm. M. O'Donnell requesting ruling from Bishop Wm. T. Watkins at Memphis Annual Conference
112.outcome: Affirmed Bishop Watkins' ruling that Approved Supply Pastors cannot be elected as lay members to Annual Conference

113.title: Ruling of Bishop Dana Dawson as to What Constitutes a Pastoral Charge in the Election of Lay Members of An Annual Conference
