113.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that each pastoral charge (including circuit charges with multiple churches) may elect only one lay member to Annual Conference, not one for each church on the charge.
113.keyHolding: A pastoral charge, whether consisting of one church or multiple churches in a circuit, is entitled to elect only one lay member to Annual Conference.
113.parties: Bishop Dana Dawson of Central Kansas Conference

114.title: Requiring the Consent of a Ministerial Member of An Annual Conference Before He Can Be Transferred to Another Annual Conference
114.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that bishops cannot transfer ministers between annual conferences without the minister's consent, upholding the constitutional requirement for ministerial consent in transfers.
114.keyHolding: The General Conference has constitutional authority to require ministerial consent for transfers between annual conferences, and such requirement does not remove any established episcopal powers.
114.outcome: Constitutional - The consent requirement for ministerial transfers between annual conferences was upheld as constitutional

115.title: Ruling of Bishop Clare Purcell Relative to the Real and Legal Date of the Close of the Annual Conference Year
115.summary: The Judicial Council clarified that the legal conference year runs from adjournment of one annual conference to adjournment of the next, while annual conferences can set different fiscal years for business purposes.
115.keyHolding: The legal Conference year runs from the adjournment of an Annual Conference session to the adjournment of the next regular session, regardless of any fiscal year dates adopted by the conference for business purposes.
115.parties: G. M. Davenport requesting ruling from Bishop Clare Purcell at North Alabama Annual Conference
115.outcome: Affirmed bishop's ruling distinguishing between legal conference year and fiscal year

116.title: Appeal of Reverend L. Blake Craft in the Case of North Georgia Annual Conference vs. the Reverend L. Blake Craft
116.summary: A Methodist minister was convicted of unchristian conduct and imprudent behavior for publishing a paper called 'One Methodist Voice' that attacked fellow ministers and church leadership. The Judicial Council affirmed the conviction, ruling that the charges were adequate and the trial procedures were properly followed.
116.keyHolding: Charges against clergy need only be sufficient to inform the accused of the offense, and five days' preparation time for trial is legally adequate under the Discipline.
116.parties: North Georgia Annual Conference vs. Reverend L. Blake Craft
116.outcome: Affirmed - Trial court and Court of Appeals judgments upheld in all respects

117.title: Request of Council of Bishops for a Declaratory Decision on the Question "Whether or Not a Retired Bishop of a Central Conference Is Authorized to Attend Meetings of the Council of Bishops with Expenses Paid"
117.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that retired bishops from Central Conferences can attend Council of Bishops meetings with paid expenses and participate when Central Conference interests are involved, but without voting rights.
117.keyHolding: Retired bishops of Central Conferences retain membership in the Council of Bishops and are entitled to attend meetings with expenses paid, but may only participate when Central Conference interests are involved and cannot vote.
117.outcome: Retired Central Conference bishops authorized to attend Council of Bishops meetings with expenses paid but without vote

118.title: Request of the Ohio Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision on the Question "Can the Church Treasurer Withhold Pension Fund Assessments and Send Them in Directly to the Pension Office or Must the Ministers Send the Money in Themselves?"
118.summary: The Ohio Conference asked whether church treasurers could automatically withhold pension contributions from ministers' salaries and send them directly to the pension office. The Judicial Council ruled that ministers must send their own pension contributions unless they specifically authorize the treasurer to do so.
118.keyHolding: Church treasurers may not withhold pension fund contributions from ministers' salaries without the ministers' agreement and authorization.
118.outcome: Church treasurers cannot withhold pension assessments without ministerial consent

119.title: Whether the Proceeds of the Sale of Grace Methodist Church of Portland, Oregon, Should Be Turned Over to the Conference Claimants' Endowment Fund, or to the Portland District of the Oregon Annual Conference
119.summary: The Oregon Annual Conference had a standing rule directing proceeds from abandoned German-speaking church properties to the Conference Claimants' Endowment Fund, but later voted to send Grace Methodist Church proceeds to the Portland District without suspending the rule.
119.keyHolding: Annual Conference actions that conflict with existing Standing Rules are void unless the Standing Rule is first suspended or rescinded.
119.outcome: Proceeds belong to Conference Claimants' Endowment Fund per Standing Rule

120.title: Validity of the Election of Fred B. Noble, Member of the Judicial Council as a Delegate to the 1956 Jurisdictional Conference of the Southeastern Jurisdiction of The Methodist Church
120.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that Fred B. Noble could be elected as a delegate to the 1956 Jurisdictional Conference even while serving on the Judicial Council, because he would automatically retire from the Council due to age before the conference convened.
120.keyHolding: A member of the Judicial Council may be elected as a delegate to a Jurisdictional Conference if they will no longer be serving on the Council when the conference meets, regardless of when the election occurs.
120.parties: College of Bishops of the Southeastern Jurisdiction
120.outcome: Election declared valid - Noble eligible to serve as delegate upon retirement from Judicial Council

121.title: Request of the Northwest Philippines Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision Concerning Its Right or Power to Ordain a Woman as Local Deacon
121.summary: The Northwest Philippines Annual Conference asked if it could ordain a woman as a Local Deacon, and the Judicial Council ruled that it could since the Central Conference had not acted to restrict this power.
121.keyHolding: When a Central Conference fails to exercise its constitutional authority to regulate women's ordination, Annual Conferences retain their disciplinary power to ordain women as Local Deacons and Local Elders.
121.outcome: Conference has authority to ordain woman as Local Deacon

122.title: The Request of the Virginia Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision Concerning the Required Appointment of a Preacher on Trial in Paragraph 341 of the 1952 Discipline
122.summary: The Virginia Conference asked whether preachers on trial serving in institutional roles (like Children's Home superintendent or Wesley Foundation director) could be admitted into full connection. The Judicial Council ruled that only pastoral appointments to churches qualify under the discipline's requirements.
122.keyHolding: The phrase 'regular itinerant work on Circuits or Stations' in Paragraph 341 must be interpreted to apply only to pastoral appointments to Circuits or Stations, not institutional or connectional work.
122.outcome: Institutional appointments do not qualify for admission into full connection under Paragraph 341

123.title: Ruling of Bishop Frederick B. Newell in the New York East Conference Regarding the Right of a Board of An Annual Conference to Present a Report Referring to Persons or Organizations in a Derogatory Manner Without Their Having Prior Notice
123.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that Annual Conference boards can present reports criticizing public officials or organizations without giving them advance notice. The Conference has broad authority to consider and act on all board reports.
123.keyHolding: Annual Conferences have the constitutional authority to consider, amend, adopt or reject reports from their boards regardless of whether such reports contain derogatory material about non-members without prior notice.
123.parties: Lay Member of the New York East Annual Conference requesting ruling from Bishop Frederick B. Newell

124.title: Ruling of Bishop Jose L. Valencia in the Session of the Philippines Annual Conference on the Election of Lay Delegates to the Philippines Central Conference
124.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that once Dr. Juan Nabong was admitted as a preacher on trial, he could no longer serve as a lay delegate to the Central Conference since clergy cannot hold lay positions.
124.keyHolding: A preacher On Trial in an Annual Conference cannot serve as Lay Delegate in a Central Conference.
124.parties: Dr. Juan Nabong and the Philippines Annual Conference
124.outcome: Reversed - Dr. Nabong was ineligible to serve as lay delegate after admission on trial

125.title: Re Election of Delegates to General Jurisdictional Conferences
125.summary: The Tennessee Conference with 41 ministerial members is entitled to only one ministerial and one lay delegate to both the General and Jurisdictional Conferences, with these same two people serving as delegates to both conferences.
125.keyHolding: An Annual Conference with the minimum number of ministerial members is entitled to one ministerial and one lay delegate who serve as delegates to both the General Conference and Jurisdictional Conference.
125.parties: Tennessee Annual Conference of the Central Jurisdiction challenging Bishop Matthew W. Clair Jr.'s ruling
125.outcome: Bishop's interpretation that Tennessee Conference delegates serve both General and Jurisdictional Conferences was analyzed under constitutional and disciplinary provisions

126.title: Request of the General Conference Commission on the Structure of Methodism Overseas for a Declaratory Decision on the Question, "May a Central Conference Bishop Preside Over the General Conference?"
126.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that bishops elected by Central Conferences overseas have the same authority as bishops from US jurisdictions and can be selected to preside over General Conference sessions.
126.keyHolding: Central Conference Bishops have equal status with Jurisdictional Conference Bishops and may preside over the General Conference if selected according to the Discipline.
126.parties: General Conference Commission on the Structure of Methodism Overseas
126.outcome: Central Conference Bishop may preside over General Conference

127.title: The Election of Missionary Bishops
127.summary: The General Conference can give permission to a Jurisdictional Conference to elect a Missionary Bishop for a specific foreign mission field.
127.keyHolding: The General Conference has the power to authorize a Jurisdictional Conference to elect a Missionary Bishop for a specified mission field.
127.parties: General Conference Commission on the Structure of Methodism Overseas
127.outcome: Constitutional - General Conference has authority to authorize jurisdictional election of missionary bishops

128.title: Whether the Liberia Annual Conference May Be Made a Part of the Central Jurisdiction
128.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that the Liberia Annual Conference cannot be part of the Central Jurisdiction because jurisdictional conferences are limited to the United States.
128.keyHolding: Jurisdictional Conferences can only be composed of conferences and missions within the United States, not international conferences.
128.parties: Commission on the Structure of Methodism Overseas
128.outcome: The Liberia Annual Conference cannot participate in the Central Jurisdiction due to constitutional geographic limitations

129.title: Whether or Not a Minister in a Sister Church Can Be Given the Privileges of the Floor, Including the Right to Vote, by An Annual Conference of The Methodist Church
129.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that while Annual Conferences can give ministers from other Methodist churches privileges like speaking on the floor, they cannot grant voting rights to non-members.
129.keyHolding: Only members of an Annual Conference have the constitutional right to vote, and this right cannot be extended to non-members including ministers from sister churches.
129.parties: Council of Bishops requesting declaratory judgment on behalf of Bishop Raymond L. Archer of the Singapore Area
129.outcome: Annual Conferences may grant floor privileges but cannot grant voting rights to ministers from sister churches

130.title: Request from the Council of Bishops of a Declaratory Decision on a question raised in a letter from Mr. C. E. Hines of Worthington
130.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that a Quarterly Conference can adopt a policy limiting trustees to three-year terms with a one-year break before re-election, but such policy must always be subject to change by majority vote.
130.keyHolding: A Quarterly Conference has the power to adopt trustee term limit policies provided such policies can always be suspended or rejected by majority vote of the Quarterly Conference.
130.parties: Council of Bishops requesting declaratory decision based on letter from Mr. C. E. Hines of Worthington, Indiana
130.outcome: Quarterly Conference has power to adopt trustee term limit policies subject to majority vote modification

131.title: Whether a Minister on Missionary Service Shall Be Counted on the Mission Field or at His Annual Conference for Representation at the General Conference
131.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that missionary ministers serving overseas must be counted for General Conference representation in their home Annual Conference, not where they are serving.
131.keyHolding: Ministers on missionary service shall be counted at the Annual Conference of which they are a member for representation at the General Conference, not at their mission field location.
131.outcome: Missionary ministers counted in home Annual Conference for General Conference representation

132.title: May a Provisional Annual Conference Vote on the Constitutional Amendments Handed Down to the Annual Conferences by the 1956 General Conference?
132.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that Provisional Annual Conferences cannot vote on constitutional amendments, as only Annual Conferences have this reserved right under the Constitution.
132.keyHolding: Provisional Annual Conferences do not have the constitutional right to vote on amendments, which is reserved exclusively to Annual Conferences.
132.outcome: Provisional Annual Conferences may not vote on constitutional amendments

133.title: The Effective Date of Retirement in the Case of Voluntary Retirement of Ministers
133.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that when a minister voluntarily retires, the retirement takes effect on the date the Annual Conference adjourns, not on a different date chosen by the conference.
133.keyHolding: An Annual Conference cannot set an arbitrary effective date for ministerial retirement; retirement becomes effective on the date of conference adjournment when the retirement is approved.
133.outcome: The Minnesota Annual Conference's standing order allowing for flexible retirement dates was ruled not in keeping with church law

134.title: Interpretation of Amendment to Paragraph 1924 of the 1952 Discipline Providing a Ritual for Admission on Trial
134.summary: The Judicial Council clarified that when the Discipline refers to a "formal vote of the Conference" on admitting candidates for ministry on trial, it means only ministerial members can vote, not lay members of Annual Conference.
134.keyHolding: The phrase "formal vote of the Conference" in matters of ministerial admission refers only to the vote of ministerial members who are constitutionally entitled to vote on such matters.
134.outcome: Interpreted that formal conference vote on ministerial matters means ministerial members only

135.title: The Acceptance by a Board of Trustees of an Annual Conference or Other Group or Organization Within an Annual Conference of Title to Real Estate Which Does not Contain the Trust Clause as Contained in Paragraph 174 of the 1952 Discipline
135.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that annual conference boards of trustees can accept property titles without the trust clause that local churches must use. The trust clause requirement in Paragraph 174 only applies to local churches, not conference-level organizations.
135.keyHolding: Annual conference boards of trustees and other annual conference organizations are not bound by the trust clause requirements of Paragraph 174 that apply only to local churches.
135.outcome: Annual conference organizations may legally accept property titles without trust clause

136.title: Privilege of Voting for Approved Supply Elders
136.summary: The North-East Ohio Annual Conference asked if they could grant voting rights to full-time approved supply pastors who are ordained elders. The Judicial Council ruled they cannot, because voting rights effectively grant membership in Annual Conference, which is constitutionally limited to traveling preachers in full connection and elected lay members.
136.keyHolding: Annual Conferences cannot grant voting privileges to approved supply pastors because voting rights effectively constitute membership in the Annual Conference, which is constitutionally restricted to traveling preachers in full connection and elected lay members.
136.outcome: Unconstitutional - Annual Conference cannot extend voting privileges to approved supply pastors

137.title: Standards for Wesley Foundations
137.summary: When a local church is discontinued, the Annual Conference trustees have authority to dispose of all church assets, including funds belonging to the Woman's Society of Christian Service.
137.keyHolding: Annual Conference trustees may dispose of funds belonging to the Woman's Society of Christian Service of a discontinued church as directed by the Annual Conference.
137.outcome: Annual Conference trustees authorized to dispose of Woman's Society funds from discontinued church

138.title: Whether the Trustees of an Annual Conference Can Dispose of Funds Belonging to The Woman's Society of Christian Service of a Discontinued Church
138.summary: When a local church is discontinued, the Annual Conference trustees have authority to dispose of all church assets, including funds belonging to the local Woman's Society of Christian Service.
138.keyHolding: Annual Conference trustees may dispose of all property, including funds of constituent organizations like the Woman's Society of Christian Service, when a local church is discontinued.
138.outcome: Annual Conference trustees authorized to dispose of Woman's Society funds from discontinued church

139.title: Ruling of Bishop Bachman G. Hodge in the Alabama-West Florida Annual Conference Concerning the Application of Paragraph 1103 of the Discipline to the Methodist Children's Home at Selma, Alabama
139.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that conflict of interest rules for board members receiving compensation apply only to general church agencies, not to conference-owned institutions like children's homes.
139.keyHolding: Paragraph 1103's prohibition on compensated board members applies only to general administrative agencies of The Methodist Church, not to conference boards or agencies.
139.parties: Rev. L. B. Green requesting ruling on Methodist Children's Home Board conflicts of interest
139.outcome: Bishop's ruling affirmed that general agency conflict of interest rules do not apply to conference agencies

140.title: Ruling of Bishop Donald Harvey Tippett in the California-Nevada Annual Conference with Reference to the Report of Joint Committee on Distribution of Responsibility for Conference Claimants
140.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed a bishop's ruling that a 1955 joint committee report did not change or alter the original 1940 distributing committee report regarding pension responsibilities for conference claimants.
140.keyHolding: A joint committee cannot change or alter the allocations of conference claimants and distributable assets made by a properly authorized distributing committee under church law.
140.parties: Dr. John R. Kenney requesting ruling from Bishop Donald Harvey Tippett

141.title: May an Annual Conference Adopt a Rule Establishing a Quorum for the Transaction of Business?
141.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that Annual Conferences have the authority to establish quorum requirements for conducting business under their power to make procedural rules.
141.keyHolding: Annual Conferences may adopt rules establishing a quorum for business transactions under their constitutional authority to govern their own procedures.
141.outcome: Constitutional - Annual Conferences may establish quorum rules

142.title: The Power of a Central Conference to Add a New Paragraph to the Discipline in Accordance with the Provisions of Paragraph 578 of the 1952 Discipline (Paragraph 562 of the 1956 Discipline) of The Methodist Church
142.summary: The Latin American Central Conference attempted to modify baptismal practices by allowing child dedication without baptism until the child accepts Christ. The Judicial Council ruled this violated constitutional doctrine requiring infant baptism.
142.keyHolding: Central Conferences cannot make changes to the Discipline that contradict established Articles of Religion or constitutional doctrine, even under their adaptation powers.
142.outcome: Unconstitutional - Central Conference modifications rejected as contrary to Articles of Religion XVII regarding infant baptism

143.title: When an Annual Conference Is Incorporated Should the Sale of Property of an Abandoned Church Be Authorized by Action of the Conference Corporation in Session or by Action of the Annual Conference in Session as an Ecclesiastical Body?
143.summary: When an Annual Conference is incorporated, decisions about selling property of abandoned churches must be made by the Conference acting as an ecclesiastical body, not as a corporate entity.
143.keyHolding: The abandonment of local churches and disposition of their property are ecclesiastical matters that must be determined by the Annual Conference as an ecclesiastical body, not as a corporation.
143.outcome: Declaratory decision that abandoned church property sales must be authorized by the Annual Conference in ecclesiastical session

144.title: Appeal of J. R. Parker
144.summary: A Kentucky minister's appeal of his suspension for unministerial conduct was dismissed because he failed to provide written grounds for appeal at the time he filed his notice of appeal, as required by church law.
144.keyHolding: Appeals must be dismissed when appellants fail to provide written grounds for appeal simultaneously with their notice of appeal as required by the Discipline.
144.parties: J. R. Parker (Kentucky Annual Conference minister)
144.outcome: Appeal dismissed for failure to comply with procedural requirements

145.title: The Constitutionality of Paragraph 1612 (3) of the 1956 Discipline Referring to the Restriction on Loans of Pension-Related Funds to Local Churches and Its Applicability to the West Texas Conference Endowment Association
145.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that General Conference has constitutional authority to prohibit pension funds from being loaned to local churches, and this restriction applies to conference endowment associations.
145.keyHolding: General Conference has constitutional power under Article IV, Paragraph 8 to regulate pension-related funds as connectional matters, including prohibiting loans to local churches.
145.outcome: Constitutional - General Conference restriction on pension fund loans to local churches upheld and binding on West Texas Conference Endowment Association

146.title: The Publication of Names and Addresses of Local Church Lay Leaders in the Journals of Annual Conferences
146.summary: The Illinois Conference questioned whether the General Conference could require publication of local church lay leaders' names in conference journals. The Judicial Council ruled this requirement was constitutional and mandatory.
146.keyHolding: The General Conference has constitutional authority to require Annual Conferences to publish names and addresses of local church lay leaders in their journals, and this requirement is mandatory, not optional.
146.parties: Illinois Conference of The Methodist Church
146.outcome: Constitutional and mandatory - General Conference has authority to require publication of lay leaders' names in conference journals

147.title: The Right of a Central Conference to Amend Paragraph 207 of the Discipline of The Methodist Church Relating to the Qualifications for Membership on the Official Board of the Local Church
147.summary: The Latin American Central Conference tried to modify requirements for church board membership, changing rules about alcohol abstinence. The Judicial Council ruled that Central Conferences cannot change General Conference legislation.
147.keyHolding: Central Conferences cannot enact legislation that contradicts or modifies existing General Conference legislation, as they have only administrative rule-making authority within constitutional limits.
147.parties: Latin American Central Conference of the Methodist Church
147.outcome: Central Conference action ruled unconstitutional - cannot modify General Conference legislation

148.title: The Right of a Conference Commission on World Service and Finance to Use the Service of an Interboard Council as a Budget Review Committee
148.summary: The Pacific Northwest Annual Conference asked if their Interboard Council could help review budgets for conference boards and commissions before the Commission on World Service and Finance makes final recommendations.
148.keyHolding: An Interboard Council may assist the Conference Commission on World Service and Finance in budget review as part of correlating church program planning, but the Commission cannot delegate its core responsibilities and must still hear directly from each agency.
148.outcome: Interboard Council may assist with budget review but Commission on World Service and Finance cannot delegate its core duties

149.title: Can a Ministerial Member of an Annual Conference, Who Has Been Placed in the Retired Relation with the Privilege of Making an Annuity Claim on the Ground of Personal Disability, Serve a Church in a Ministerial Capacity and Receive Compensation for Such Service and at the Time Draw an Annuity from the Board of Pensions of an Annual Conference
149.summary: A minister who retires due to disability and receives pension benefits cannot simultaneously serve a church and receive salary while continuing to draw pension payments. The disability retirement assumes inability to perform ministerial duties.
149.keyHolding: A minister retired for disability with annuity privileges cannot simultaneously serve a church for compensation and draw pension benefits, as the disability that qualifies for annuity payments precludes the ability to perform ministerial service.
149.outcome: Ministers retired for disability cannot serve churches while drawing pension benefits

150.title: Whether or Not Years of Service as a Full-time Approved Supply Pastor Can Be Counted as a Part of the 40 Years of Service as a Basis for Retirement
150.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that years served as a full-time approved supply pastor before being admitted on trial can count toward the 40 years of service needed for retirement eligibility.
150.keyHolding: Years of full-time service as an approved supply pastor prior to admission on trial may be counted toward the forty years of service required for retirement under Paragraph 1617.
150.parties: Virginia Annual Conference (through C. A. Tucker, Secretary)
150.outcome: Full-time approved supply service years count toward retirement eligibility

151.title: Request from the Wisconsin Annual Conference Relating to the Payment of Parsonage Utility Bills as Affected by the Provisions of Section 6 of Paragraph 1624 of the 1956 Discipline
151.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that annual conferences can allow local churches to pay parsonage utility bills for pastors as long as the payments cover actual costs and are properly reported, not hidden salary supplements.
151.keyHolding: Payment of parsonage utilities by Official Boards does not constitute prohibited supplementary compensation under Paragraph 1624 if it represents actual expenses and is properly reported rather than being a cover-up for additional salary.
151.outcome: Constitutional - rule allowing payment of parsonage utilities permitted

152.title: Whether Appointment of a Member on Trial of an Annual Conference to Attend School May Be Considered as Fulfilling the Disciplinary Requirement of "Regular Appointment Under the Supervision of a District Superintendent"
152.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that being appointed to attend school does not count as the required two years of supervised service under a District Superintendent needed for full membership in an Annual Conference.
152.keyHolding: An appointment to attend school under ¶432.7 cannot fulfill the requirement of two years of supervised service under ¶341(a) for admission into full connection in an Annual Conference.
152.parties: Little Rock Annual Conference Board of Ministerial Training
152.outcome: School appointment does not fulfill supervised service requirement

153.title: Ruling of Bishop Matthew W. Clair in the Lexington Conference
153.summary: The Judicial Council declined to take jurisdiction over a bishop's ruling about locating a minister because proper procedures for bringing questions to the Council were not followed by the Annual Conference.
153.keyHolding: The Judicial Council must decline jurisdiction when the proper disciplinary procedures for appeals or episcopal decisions are not followed.
153.parties: Bishop Matthew W. Clair and the Lexington Annual Conference regarding LaFurd Young

154.title: Constitutionality of the Adoption of Amendments VII and VIII
154.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that constitutional amendments VII and VIII concerning delegate elections by Provisional Annual Conferences were validly adopted, despite questions raised about discrepancies between proposed and adopted text.
154.keyHolding: Constitutional amendments are valid when they meet all procedural requirements as recorded in official General Conference journals, regardless of discrepancies in unofficial records.
154.parties: Council of Bishops requesting declaratory decision based on concerns raised by Assistant Book Editor Gordon B. Duncan
154.outcome: Constitutional - amendments VII and VIII were duly and constitutionally adopted

155.title: Central Conference Powers with Respect to Full Clergy Rights for Women
155.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that Central Conferences cannot override General Conference decisions granting full clergy rights to women, and must accept women clergy who have been properly credentialed by Annual Conferences.
155.keyHolding: Central Conferences lack authority to contradict General Conference legislation on clergy qualifications, including full clergy rights for women.
155.parties: General Conference Commission on the Structure of Methodism Overseas
155.outcome: Central Conferences cannot change General Conference legislation on women's clergy rights or refuse to accept properly credentialed women clergy

156.title: Request for the Definition of the Terms "Part-Time" and "Full-Time" as Applied to Approved Supply Pastors
156.summary: Conference boards asked the Judicial Council to define what constitutes "part-time" versus "full-time" approved supply pastors. The Council ruled that defining these terms is a legislative responsibility of General Conference, not a judicial matter.
156.keyHolding: Defining the meaning of "part-time" and "full-time" approved supply pastors is a legislative matter for General Conference, not a judicial interpretation matter for the Judicial Council.
156.parties: Conference Boards of Ministerial Training and General Board of Education
156.outcome: No Jurisdiction - matter is legislative not judicial

157.title: Ruling of Bishop William T. Watkins at Memphis Annual Conference, June 8, 1958, Relating to the Powers and Duties of an Annual Conference Board of Ministerial Training and Qualifications
157.summary: The Judicial Council ruled on whether a conference board can refuse to recommend candidates for ordination who have violated their ministerial vows (specifically tobacco use). The bishop ruled the board has authority over candidates before admission but not after they become members on trial.
157.keyHolding: A Conference Board of Ministerial Training and Qualifications has authority to investigate character and make recommendations for candidates seeking admission, but once a candidate is admitted to membership on trial, the board's authority over their character is limited.
157.parties: Memphis Annual Conference Board of Ministerial Training and Qualifications
157.outcome: Bishop's ruling affirmed regarding limited authority of board over members already admitted on trial

158.title: Ruling of Bishop Jose L. Valencia Anent the Eligibility of Mr. Lingkod A. Juane to serve as a Lay Member of the Philippines Annual Conference
158.summary: A bishop ruled that a lay delegate was eligible to serve at annual conference despite incomplete church records, finding sufficient evidence of four years membership. The Judicial Council affirmed this decision.
158.keyHolding: Incomplete church membership records are insufficient to disqualify a lay member when other evidence reasonably establishes the required four-year membership period prior to election.
158.parties: Lingkod A. Juane appealing District Superintendent's ruling
158.outcome: Bishop's ruling affirmed - lay member eligible to serve

159.title: Lay Representation of Pastoral Charges in Annual Conferences
159.summary: The Westfield Methodist Church, served by three ministers but only one in full connection with the Newark Conference, is entitled to only one lay delegate to Annual Conference, not two.
159.keyHolding: Only ministers in full connection with the Annual Conference in which a pastoral charge is situated count toward determining additional lay representation rights.
159.parties: Newark Annual Conference requesting declaratory decision regarding Westfield Methodist Church
159.outcome: Church entitled to only one lay delegate despite having three ministers

160.title: Ruling of Bishop Nolan B. Harmon That Funds in the Permanent Trust Fund of the South Carolina Annual Conference Are Disposable by That Annual Conference
160.summary: The South Carolina Annual Conference asked whether they could use general trust funds to reduce a mortgage on youth camp property. The Judicial Council affirmed that conferences can dispose of permanent fund monies not tied to specific trusts.
160.keyHolding: Trust funds held by Annual Conference trustees that are not designated for specific purposes belong to the permanent fund and may be disposed of by direction of the Annual Conference.
160.parties: Board of Trustees of the South Carolina Annual Conference
160.outcome: Affirmed - Annual Conference may dispose of undesignated trust funds in permanent fund

161.title: Ruling of Bishop William T. Watkins in Connection with Action Taken by the Board of Trustees of Kentucky Wesleyan College
161.summary: A college board voted to accept their president's resignation, then voted to rescind that action at a later meeting, raising questions about proper procedures. The case became moot when the president retired before a ruling was issued.
161.keyHolding: The Judicial Council will not rule on matters that have become moot due to changed circumstances.
161.parties: Board of Trustees of Kentucky Wesleyan College

162.title: Ruling of Bishop Clement D. Rockey in the Indus River Annual Conference of the Election of U. B. Ernest as Ministerial Delegate to the General Conference and the Central Conference of Southern Asia
162.summary: The Judicial Council reviewed a bishop's ruling that a minister's eligibility for election as a delegate should be counted from when he was admitted on trial, not just from full connection. This allowed Rev. U.B. Ernest to qualify as a delegate despite not having four full years in full connection.
162.keyHolding: A traveling preacher's years of service for delegate eligibility purposes begin from the date of admission on trial, not from admission into full connection.
162.parties: Bishop Clement D. Rockey and the Indus River Annual Conference regarding Rev. U. B. Ernest's delegate eligibility
162.outcome: Bishop's ruling affirmed that admission on trial begins the count for traveling preacher years

163.title: Petition of the Council of Bishops Requesting the Judicial Council to Reconsider and Re-hear the Question Which Was Presented to the Council and Answered by Its Opinion No. 114
163.summary: The Council of Bishops asked the Judicial Council to reconsider a previous decision about whether ministers need consent before being transferred to another Annual Conference. The Judicial Council denied the request for a rehearing.
163.keyHolding: The Judicial Council denied the Council of Bishops' petition to reconsider Decision No. 114 regarding ministerial transfers between Annual Conferences.

164.title: The Right of Central Conference Bishops to Attend All Sessions of the Council of Bishops with Expenses Paid
164.summary: Central Conference bishops have full membership rights in the Council of Bishops and cannot have their travel expenses limited to only one meeting per quadrennium, as this would restrict their constitutional right to vote and participate.
164.keyHolding: Central Conference bishops are entitled to attend all meetings of the Council of Bishops with expenses paid from the General Episcopal Fund as this constitutes official travel for members with full participation rights.
164.parties: Commission on Structure of Methodism Overseas of the Central Conference of Southern Asia
164.outcome: Constitutional right affirmed - Central Conference bishops entitled to attend all Council meetings with expenses paid

165.title: Whether a Ministerial Member or Approved Supply Pastor Automatically Retired at Age Seventy-Two Is Retired for Payment of Annuity Whether or Not the Conference Acts on His Retirement in the Session Following Such Minister's Seventy-Second Birthday
165.summary: The Virginia Conference asked whether ministers are automatically eligible for retirement annuity benefits at age 72 regardless of conference action, and whether pension boards can determine service years for annuity purposes.
165.keyHolding: Ministers who reach age seventy-two are automatically retired and entitled to annuity benefits based on their years of approved service, regardless of whether the Annual Conference takes formal action on their retirement.
165.outcome: Declaratory ruling that automatic retirement at age 72 triggers annuity eligibility and pension boards may determine service years

166.title: The Request of Southern Methodist University for a Declaratory Decision on the Relationship of an Effective Methodist Minister Who Has Been Appointed by a Bishop to the Faculty of Southern Methodist University
166.summary: Southern Methodist University sought clarification on whether it is an integral agency of The Methodist Church and whether ministers appointed by bishops to its faculty are serving under church assignment and in the exercise of their ministry.
166.keyHolding: Southern Methodist University is an integral agency of The Methodist Church, and effective Methodist ministers appointed by bishops to its faculty are performing church assignments and exercising their ministry.
166.outcome: University confirmed as integral church agency; episcopal appointments to faculty confirmed as church assignments and ministerial exercise

167.title: Request of the Southwest Texas Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision on the Relationship of an Effective Methodist Minister Who Has Been Appointed by a Bishop to the Faculty of a Methodist Theological School
167.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that Methodist ministers appointed by bishops to teach at Methodist theological schools are still serving on church assignment and exercising their ministry.
167.keyHolding: An effective Methodist minister appointed by a bishop to a Methodist theological school faculty is performing services on church assignment and exercising ministry in that role.
167.outcome: Affirmed that theological school faculty appointments constitute church assignment and ministry exercise

168.title: Re-Submission of the Rev. Blake Craft's Appeal to Answer Questions Raised in Decision No. 116
168.summary: A minister attempted to reopen a 1955 Judicial Council decision by submitting new arguments in 1960, but the Council declined to reconsider the case as neither meritorious nor timely.
168.keyHolding: The Judicial Council may decline to rehear final decisions when the re-submission is neither meritorious nor made within a reasonable time.
168.outcome: Re-submission declined as unmeritorious and untimely

169.title: Constitutionality of a Transfer of an Annual Conference from One Jurisdiction into Another
169.summary: The General Conference asked whether it was constitutional for a Jurisdictional Conference to invite Annual Conferences outside its geographical boundaries to transfer to its membership. The Judicial Council ruled that such transfers are constitutional under Amendment IX.
169.keyHolding: An Annual Conference may be transferred from one Jurisdiction to another without regard to geographical boundaries under Amendment IX (Article V.2), which supersedes other constitutional provisions about jurisdictional boundaries.
169.outcome: Constitutional - Annual Conference transfers between jurisdictions without regard to geographical boundaries are permitted under Amendment IX

170.title: Ruling of Bishop Jose L. Valencia Upholding the Action of the Northwest Philippines Annual Conference in Unseating Benjamin Casiano
170.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed a bishop's ruling that an Annual Conference has the authority to unseat a lay delegate based on its Credentials Committee recommendation.
170.keyHolding: Annual Conferences have the exclusive authority to seat or unseat delegates representing pastoral charges through their established credentials processes.
170.parties: Benjamin Casiano challenging his unseating as lay delegate
170.outcome: Affirmed - Annual Conference authority to unseat delegate upheld

171.title: Whether a Minister Retired on Disability Can Receive Annuity
171.summary: A disabled retired minister can work full-time in a secular job and still receive pension benefits, as long as they are not serving as a minister.
171.keyHolding: A minister retired due to disability may receive full-time secular employment compensation while simultaneously drawing an annuity from the Conference Board of Pensions.
171.outcome: Ministers retired on disability may receive secular employment income while drawing pension benefits

172.title: Request of the Central Conference of Southern Asia Commission on Structure of Methodism Overseas for a Joint Statement of the General Conference and the Judicial Council Clarifying the Power of Central Conferences to Make Such Changes and Adaptations in the Discipline as the Peculiar Conditions in the Fields Concerned May Require
172.summary: The Central Conference of Southern Asia requested clarification from both the General Conference and Judicial Council about their powers to adapt church law, particularly regarding women's clergy rights. The Judicial Council ruled they cannot issue joint statements with the General Conference.
172.keyHolding: The powers and duties of the General Conference and the Judicial Council are totally different and separate and cannot be jointly exercised.
172.parties: Central Conference of Southern Asia Commission on Structure of Methodism Overseas
172.outcome: No Jurisdiction - request for joint statement denied as beyond Judicial Council's authority

173.title: Ruling of Bishop Jose L. Valencia in the Northwest Philippines Annual Conference That Ezekias G. Gacutan Is a Layman
173.summary: A bishop ruled that a former minister who voluntarily located (stepped back from active ministry) became a layman, making him eligible to serve as a lay delegate.
173.keyHolding: A minister who voluntarily locates automatically becomes a layman and local preacher with membership in a Quarterly Conference.
173.parties: Samuel Rabanillo appealing Bishop Jose L. Valencia's ruling regarding Ezekias G. Gacutan's status
173.outcome: Affirmed - Bishop's ruling that voluntarily located minister becomes a layman upheld

174.title: Election of Voluntarily Located Former Minister as Delegate to General or Central Conference
174.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that ministers under voluntary location can be elected as lay delegates to General or Central Conference, and that reserve lay members can also be elected as delegates if they meet constitutional requirements.
174.keyHolding: A former minister under voluntary location may be elected as a lay delegate to General or Central Conference by an Annual Conference, provided constitutional requirements are met.
174.outcome: Both questions answered affirmatively - voluntarily located ministers and reserve lay members can be elected as delegates if they meet constitutional requirements

175.title: Direct and Final Responsibility for the Supervision of a Local Wesley Foundation or Methodist Student Movement Including Local Church Relationships and Employed Personnel
175.summary: The Judicial Council clarified the chain of authority for Wesley Foundations and Methodist Student Movement programs, establishing that local boards of directors have direct responsibility subject to higher church authorities and appointive system obligations.
175.keyHolding: Direct and final responsibility for supervising Wesley Foundations rests with local boards of directors, subject to prior authority of Annual Conference Boards of Education and the General Board of Education.
175.outcome: Declaratory decision clarifying supervisory authority structure for Wesley Foundations and Methodist Student Movement programs

176.title: Constitutionality of Resolution of General Conference Relating to the So-called Sit-in Demonstrations
176.summary: The General Conference passed a resolution supporting civil rights sit-in demonstrations and commending students for their non-violent conduct. A delegate appealed the constitutionality of this resolution, but the Judicial Council ruled it was constitutional.
176.keyHolding: A General Conference resolution expressing moral support for civil rights demonstrations does not violate the constitutional restriction against altering Articles of Religion or establishing new doctrinal standards.
176.parties: John A. Dickson, Jr., of the Louisiana Conference in the South Central Jurisdiction

177.title: Request of General Conference for Opinion Concerning Procedure Regarding Consecration and Induction of Bishops
177.summary: The General Conference asked the Judicial Council to clarify constitutional provisions about bishop consecration and induction procedures, but the Council ruled it lacked authority to interpret constitutional language or rule on hypothetical future legislation.
177.keyHolding: The Judicial Council has no authority to render declaratory decisions interpreting constitutional language at the request of General Conference or to rule on the constitutionality of hypothetical future legislation.
177.outcome: No Jurisdiction - Judicial Council lacks authority to interpret constitutional provisions on General Conference request

178.title: The Right of a Conference Board of Missions (and Church Extension) to Purchase and Hold Property
178.summary: The Oregon Annual Conference asked whether its Board of Missions and Church Extension could own property, or if only the Conference Board of Trustees could hold property. The Judicial Council ruled that Conference Boards of Missions can own and hold property in their own name.
178.keyHolding: An Annual Conference Board of Missions may own property and take title thereto in its own name if incorporated, and if not incorporated, in the name of trustees elected by it.
178.outcome: Board of Missions may purchase and hold property

179.title: Ruling of Bishop Hazen G. Werner in the North-East Ohio Conference as to the Right of the Annual Conference to Enact a Compulsory Apportionment to the Ministerial Members for the Support of the Minimum Salary Plan
179.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that annual conferences cannot require individual ministers to pay mandatory fees to support the minimum salary fund, as The Discipline specifies that such funding must come through apportionments to districts and charges, not individual ministers.
179.keyHolding: Annual conferences cannot enact compulsory apportionments on ministerial members for minimum salary support because The Discipline mandates a specific procedure requiring apportionments to districts and charges instead.
179.parties: North-East Ohio Conference requesting ruling from Bishop Hazen G. Werner
179.outcome: Reversed - Bishop's ruling was incorrect; Annual Conference cannot enact compulsory apportionment on ministers

180.title: Ruling of Bishop Nolan B. Harmon Relative to the Authority of the Western North Carolina Conference to Grant Annuities on an Adjusted Basis to Conference Members Related to Approved Institutions That Have Pension Plans
180.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed that the Western North Carolina Conference could provide adjusted annuities to members serving Methodist institutions that have their own pension plans, paying the difference between the institution's pension and the conference annuity.
180.keyHolding: Annual conferences have authority under ¶1618.9 to determine Methodist institutions approved for annuity responsibility and may grant adjusted annuities to members serving institutions with existing pension plans.
180.parties: Western North Carolina Conference Board of Pensions
180.outcome: Bishop's decision affirmed - conference has authority to grant adjusted annuities

181.title: The Request of the Texas Conference for a Declaratory Decision Whether a Retired Minister Serving a Charge as a Supply Pastor May Be Lawfully Required to Pay a Portion of His Salary to a Fund for Pensions
181.summary: The Texas Conference asked whether retired ministers serving as supply pastors must contribute 1% of their salary to the pension fund. The Judicial Council ruled they cannot be required to pay into pension funds since they cannot accumulate additional pension credit while retired.
181.keyHolding: A retired minister appointed as supply pastor cannot be required to pay any percentage of his salary into pension funds because they cannot receive annuity credit for service rendered after retirement.
181.outcome: Retired ministers serving as supply pastors cannot be required to contribute to pension funds

182.title: Action of the Northeastern Jurisdictional Conference with Respect to the Election of a Bishop by the Africa Central Conference and Reassignment of Bishop Newell S. Booth
182.summary: The Northeastern Jurisdictional Conference tried to delegate authority to its Committee on Episcopacy to decide when to create a new bishop position for Africa and reassign Bishop Booth, but this delegation was ruled unconstitutional.
182.keyHolding: A Jurisdictional Conference cannot delegate its constitutional authority to elect bishops and make episcopal assignments to a committee.
182.parties: Northeastern Jurisdictional Conference action referred to Judicial Council
182.outcome: Unconstitutional - delegation of episcopal election and assignment authority to committee invalid

183.title: Constitutionality of Legislation Adopted by the 1960 General Conference Providing for the Election by the General Conference of the Required Number of Members From each Jurisdiction to the General Board of Pensions
183.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that General Conference cannot elect members to the General Board of Pensions from jurisdictions because the Constitution gives jurisdictional conferences the right to choose their own representatives on general boards.
183.keyHolding: General Conference legislation providing for election of jurisdictional representatives to the General Board of Pensions violates the constitutional right of jurisdictional conferences to choose their own representatives on general boards.

184.title: Request of the West Virginia Annual Conference for An Opinion As to the Legality Or Legal Effect of the Amendment of One of Its Standing Rules to Permit the Election of Supply Pastors, Who Have Been Ordained Elders and Are Serving Under Episcopal Appointment, to Membership on Conference Boards and Agencies
184.summary: The West Virginia Annual Conference asked the Judicial Council to rule on whether supply pastors who are ordained elders could serve on conference boards and agencies. The Judicial Council declined to rule, stating it lacks jurisdiction to provide advisory opinions on annual conference rules upon direct request.
184.keyHolding: The Judicial Council does not have jurisdiction to render declaratory decisions on the legality of Annual Conference actions upon direct request from that conference.

185.title: Petition from the Northwest Philippines Annual Conference on Eligibility of Candidates for Conference Treasurer
185.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that Annual Conferences can only elect conference treasurers from among candidates nominated by their Commission on World Service and Finance, not from nominations made from the floor of the conference.
185.keyHolding: Annual Conferences are limited in their election of conference treasurer to persons who have been nominated by the Commission on World Service and Finance.
185.outcome: Conference limited to Commission nominees for treasurer election

186.title: Ruling of Bishop Alejandro on Whether St. Paul's Church Is Entitled to Two Lay Members to the Philippines Annual Conference When One of the Ministers Appointed to It Belongs to Another Conference
186.summary: A church served by two ministers, one from a different annual conference, was ruled entitled to only one lay member since only ministers in full connection with that specific conference count for additional lay representation.
186.keyHolding: For a pastoral charge to be entitled to two lay members in an annual conference, it must be served by more than one minister in full connection with that particular annual conference.
186.parties: William M. Pickard, Jr. requesting ruling from Bishop D. D. Alejandro

187.title: Ruling of Bishop D. D. Alejandro in the Philippines Annual Conference As to the Legality of the Readmission on Trial of Miguel Fernandez
187.summary: The Judicial Council reversed a bishop's ruling that allowed a 59-year-old man to be readmitted on trial to ministry despite Central Conference age limits. The bishop had allowed the exception for missional needs, but the Council found this violated established requirements.
187.keyHolding: Central Conference educational standards and other requirements for admission must be followed by Annual Conferences within their territories, and bishops cannot override these established standards.
187.parties: William M. Pickard requesting ruling on Miguel Fernandez's readmission
187.outcome: Reversed - Bishop's ruling allowing readmission despite age requirements was overturned

188.title: Whether Rally Day Funds May Legally Be Absorbed Into the Total Annual Conference Council Budget, Which Includes the Budget Askings of the Various Agencies, Boards and Commissions of the Conference and Also the Administrative Expenses of the Conference Council
188.summary: The Pacific Northwest Conference was combining Rally Day offerings designated for the Board of Education into their general conference budget shared by all agencies. The Judicial Council ruled this practice violated church law requiring funds to be used as designated.
188.keyHolding: Funds solicited for a specific purpose cannot be diverted to another use, and Rally Day offerings designated for the Board of Education cannot be absorbed into a general conference budget shared by all agencies.
188.parties: Oscar M. Adam, Executive Secretary, Program Division of the Pacific Northwest Annual Conference
188.outcome: Rally Day funds must go directly to Board of Education as designated, not be absorbed into general conference budget

189.title: Request of the Virginia Annual Conference For Declaratory Decision As to the Right of Conference Trustees to Lend Money
189.summary: The Virginia Annual Conference asked whether conference trustees could lend money without conference approval, but the Judicial Council refused to answer because the conference had already approved the action in question.
189.keyHolding: The Judicial Council will not render declaratory decisions on moot or academic questions raised after the relevant action has already been taken and effectively ratified.

190.title: The Right of the North Carolina Annual Conference to Direct Its Trustees Concerning the Investment of Trust Funds
190.summary: The North Carolina Annual Conference has the authority to direct how its Board of Trustees invests church funds and can require that these funds not be mixed with other investments.
190.keyHolding: Annual Conferences have broad powers to direct their Board of Trustees concerning the investment of trust funds, including the right to instruct against commingling funds.
190.parties: North Carolina Annual Conference, Southeastern Jurisdiction
190.outcome: Conference authority to direct trustee investment practices affirmed

191.title: Request of the North Carolina Annual Conference (SEJ) for a Declaratory Decision Interpreting the Powers of the Conference Board of Education and the Conference Commission on Higher Education
191.summary: The Judicial Council clarified the respective roles of the Conference Board of Education and Commission on Higher Education regarding Methodist colleges and Wesley Foundations. The Board of Education has primary responsibility for determining financial needs and fund distribution.
191.keyHolding: The Conference Board of Education has the duty to determine financial needs of related colleges and Wesley Foundations and is responsible for allocation and distribution of conference funds to these institutions.
191.outcome: Clarified respective roles and responsibilities of Conference Board of Education and Commission on Higher Education

192.title: Ruling of Bishop Richard C. Raines Concerning the Readmission of R. W. Parsley, a Voluntarily Located Person to the Indiana Annual Conference
192.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that an Annual Conference has the authority to readmit a voluntarily located minister at its discretion, even for retirement purposes, despite disciplinary provisions that seemed to restrict such readmissions.
192.keyHolding: An Annual Conference has discretionary authority to readmit voluntarily located ministers and determine their retirement status and annuity claims, which cannot be abridged by other disciplinary provisions.
192.parties: Indiana Annual Conference appealing Bishop Richard C. Raines' ruling regarding R. W. Parsley's readmission
192.outcome: Bishop's ruling reversed - Annual Conference has authority to readmit voluntarily located ministers for retirement purposes

193.title: Request of the Central Conference of Southern Asia for a Declaratory Decision as to the Powers of Said Conference to Act Under a Possible Future Enabling Act of the General Conference Not Yet Passed or Granted
193.summary: The Central Conference of Southern Asia asked the Judicial Council to interpret powers they might have under a future enabling act for church union that hadn't been requested or passed yet. The Council ruled it cannot give advisory opinions on hypothetical future legislation.
193.keyHolding: The Judicial Council will not render decisions on possible future legislation or hypothetical situations, as it lacks jurisdiction to provide advisory opinions on legislation that may never exist.
193.outcome: No Jurisdiction - Council cannot rule on hypothetical future legislation

194.title: Equity of Central Pennsylvania Annual Conference in Washington Area Episcopal Residence Fund
194.summary: The Central Pennsylvania Annual Conference contributed $27,085.76 toward the Washington Area episcopal residence and requested its equity when transferred to a new area. The Judicial Council ruled that the conference was entitled to payment for its equity under church law.
194.keyHolding: An annual conference that contributes to an episcopal residence and is later transferred to an area not owning one has a right to payment for its equity that cannot be denied.
194.outcome: Conference entitled to equity payment from Washington Area Episcopal Residence Fund

195.title: The Ruling of Bishop Jose L. Valencia Regarding Eligibility of Lay Delegates to a Provisional Annual Conference
195.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that lay delegates to Provisional Annual Conferences must meet the same 4-year membership requirement as regular Annual Conferences, even if their local church was organized less than 4 years ago.
195.keyHolding: A Provisional Annual Conference cannot apply lesser membership standards than those required by the Constitution for Annual Conference lay delegates.
195.parties: Bishop Jose L. Valencia (submitting ruling for review)
195.outcome: Partially affirmed - constitutional membership requirements upheld, but exception for newer churches reversed

196.title: The Eligibility of a Member of the Judicial Council for Administrative Service on the Annual Conference or District Level
196.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that its members can serve in administrative positions at the annual conference or district level, clarifying that the restriction against 'connectional office' service applies only to general and jurisdictional level positions.
196.keyHolding: The prohibition against Judicial Council members serving in 'connectional office' refers only to general and jurisdictional level positions, not to administrative service at the annual conference or district level.
196.outcome: Judicial Council members are eligible for administrative service at annual conference and district levels

197.title: Rulings of Bishop James W. Henley Made During the District Conference of the Tampa District of the Florida Conference Concerning the Status of an Elder on Voluntary Location
197.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed a bishop's rulings about the rights and obligations of clergy who have voluntarily located (left active ministry) but retain their elder status.
197.keyHolding: An Elder on Voluntary Location is governed by specific disciplinary provisions distinct from local preachers and remains amenable to their Annual Conference for conduct and ordination matters.
197.parties: Reverend Ellsworth Hartsfield, an Elder on Voluntary Location from the Louisville Conference

198.title: Request of South Central Jurisdictional Council for a Declaratory Decision as to Whether It or the General Board of Education Has Authority to Fill Vacancies in the General Board of Education Between Sessions of the South Central Jurisdictional Conference
198.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that when there's a vacancy on the General Board of Education between jurisdictional conferences, only the College of Bishops from that jurisdiction can fill the position, not the jurisdictional council or the board itself.
198.keyHolding: The authority of a Jurisdictional Conference to elect members to the General Board of Education cannot be delegated to another body, and vacancies in jurisdictional representation must be filled by the College of Bishops as specified in the Discipline.
198.outcome: Neither the South Central Jurisdictional Council nor the General Board of Education has authority to fill the vacancy; only the College of Bishops may do so

199.title: Compulsory Retirement of a Bishop of a Central Conference
199.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that Bishop Alejandro of the Philippines Central Conference could continue serving after age 70 until the next Central Conference session, even though the conference had adopted a compulsory retirement age of 70.
199.keyHolding: A bishop's term of office expires at the close of the Central Conference at which his successor is elected, not simply upon reaching retirement age.
199.outcome: Bishop continues in office until successor elected at Central Conference session

200.title: Request of the Commission on Entertainment and Program of The 1964 General Conference for an Opinion as to Whether or not the Tenure Rule in Paragraph 1104 is Applicable to this Commission
200.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that tenure limits for church agencies do not apply to the Commission on Entertainment and Program because it is not a Disciplinary agency but rather an administrative committee of General Conference.
200.keyHolding: Paragraph 1104 tenure limitations apply only to administrative agencies of the church responsible for connectional work, not to commissions created by General Conference for its own administrative purposes.
200.parties: Commission on Entertainment and Program of The 1964 General Conference
200.outcome: Commission exempt from tenure limitations as it is not a Disciplinary administrative agency

201.title: Request of the Central Kansas Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision Concerning the Eligibility of Mrs. Margaret Rickard for a Pension Under Paragraph 1620.5
201.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that a divorced wife of a former minister cannot receive a pension under Paragraph 1620.5, which only applies to current wives, not former or divorced wives.
201.keyHolding: Paragraph 1620.5 of the 1960 Discipline applies only to current wives, not divorced or former wives of ministers.
201.outcome: Mrs. Margaret Rickard ruled ineligible for pension as divorced wife does not qualify under current Discipline language

202.title: Request of the New England Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision As to the Legality of Conference Action Concerning Pension Payments of a Federated Church Served by a Conference Member
202.summary: The New England Annual Conference sought approval for rules treating Methodist ministers serving federated churches as part-time service for pension purposes. The Judicial Council confirmed these pension arrangements were legal under Methodist Discipline.
202.keyHolding: Annual conferences may establish pension arrangements for federated churches served by Methodist ministers that treat such service as part-time and require proportional pension contributions based on Methodist constituency.
202.outcome: Conference actions declared legal and in conformity with Discipline

203.title: Ruling of Bishop D. D. Alejandro in The Philippines Annual Conference Regarding Annual Conference Responsibility for Annuity Claim of a Minister
203.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed a bishop's ruling that when an annual conference is divided, each resulting conference must assume pension responsibility for the years of service performed within its territory.
203.keyHolding: Annual conference responsibility for minister annuities follows the territory where service was performed, with legal successor conferences assuming corresponding obligations when conferences are divided.
203.parties: Rev. William M. Pickard (petitioner) regarding Rev. Candido Padilla's annuity claim
203.outcome: Affirmed - Bishop's ruling upheld that Middle Philippines Annual Conference must assume responsibility for pension obligations corresponding to years of service performed within its bounds

204.title: Request of the Southern Illinois Conference for a Declaratory Decision on the Constitutionality of Paragraphs 304.2, 392 and 402, Limiting the Ministerial Functions of Approved Supply Pastors
204.summary: The Southern Illinois Conference questioned whether church rules limiting approved supply pastors' ministerial functions to their assigned charges were constitutional. The Judicial Council ruled these restrictions are constitutional because the General Conference has constitutional authority to define the duties and limitations of all ministers.
204.keyHolding: The General Conference has constitutional authority to define and fix the qualifications and duties of ministers, including placing geographical limitations on where ordained and unordained local preachers may exercise their ministerial functions.
204.outcome: Constitutional - restrictions on approved supply pastors' ministerial functions upheld

205.title: Tenure of Members of the General Committee on Family Life
205.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that the twelve-year term limit for church agency members does not apply to committees, only to divisions, boards, commissions, and councils specifically named in the Discipline.
205.keyHolding: Paragraph 1104's twelve-year tenure limitation applies only to divisions, boards, commissions, and councils, not to committees, based on the specific language used by the General Conference.
205.outcome: Committee members are not subject to twelve-year tenure limitations

206.title: The Effective Years of Service of Ad-Interim Local Preachers
206.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that local preachers appointed between annual conference sessions cannot count that first year as approved service time, and can only count subsequent years after meeting specific requirements including four consecutive years of full-time service.
206.keyHolding: Ad-interim local preachers may not count their initial appointment year as approved service and may only count subsequent years after rendering not less than four consecutive years of full-time approved service as pastor of a charge meeting minimum salary requirements.
206.outcome: Clarification provided that ad-interim local preachers cannot count initial appointment year as approved service time

207.title: Request of the Lexington Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision Involving Paragraph 127 of the 1960 Discipline
207.summary: The Judicial Council clarified that only the Quarterly Conference has authority to remove members from church rolls under Paragraph 127, and the five-year waiting period begins when the pastor and committee start the required cultivation process.
207.keyHolding: The Quarterly Conference has sole authority to determine whether members may be dropped from the membership roll of a local Methodist Church following the procedures in Paragraph 127.
207.outcome: Clarified procedures for membership removal and timing requirements under Paragraph 127

208.title: Ruling of Bishop Nolan B. Harmon in North Alabama Annual Conference Session of 1962
208.summary: The Judicial Council confirmed that Annual Conferences have discretionary authority to determine how to distribute minimum salary fund apportionments among their districts and churches, as long as the method complies with Disciplinary requirements.
208.keyHolding: Annual Conferences have sovereign authority under Paragraph 822 to determine the plan and method for distributing minimum salary fund apportionments to districts and charges.
208.parties: Member of North Alabama Conference questioning ruling by Bishop Nolan B. Harmon
208.outcome: Affirmed - Annual Conference has authority to determine minimum salary fund distribution method

209.title: Tenure of Members of the Methodist Committee for Overseas Relief
209.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that tenure limits for church agency members do not apply to the Methodist Committee for Overseas Relief because it is designated as a 'committee' rather than a division, board, commission, or council.
209.keyHolding: Paragraph 1104's twelve-year tenure limits apply only to divisions, boards, commissions, and councils, not to committees, so the Methodist Committee for Overseas Relief is exempt from these restrictions.
209.outcome: Committee exempted from tenure limitations based on statutory interpretation

210.title: In Re: Petition of the Boundaries Committee of the Northeastern Jurisdiction of The Methodist Church for a Declaratory Decision as to the Status of Bishop Newell Booth with Respect to an Assignment to an Area in the Northeastern Jurisdiction
210.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that Bishop Newell Booth, who was elected by the Northeastern Jurisdiction to serve in Africa, remains available for assignment within that jurisdiction and must be provided for like any other effective bishop.
210.keyHolding: A bishop elected by a jurisdictional conference remains connected to and available for assignment by that jurisdiction regardless of their service location.
210.parties: Boundaries Committee of the Northeastern Jurisdiction
210.outcome: Bishop Booth declared available for assignment by the Northeastern Jurisdictional Conference with full responsibility for his placement

211.title: Constitutionality of Paragraph 680 of the Discipline Implementing Amendment IX of the Constitution of The Methodist Church
211.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that new Discipline paragraph 680, which clarifies procedures for transferring local churches between conferences and conferences between jurisdictions, is constitutional.
211.keyHolding: Legislation that clarifies and implements constitutional provisions without conflicting with them is constitutional.
211.parties: General Conference of The Methodist Church
211.outcome: Constitutional - Paragraph 680 ruled constitutional as proper clarification of Amendment IX procedures

212.title: Request of General Board of Christian Social Concerns for Answers to Certain Questions Without Reference to any Act or Legislation of the General Conference or Paragraph or Paragraphs of The Discipline
212.summary: The General Board of Christian Social Concerns asked the Judicial Council to answer questions about who has authority to exclude people from Methodist churches, but the Council dismissed the request because it didn't cite specific church laws or Discipline paragraphs that needed interpretation.
212.keyHolding: The Judicial Council can only make declaratory decisions about specific acts of General Conference or specific paragraphs of the Discipline, not answer abstract questions without reference to particular church laws.
212.parties: General Board of Christian Social Concerns
212.outcome: No Jurisdiction - petition dismissed for failure to cite specific church laws requiring interpretation

213.title: Request of the Nebraska Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision as to the Legality of a Resolution of its Board of Pensions
213.summary: The Nebraska Annual Conference asked if they could designate 20% of all pastors' salaries as 'travel and expense fund' for statistical reporting purposes. The Judicial Council ruled this practice illegal.
213.keyHolding: An Annual Conference cannot arbitrarily designate a fixed percentage of pastoral support as travel expenses for statistical purposes without regard to actual expenses incurred.
213.outcome: Illegal - Conference cannot designate arbitrary percentage as travel expenses

214.title: Constitutionality of Legislation Adopted by the 1964 General Conference Providing for the Composition of the General Board of Pensions
214.summary: The 1964 General Conference asked the Judicial Council to rule on whether new legislation about how members of the General Board of Pensions are selected is constitutional. The Council ruled that the revised composition, including eight members elected by General Conference upon nomination by the Council of Bishops, is constitutional.
214.keyHolding: The General Conference has constitutional authority to provide boards and determine their composition under its power over connectional enterprises, and the 1964 legislation for the General Board of Pensions composition conforms with constitutional requirements.
214.parties: 1964 General Conference via motion referring question to Judicial Council
214.outcome: Constitutional - the legislation providing for composition of the General Board of Pensions was ruled constitutional

215.title: Request of the Commission on the Structure of Methodism Overseas for a Declaratory Decision Concerning the Necessity for a Constitutional Amendment to Remove the Word CUBA from Paragraph 26, Article I, of the Constitution of The Methodist Church and Regarding the Source of Authority for Granting Autonomy to a Church Requesting the Same
215.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that Cuba Annual Conference can be removed from the Southeastern Jurisdiction by General Conference action with majority consent of annual conferences, but removing 'CUBA' from the constitutional text requires a constitutional amendment. Only General Conference has authority to grant autonomy to churches.
215.keyHolding: A constitutional amendment is required to remove the word 'CUBA' from the Constitution, though the Cuba Annual Conference itself may be removed from the Southeastern Jurisdiction through regular General Conference legislative processes with proper consent.
215.parties: Commission on the Structure of Methodism Overseas
215.outcome: Constitutional amendment required to remove 'CUBA' from constitutional text; General Conference has sole authority to grant autonomy

216.title: Request of the Council of Bishops for a Reconsideration of Decision No. 163 Regarding the Constitutionality of Paragraph 431.7 of The Discipline
216.summary: The Council of Bishops asked the Judicial Council to reconsider whether ministers can be transferred between Annual Conferences without their consent, but the Judicial Council refused to reopen the question.
216.keyHolding: A ministerial member of an Annual Conference may not be transferred to another Annual Conference without his consent, and the Judicial Council will not reconsider this settled principle without constitutional or legislative changes.

217.title: Authority Over Mergers of Annual Conferences
217.summary: The Central Jurisdiction tried to give Annual Conferences authority to merge with each other without going through the Jurisdictional Conference first. The Judicial Council ruled this unconstitutional because only Jurisdictional Conferences have the power to authorize Annual Conference mergers.
217.keyHolding: A Jurisdictional Conference may not delegate to its constituent Annual Conferences its constitutional authority to determine when and under what conditions two Annual Conferences may merge.
217.outcome: Unconstitutional - delegation of authority ruled invalid

218.title: Request of the Southwest Texas Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision As to the Legality of Its Proposed 'Tax-Sheltered Annuity Trust Fund'
218.summary: The Southwest Texas Annual Conference asked if it could legally establish a tax-sheltered annuity fund for its ministers. The Judicial Council ruled that the Discipline does not give Annual Conferences authority to create such pension funds.
218.keyHolding: Annual Conferences lack disciplinary authority to organize and administer tax-sheltered annuity trust funds for their ministerial members.
