463.keyHolding: The Judicial Council lacks jurisdiction to rule on where General Boards hold meetings because such decisions do not affect Annual Conferences or the work therein.

464.title: Whether a Diaconal Minister (Par. 303-311,Discipline) may Serve as a Lay Member of an Annual Conference According to Par. 307
464.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that diaconal ministers can serve as lay members of Annual Conference if they are properly elected to that position.
464.keyHolding: A diaconal minister may become a member of the Annual Conference as a lay person when elected as a lay member of the Annual Conference.
464.outcome: Diaconal ministers may serve as lay members of Annual Conference when properly elected

465.title: Whether the Requirement of Disclosure of Remuneration, Discipline Par. 937, Prevails over Institutional Policies which Prohibit such Disclosures
465.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that UMC ministers in special appointments must disclose their salaries for publication in conference journals, even if their employers have policies against such disclosure.
465.keyHolding: Discipline requirements for salary disclosure by ministers in special appointments are mandatory and override conflicting institutional policies.
465.outcome: Disciplinary requirement prevails over institutional policies prohibiting salary disclosure

466.title: The Membership Status of a Missionary Who is a Ministerial Member of a Provisional Annual Conference Serving Under Assignment by the Board of Global Ministries
466.summary: A missionary minister in Austria challenged his conference's decision to give him honorable location instead of retirement status when his missionary service ended. The Judicial Council ruled that missionaries retain conference membership after their Board of Global Ministries service ends.
466.keyHolding: A missionary who is a ministerial member of a Provisional Annual Conference retains membership in that conference after discontinuing service under the Board of Global Ministries and cannot be involuntarily located instead of retired.
466.parties: Rev. Robert M. Hanson (missionary) vs. Austrian Provisional Annual Conference and Bishop Franz W. Schaefer
466.outcome: The missionary retains conference membership after discontinuing Board of Global Ministries service and cannot be involuntarily located in lieu of retirement

467.title: Nomination by the Annual Conferences of Basic Members of the Program Boards Under Par. 804
467.summary: The Southeastern Jurisdictional Conference asked if Annual Conferences could submit a pool of nominees rather than specific board nominations. The Judicial Council ruled that jurisdictions may suggest such plans as long as they don't restrict Annual Conference nomination rights.
467.keyHolding: Jurisdictional Conferences may suggest nomination procedures including pools of candidates, provided they do not restrict the Annual Conference's constitutional right to nominate persons for general boards.
467.parties: College of Bishops of the Southeastern Jurisdiction
467.outcome: Valid - Jurisdictional Conference proposal upheld as constitutional

468.title: Invalidity of 1972 Amendment of General Rules by General Conference Without Required Vote of the Annual Conferences, and Modification of Decision No. 358
468.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that the 1972 General Conference illegally changed the General Rules without following constitutional requirements, specifically regarding language about alcohol consumption.
468.keyHolding: The General Conference cannot revoke or change the General Rules without the constitutionally required process, and changes made in 1972 were invalid.
468.outcome: The 1972 changes to General Rules were declared invalid and unconstitutional; Decision 358 was modified

469.title: Unconstitutionality of an Annual Conference Action That Requires All Local, District and Conference Officers and Central and General Conference Delegates From an Annual Conference to Make a Covenant to Tithe in Order to Qualify for These Positions
469.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that the Middle Philippines Annual Conference could not require church officers and conference delegates to take a tithing covenant as a condition for holding office. Only the General Conference has authority to set qualifications for such positions.
469.keyHolding: Annual Conferences may not add to or subtract from the qualifications for church officers established by General Conference.
469.outcome: Unconstitutional - Annual Conference cannot require tithing covenant for officers and delegates

470.title: The Right of the Puerto Rico Annual Conference to Become an Affiliated Autonomous Church, According to an Action of the 1972 General Conference; or to Become a Central Conference under Par. 650 of the 1976 Discipline
470.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that Puerto Rico Annual Conference can become an autonomous church based on 1972 General Conference authorization, and that General Conference has authority to decide if Puerto Rico can become a Central Conference.
470.keyHolding: The 1972 General Conference authorization for Puerto Rico Annual Conference to become an Affiliated Autonomous Church remains valid and in effect unless rescinded.
470.outcome: Puerto Rico may become autonomous church per 1972 authorization; General Conference has authority over Central Conference status

471.title: The Meaning and Application of Pars. 734.4 and 1701.1, Including a Reduction of Pension of the Pastor Serving a Church Which Fails to Pay its Apportionment for the Minister's Share of the Health Insurance Plan of the Annual Conference
471.summary: The North Alabama Annual Conference can place liens against pastors' pension credits when their churches fail to pay required apportionments for health insurance and ministerial support, as this is authorized under church law regarding proportional payment.
471.keyHolding: Annual Conferences have disciplinary authority to reduce pastors' pensions when churches fail to make proportional payments for pension and benefit programs, including health insurance plans.
471.outcome: Annual Conference action declared valid and constitutional

472.title: Election of Jurisdictional Conference Committees on Episcopacy and the Constitutionality of Pars. 632.1 and 620.1 of the 1976 Discipline
472.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that provisions allowing Annual Conferences to elect Jurisdictional Committees on Episcopacy were unconstitutional because the Constitution requires these committees to be elected by Jurisdictional Conferences themselves.
472.keyHolding: Jurisdictional Committees on Episcopacy must be elected by Jurisdictional Conferences, not by Annual Conferences or delegations, and serve as standing committees until successors are elected.
472.outcome: Paragraphs 632.1 and 620.1 declared partially unconstitutional regarding election procedures

473.title: Eligibility of Ministerial Members of the Annual Conference on Leave to Participate in the Election of Delegates, or Be Elected, to General or Jurisdictional Conferences
473.summary: Ministers in full connection who are on various types of approved leave can still vote for and be elected as delegates to General and Jurisdictional Conferences.
473.keyHolding: Ministerial members in full connection retain voting and election eligibility rights for General and Jurisdictional Conference delegates even while on sabbatical leave, disability leave, or leave of absence.
473.outcome: Declaratory decision affirming voting and election eligibility rights for ministers on leave

474.title: Request for a Declaratory Decision Relative to a Number of Questions Relating to Actions Taken at a Local Church Charge Conference
474.summary: The North Carolina Annual Conference requested a declaratory decision about District Superintendent actions at charge conferences, but the Judicial Council ruled it lacked jurisdiction because the request did not properly seek interpretation of the Discipline itself.
474.keyHolding: The Judicial Council's authority to issue declaratory decisions is limited to rulings on the constitutionality, meaning, application and effect of the Discipline or General Conference legislation, not challenges to specific actions taken at local church conferences.
474.parties: North Carolina Annual Conference (at request of local church member)

475.title: Accountability of Bishops and the Constitutionality of Par. 525.3 of the Discipline
475.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that a Discipline paragraph making bishops accountable to the Council of Bishops was unconstitutional because it conflicts with the Constitution, which makes bishops accountable to their electing Jurisdictional Conferences.
475.keyHolding: Bishops elected by Jurisdictional Conferences are accountable to those Jurisdictional Conferences, not to the Council of Bishops.
475.outcome: Par. 525.3 declared unconstitutional and of no effect

476.title: Constitutionality of an Annual Conference voting to include parts of the Discipline in its own Standing Rules
476.summary: Annual conferences can quote parts of the Discipline in their own rules for clarity and compliance, but they cannot vote to approve or disapprove General Conference decisions.
476.keyHolding: Annual Conferences may include quotations from the Discipline in their Standing Rules for information and clarification, but cannot vote to approve, disapprove, or modify General Conference actions.
476.outcome: Constitutional - Annual conferences may include Discipline quotations in Standing Rules but cannot vote on General Conference actions

477.title: Constitutionality of Making Local Pastors, under Full Time Appointment to a Pastoral Charge, Ministerial Members of the Annual Conference with Limited Voting Rights
477.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that General Conference can grant limited voting rights to full-time local pastors by making them ministerial members of Annual Conference.
477.keyHolding: General Conference has constitutional authority under Paragraph 36 to define ministerial members of Annual Conference, including granting limited voting rights to full-time local pastors.
477.parties: General Conference Legislative Committee on Conferences
477.outcome: Constitutional - General Conference has authority to grant limited voting rights to full-time local pastors as ministerial members

478.title: Constitutional Authority of the General Conference to Amend Ministerial Education Fund Legislation
478.summary: The General Conference asked whether it could amend rules about ministerial education loans to prevent Annual Conferences from requiring loan recipients to serve in that specific conference for loan forgiveness.
478.keyHolding: The General Conference has the constitutional power to revise its previous actions provided such revision does not conflict with the Constitution.
478.outcome: Constitutional - General Conference has power to make proposed revision

479.title: Equalization of Lay and Ministerial Membership of the Annual Conference
479.summary: The Constitution requires annual conferences to add lay members if there are more clergy than lay members, but does not require adding clergy if there are more lay members than clergy.
479.keyHolding: Annual conferences have no constitutional authority to equalize membership by adding ministerial members when lay membership exceeds ministerial membership.
479.outcome: Constitutional interpretation clarified - no equalization authority when ministerial membership is lower

480.title: Legal Status or Effect of Footnotes in the Discipline
480.summary: The General Conference asked whether footnotes in the Book of Discipline have legal authority. The Judicial Council ruled that footnotes only have legal effect when they directly cite law, not when they provide explanations or references.
480.keyHolding: Footnotes in the Discipline have the status or effect of law only to the extent that they cite law.
480.outcome: Footnotes have legal effect only when citing law, not when explanatory

481.title: Constitutionality of the Ministerial Pension Plan, the Comprehensive Protection Plan and Related Legislation
481.summary: The General Conference can constitutionally create pension plans for ministers, but the proposed legislation improperly delegates legislative authority to the General Board of Pensions.
481.keyHolding: The General Conference has constitutional authority to adopt pension plans but may not delegate its legislative power to General Boards to create, revise, or terminate such plans.
481.parties: General Conference requesting declaratory decision on General Board of Pensions legislation
481.outcome: Plans constitutional in principle but current wording involves unconstitutional delegation of legislative authority

482.title: Legality of Proposed Mandatory Prior Consultation of Advance Committee with Annual Conference Board or Agency Responsible for Missions
482.summary: The General Conference asked whether it could require the Advance Committee to consult with annual conference mission boards before approving mission projects in their territories. The Judicial Council ruled this requirement would be legal.
482.keyHolding: The General Conference has authority to require the Advance Committee to consult with Annual Conference mission boards before approving projects within conference boundaries.
482.outcome: Constitutional - General Conference has authority to require consultation

483.title: Method of Amendment of Constitution
483.summary: The General Conference asked if it could delete outdated constitutional provisions without Annual Conference votes. The Judicial Council ruled that only provisions with automatic deletion clauses can be removed without the full amendment process.
483.keyHolding: Constitutional provisions cannot be deleted by General Conference alone unless the Constitution itself specifically provides for automatic deletion.
483.outcome: Constitutional amendment procedures must be followed except where Constitution provides for automatic deletion

484.title: Question Regarding General Conference Parliamentary Procedure
484.summary: The General Conference asked the Judicial Council to determine if their rules were violated during a vote. The Judicial Council ruled they have no jurisdiction over parliamentary procedure questions that delegates could have raised with the chairperson.
484.keyHolding: The Judicial Council does not have jurisdiction to decide matters of parliamentary procedure that could have been addressed through points of order during the session.

485.title: Administrative Location-Validity of Discipline Par. 449.2
485.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that the new administrative location process in the 1980 Discipline is constitutional because ministers retain the right to choose a trial under other provisions.
485.keyHolding: Administrative location procedures are constitutionally valid when read together with other Discipline provisions that preserve a minister's right to trial and appeal.
485.outcome: Constitutional - administrative location provisions upheld as valid when read with related paragraphs

486.title: Request of the General Conference for a Declaratory Decision as to the Constitutionality of Discipline Par. 2623.3(c), Dealing with Suspension by a Bishop of a Local Pastor or Ministerial Member of an Annual Conference Pending Investigation
486.summary: The General Conference asked if bishops can suspend clergy from ministerial duties pending investigation. The Judicial Council ruled this is unconstitutional for ordained ministers but allowed for local pastors.
486.keyHolding: A bishop cannot suspend ministerial members of an Annual Conference from all ministerial responsibilities because authority over conference relations rests with the ministerial members of the Annual Conference, not the bishop.
486.outcome: Unconstitutional for ministerial members of Annual Conference; constitutional for local pastors

487.title: Request of the General Conference for a Declaratory Decision on the Application of General Conference Rule 35 to the Committee on Administrative Order's Report Calendar Item No. 535
487.summary: The General Conference asked the Judicial Council to rule on whether proper parliamentary procedure was followed during a vote. The Judicial Council declined to rule, saying this was a parliamentary matter that delegates should have addressed during the session itself.
487.keyHolding: The Judicial Council does not have jurisdiction over questions of parliamentary procedure that could have been raised by delegates during General Conference proceedings.

488.title: Application for Rehearing of Decision No. 474
488.summary: The Judicial Council denied an application requesting a rehearing of Decision No. 474.
488.keyHolding: The Judicial Council has discretionary authority to deny applications for rehearing of its previous decisions.

489.title: Constitutionality of Equitable Salary Plan Provision Dealing With a Refusal by a Full Time Pastor of a Ministerial Appointment Above the Equitable Salary Level
489.summary: The Louisiana Annual Conference asked the Judicial Council to rule on whether they could remove pastors from equitable salary support if they refuse appointments with higher pay. The Judicial Council declined to hear the case because it lacked jurisdiction.
489.keyHolding: The Judicial Council lacks jurisdiction to make declaratory decisions on local conference policies that do not involve General Conference legislation or bishops' decisions of law.

490.title: Request of General Conference for a Ruling on the Constitutionality of a Study Document on Human Sexuality
490.summary: The General Conference asked the Judicial Council to rule on whether a study document on human sexuality contradicted the Social Principles, but the Judicial Council found it lacked jurisdiction to make this determination.
490.keyHolding: The Judicial Council lacks jurisdiction to determine the constitutionality of study documents that are not legislation or proposed legislation when compared against Social Principles.

491.title: Right of an Annual Conference to Create a Task Force to Study Homophobia
491.summary: An Annual Conference has the right to establish a task force to study homophobia using its own funds, as this does not violate the prohibition on using general church funds to promote acceptance of homosexuality.
491.keyHolding: Paragraph 906.13 restricts only the use of general church funds, not annual conference funds, for gay-related activities or groups.
491.parties: Roy Dunn challenged Bishop R. Marvin Stuart's ruling in California-Nevada Annual Conference
491.outcome: Bishop's ruling affirmed - Annual Conference may create homophobia study task force

492.title: Right of a Ministerial Member in Good Standing of an Annual Conference to an Appointment and Financial Responsibility for Failure to Appoint
492.summary: A pastor left without appointment for 38 days must receive minimum salary payments from the conference. All ministers in good standing have the right to appointment and compensation during gaps.
492.keyHolding: All ministerial members in good standing must receive appointments and are entitled to minimum salary compensation prorated for any period left without appointment, with the Conference Council on Finance and Administration responsible for payment.
492.parties: Wisconsin Annual Conference appealing Bishop's decisions regarding Rev. Jerry Eckert
492.outcome: Conference must pay minimum salary to pastor left without appointment; reaffirmed right to appointment for ministers in good standing

493.title: Constitutionality of Par. 810.5 (1980 Discipline) Which Makes any Voting Member of a General Agency a Voting Member of the Corresponding Annual Conference Agency, in Light of its Apparent Conflict with Par. 706 of the 1976 Discipline. (708.2, 1980 Discipline)
493.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that a person cannot simultaneously hold voting membership on both a general church agency and the Annual Conference Council on Finance and Administration due to conflict of interest provisions.
493.keyHolding: Paragraph 810.5 creating automatic voting membership for general agency members on corresponding conference agencies is legal except when it would create prohibited dual membership with the Annual Conference Council on Finance and Administration.
493.outcome: Constitutional with limitations - dual voting membership prohibited when conflict exists with CFA membership

494.title: Obligation of Annual Conference that has Amended its Budget to Resubmit its Apportionments to the Local Churches
494.summary: Bishop Golden ruled that if an annual conference changes its budget after apportioning funds to local churches, and the change redirects money from its original purpose, the conference must provide revised apportionments to the local churches.
494.keyHolding: An annual conference must resubmit revised apportionments to local churches when it amends its budget in a way that redirects funds from their originally apportioned purpose.

495.title: Unconstitutionality of Restrictions Placed by an Annual Conference on Eligibility for Election of Lay Members of Annual Conference
495.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that Annual Conferences cannot add extra requirements for lay members to serve beyond what is in the Constitution. A proposed term limit rule was declared unconstitutional.
495.keyHolding: Annual Conferences may not impose additional requirements for lay membership beyond those prescribed in Paragraph 36 of the Constitution.
495.outcome: Unconstitutional - Annual Conference cannot impose term limits on lay members

496.title: The Program Agency Status of the Standing General Commission on Christian Unity and Interreligious Concerns and its Amenability, Accountability and Relationship
496.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that the Standing General Commission on Christian Unity and Interreligious Concerns is a program-related agency accountable to the General Council on Ministries, not an administrative agency.
496.keyHolding: The Standing General Commission on Christian Unity and Interreligious Concerns is properly classified as a program-related General Agency under ¶803.5, making it accountable to the General Council on Ministries.
496.parties: General Council on Ministries requesting declaratory decision
496.outcome: Commission classified as program-related agency accountable to GCOM with general secretary election subject to GCOM confirmation

497.title: Appeal of Joseph C. Evers
497.summary: A minister's conviction for imprudent and unchristian conduct was overturned because the presiding bishop met with the Trial Court during deliberations without the defendant or his counsel present, violating church law.
497.keyHolding: A presiding officer cannot meet with a Trial Court during deliberations without the presence of the accused and counsel, as required by church law protecting due process rights.
497.parties: Joseph C. Evers, ministerial member of Southern Illinois Annual Conference
497.outcome: Reversed - Trial Court and Court of Appeals decisions set aside, new trial ordered

498.title: Constitutionality of Temporary Suspension of an Elder from Ministerial Responsibilities, Pending Trial, Upon Recommendation of Committee on Investigation
498.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that bishops can temporarily suspend clergy from ministry before trial, but only if at least five of the seven elders on the Committee on Investigation recommend it. This differs from an earlier unconstitutional provision that would have allowed bishops to suspend clergy with district superintendent approval alone.
498.keyHolding: Bishops may temporarily suspend elders from ministerial responsibilities pending trial only upon recommendation of at least five of seven Committee on Investigation members, with proper safeguards requiring Annual Conference review.

499.title: Re-hearing of Decision No. 496 Pertaining to the Election of its General Secretary by the Standing General Commission on Christian Unity and Interreligious Concerns (COCUIC)
499.summary: The General Council on Ministries requested a re-hearing of a previous decision about how COCUIC elects its general secretary. The Judicial Council denied the request because no new evidence was presented.
499.keyHolding: A request for re-hearing will be denied when no new evidence is presented that would warrant changing the previous decision.
499.outcome: Request for re-hearing denied; Decision No. 496 reaffirmed

500.title: Limitations of the Pastor's Ex-officio Status as Defined in Discipline Par. 253
500.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that pastors are not automatic voting members of their church's Board of Trustees or Pastor-Parish Relations Committee, despite being ex-officio members of most other church committees.
500.keyHolding: A pastor's ex-officio status under ¶253 does not extend to the Board of Trustees or Pastor-Parish Relations Committee where the Discipline specifically restricts or excludes pastoral membership.
500.outcome: Pastor is not ex-officio member of Board of Trustees or Pastor-Parish Relations Committee

501.title: Interpretation and Meaning of the Disciplinary Requirements of "the Consultation Process" in Pars. 528-31
501.summary: Bishops must consult with Pastor-Parish Relations Committees and pastors before making appointments, but the committees are only advisory and bishops retain final authority to make appointments.
501.keyHolding: Consultation in the appointment process is mandatory and must occur before decisions are made, but bishops retain final authority over appointments while committees serve only in an advisory capacity.
501.outcome: Clarified that consultation is mandatory but advisory, with bishops retaining final appointment authority and no specific timeframe required for consultation process

502.title: Eligibility to Participate in the Ministerial Pension Plan
502.summary: The South Indiana Annual Conference asked the Judicial Council to rule that part-time local pastors are ineligible for the Ministerial Pension Plan due to a misplaced word 'eligible' in the legislation. The Council determined that regardless of word placement, all qualifying bishops, ministers, and local pastors may participate in the Plan.
502.keyHolding: The placement of the word 'eligible' in the pension legislation does not materially change the essential meaning that all qualifying clergy, including part-time local pastors, may participate in the Ministerial Pension Plan.
502.outcome: Request denied - all qualifying local pastors remain eligible for pension participation

503.title: Alternate Methods of Collecting Pension Funds Under the Ministerial Pension Plan
503.summary: The South Indiana Annual Conference challenged the General Board of Pensions' interpretation of pension collection rules, but the Judicial Council ruled that conferences choosing to collect pension funds must follow all plan requirements and pay the full amounts specified by the formula, regardless of what they actually collect.
503.keyHolding: Annual conferences that elect to collect pension funds under the Ministerial Pension Plan must abide by all plan provisions and are responsible for the full amount due under the prescribed formula, even if they fail to collect that amount from local churches.
503.outcome: The conference's interpretation was rejected; they must pay full amounts under the pension plan formula regardless of collection success

504.title: Request for Reconsideration of Decision No. 497 as it Relates to the Scope of the New Trial Ordered Therein
504.summary: The Judicial Council denied a request to limit a new trial to only the penalty phase, ruling that a full retrial must be conducted unless there is a guilty plea.
504.keyHolding: A new trial ordered by the Judicial Council must be a full retrial unless limited by a guilty plea under the Discipline's provisions.
504.parties: Counsel for the Church and defense attorney
504.outcome: Request for limited retrial denied; full new trial ordered with new Trial Court

505.title: Right of Lay Members to Vote on Rules Mandating Continuing Education of Ministers in Light of Pars. 701.1 (a) and 701.4 of the 1980 Discipline
505.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that lay members of Annual Conference may vote on continuing education requirements for ministers, as long as these requirements are not tied to ordination, character, or conference membership decisions.
505.keyHolding: Lay members may vote on matters affecting ministers provided those matters do not fall within the specific items prohibited by the Constitution (ordination, character, and conference relations of ministers).
505.outcome: Lay members may vote on continuing education requirements for ministers that are not tied to conference membership continuation

506.title: Requirement for All Clergy to Contribute Personally 3% of Their Support to the Pension Plan Adopted by the 1980 General Conference
506.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that clergy participating in the pension plan must personally contribute 3% of their support, as required by the plan documents adopted by General Conference.
506.keyHolding: Active Participants in the Ministerial Pension Plan are required to make personal contributions equal to 3% of their contribution base annually, as mandated by the plan documents adopted by General Conference.
506.outcome: The 3% personal contribution requirement is mandatory for all Active Participants in the Ministerial Pension Plan, with benefits paid only in proportion to contributions made

507.title: Responsibility and Authority for Determining Qualified Candidates for Certification for Diaconal Ministry
507.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that while the Division of Diaconal Ministry sets standards for certification, it cannot refuse to certify a candidate who has been approved by the Annual Conference Board and certified by the Annual Conference.
507.keyHolding: The Division of Diaconal Ministry cannot refuse to issue certification to a candidate who is recommended by the Conference Board of Diaconal Ministry and certified by the Annual Conference.
507.outcome: Division cannot refuse certification to candidates approved by Annual Conference

508.title: Prerequisite of Request by a Minister for Granting a Leave of Absence Under Par. 444 of The Discipline
508.summary: This case addresses whether an Annual Conference can force a minister to take a leave of absence without the minister's consent. The case was postponed for oral hearings and remained pending on the Judicial Council docket.
508.keyHolding: The case was postponed for oral hearings to determine whether Annual Conference may grant involuntary leave of absence to ministers under revised paragraph 444 procedures.
508.parties: A party of direct interest requesting oral hearings
508.outcome: Case retained on docket with oral hearings scheduled for April 21, 1983

509.title: Amenability of Pastor-Parish Relations Committee to Administrative Board in Recommendations Concerning Pastoral Changes
509.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed a bishop's ruling that Pastor-Parish Relations Committees are not required to be accountable to Administrative Boards regarding pastoral change recommendations.
509.keyHolding: Pastor-Parish Relations Committees operate independently from Administrative Boards when making recommendations about pastoral changes to the Cabinet.

510.title: Housing Allowances for Members of a Clergy Couple
510.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that clergy persons cannot be denied housing allowances simply because their spouse has access to a parsonage, as this would constitute discrimination based on marital status.
510.keyHolding: A member of a clergy couple may not be deprived of a housing allowance even though the other member of the clergy couple has access to a parsonage, as this constitutes discrimination on the basis of marital status.
510.parties: West Virginia Annual Conference Board of Higher Education and Campus Ministry

511.title: Equalization of Lay and Clergy Members in Missionary Conferences
511.summary: The Alaska Missionary Conference cannot elect lay members in excess of clergy members beyond what is needed for equalization. The constitutional provision only allows additional lay members when lay membership is less than clergy membership.
511.keyHolding: Missionary Conferences may only elect additional lay members to equalize lay and clergy membership when lay members are fewer than clergy members, not to exceed that number.
511.parties: Alaska Missionary Conference appealing Bishop Calvin D. McConnell's ruling
511.outcome: Bishop's ruling not sustained; Conference action declared unconstitutional

512.title: Application and Effect of Rule Limiting Tenure of Superintendents in Missionary Conferences
512.summary: The Red Bird Missionary Conference asked whether previous years of service count toward new tenure limits for superintendents. The Judicial Council ruled that all prior service counts toward the maximum.
512.keyHolding: When General Conference imposes tenure limitations without specific exceptions, all years of prior service must be counted against the maximum allowable tenure.
512.outcome: All years of service as superintendent count against tenure limits with no exceptions for prior service

513.title: Legality of Ordination of Probationer of Same Sex Preference
513.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that sexual orientation is not a disqualification for ordination under the existing church law, as the Discipline's requirements for ordination do not reference sexual preference.
513.keyHolding: Sexual orientation is not a disqualification for ordination because the General Conference has not established it as a requirement in the Discipline.
513.outcome: Affirmed - Bishop's ruling sustained that sexual orientation is not a disqualification for ordination

514.title: Appeal from Bishop's Ruling on Denial of Compensation and Pension Credit to Minister on Special Appointment Who was "Unappointed" for a Period of Five Months
514.summary: A minister who refused an appointment offered by his bishop was not entitled to salary or pension credit during the period he remained without appointment. The Judicial Council upheld the bishop's ruling that refusing an available appointment forfeits compensation rights.
514.keyHolding: A minister who refuses an offered appointment is not entitled to remuneration or pension credit for the period without appointment.
514.parties: Rev. Samuel Little appealing Bishop John Warman's ruling

515.title: Authority of an Annual Conference to Consider for Admission Under Par. 452 a Candidate not Recommended by the Board of Ordained Ministry
515.summary: A Wisconsin Annual Conference member who had surrendered his ministerial office was denied readmission by the Board of Ordained Ministry. The conference tried to override this decision, but the bishop ruled this out of order.
515.keyHolding: Annual Conferences may admit into membership only those who have met all Disciplinary requirements, including recommendation by the Board of Ordained Ministry, and have no authority to waive these requirements.
515.parties: Wisconsin Annual Conference and unnamed former ministerial member seeking readmission
515.outcome: Bishop's ruling that the motion was out of order was appealed to Judicial Council; Annual Conference cannot waive Board of Ordained Ministry recommendation requirement

516.title: Validity of a Decision by a Central Conference to Grant an Annual Conference the Right of Decision to Accept 'Headmanship' for a Ecumenical Church
516.summary: A United Methodist local church may unite with churches of other denominations to form an ecumenical church while remaining part of the UMC connection, provided it follows UMC Discipline and cannot adopt conflicting rules.
516.keyHolding: Local United Methodist churches may participate in ecumenical unions while maintaining their UMC connection, but must remain subject to UMC Discipline and cannot adopt conflicting rules.
516.parties: College of Bishops of the Northern Europe Central Conference through Bishop Ole E. Borgen
516.outcome: Constitutional - Central Conference decision upheld with conditions that ecumenical churches must remain subject to UMC Discipline

517.title: The Responsibility For Fixing Boundaries of Episcopal Areas as Part of the Plan of Episcopal Supervision of Annual Conferences
517.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that bishops, not Jurisdictional Conferences, have the constitutional authority to set the boundaries of episcopal areas as part of their responsibility for arranging episcopal supervision.
517.keyHolding: The power to fix boundaries of episcopal areas is reserved to the bishops as part of episcopal administration under the Constitution and cannot be delegated to Jurisdictional Conferences for final action.

518.title: Meaning, Application and Effect of Discipline Par. 817 on Disbursement of Funds by the National Division of the General Board of Global Ministries to an Organization in Holmes County, Mississippi
518.summary: The North Mississippi Conference asked the Judicial Council to clarify whether the General Board of Global Ministries properly followed required consultation procedures when disbursing $11,000 for civil rights programs in Holmes County, Mississippi.
518.keyHolding: Paragraph 817 requires consultation with the presiding bishop and Council on Ministries before general agency funds are disbursed for programs within an Annual Conference's geographic bounds.
518.outcome: General Board of Global Ministries found in violation of disciplinary consultation requirements

519.title: Appeal of the Decision of the North Central Court of Appeals in the Case of the Southern Illinois Conference vs. the Rev. Joseph C. Evers
519.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed a North Central Jurisdictional Court of Appeals decision in a case between the Southern Illinois Conference and Rev. Joseph C. Evers. The Council upheld the appeals court's ruling after reviewing records and hearing oral arguments from both sides.
519.keyHolding: The Judicial Council affirmed the jurisdictional court of appeals decision in the disciplinary case against Rev. Joseph C. Evers.
519.parties: Southern Illinois Conference vs. the Rev. Joseph C. Evers

520.title: Application of Discipline Par. 805.1, 2 to Annual Conferences Within Central Conferences
520.summary: The General Board of Global Ministries asked whether Annual Conferences in Central Conferences have the same representation rights as those in jurisdictional conferences. The Judicial Council ruled they do not have such rights under current church law.
520.keyHolding: Paragraph 805.1, 2 governing general agency membership applies only to jurisdictional conferences and does not extend representation rights to Annual Conferences within Central Conferences.
520.outcome: No representation rights for Central Conference Annual Conferences under current legislation

521.title: Authority of Annual Conference to Approve Conference Benevolences Budget Recommendations Made by Conference Council on Ministries
521.summary: The South Carolina Annual Conference improperly allowed its Council on Ministries to make budget allocation recommendations directly to the conference, bypassing the required role of the Council on Finance and Administration in the budget process.
521.keyHolding: The Council on Finance and Administration, not the Council on Ministries, has the disciplinary responsibility to present conference benevolences budget recommendations to the Annual Conference, including allocations to individual program agencies.
521.parties: South Carolina Annual Conference and Bishop Roy C. Clark
521.outcome: Bishop's decision reversed - the procedure violated Disciplinary requirements for budget process

522.title: A Ruling by Bishop James S. Thomas on Involuntary Retirement and the Rights of a Minister Based on Discipline Par. 447.3
522.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed the East Ohio Conference's decision to involuntarily retire an elder, finding that proper procedures were followed and the minister's rights were protected throughout the process.
522.keyHolding: Annual conferences may place ministers in involuntary retirement under paragraph 447.3 when proper procedures are followed, even without formal charges being filed against the minister.
522.parties: Rev. O. Lloyd Hutchison vs. East Ohio Annual Conference
522.outcome: Affirmed - involuntary retirement upheld as properly conducted under disciplinary procedures

523.title: Appeal from the New Mexico Annual Conference for a Definition of its Pension Liabilities in the Merger Agreement with the "Northeast New Mexico Group Ministry" in the Light of Par. 1706.9
523.summary: The New Mexico Annual Conference questioned its pension responsibilities when merging with the Northern New Mexico Group Ministry. The Judicial Council ruled that the conference must assume pension liability for all ministerial service within its geographic boundaries, both before and after 1969.
523.keyHolding: In mergers, the successor Annual Conference assumes pension responsibility for all approved pension service rendered within its geographic boundaries.
523.outcome: Bishop's ruling not affirmed; conference assumes broader pension liability

524.title: A Ruling by Bishop Jack Tuell on Discipline Par. 444 Regarding Leave of Absence for a Minister Without Consent of the Minister
524.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed that Annual Conferences can place ministers on involuntary leave of absence without their consent, following proper procedures through the Board of Ordained Ministry and a vote by ministerial members in full connection.
524.keyHolding: An Annual Conference has the authority to grant involuntary leave of absence to a minister without consent under the procedures of Paragraph 444, as a last resort when pastoral responsibilities have been exhausted.
524.parties: Pacific and Southwest Annual Conference seeking ruling on involuntary leave of absence regarding Rev. Morris Floyd
524.outcome: Affirmed - Bishop's ruling upheld that involuntary leave of absence is authorized under proper procedures

525.title: Appeal from the Philippines Annual Conference on a Bishop's Ruling on Attachment of Palawan District to that Conference
525.summary: The Philippines Annual Conference attempted to attach the Palawan District to their conference on an experimental basis, but the Judicial Council ruled this violated the Constitution because only the Central Conference has authority to change conference boundaries.
525.keyHolding: Annual conferences do not have constitutional authority to change conference boundaries, even on a temporary or experimental basis, as this power belongs exclusively to the Central Conference.
525.parties: Philippines Annual Conference appealing Bishop Emerito Nacpil's ruling
525.outcome: Reversed - Bishop's ruling declared unconstitutional and illegal, conference action nullified

526.title: Application for Rehearing of Decision No. 514
526.summary: The Judicial Council denied an application to rehear Decision No. 514.
526.keyHolding: The Judicial Council denied the application for rehearing without further explanation.

527.title: Consideration of an Application for Rehearing of Memorandum No. 509
527.summary: The Judicial Council denied an application to rehear Memorandum No. 509.
527.keyHolding: The Judicial Council denied the request to reconsider its previous Memorandum No. 509.

528.title: Application for Rehearing of Decision No. 515
528.summary: The Judicial Council denied an application requesting a rehearing of Decision No. 515.
528.keyHolding: The Judicial Council denied the application for rehearing without stated grounds.

529.title: Consideration of an Application for Rehearing of Memorandum No. 522
529.summary: The Judicial Council denied a request to rehear their previous decision in Memorandum No. 522.
529.keyHolding: The application for rehearing of Memorandum No. 522 was denied by the Judicial Council.

530.title: For Reconsideration of Decision No. 524
530.summary: Rev. Morris Floyd requested reconsideration of Decision 524, claiming it was based on incorrect facts about his appointment situation. The Judicial Council corrected the factual error but denied further reconsideration since the error didn't affect the legal ruling.
530.keyHolding: Correction of factual errors in a decision does not require reversal if the error was not material to the legal ruling made.
530.outcome: Factual error corrected but reconsideration denied

531.title: Eligibility of a Retired Ministerial Member of an Annual Conference for Election to General and Jurisdictional Conferences
531.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed a bishop's ruling that retired ministers can be elected as delegates to General and Jurisdictional Conferences if they meet all constitutional requirements.
531.keyHolding: Retired ministers who meet the constitutional requirements for traveling ministers are eligible for election to General and Jurisdictional Conferences.
531.parties: Members of the Southern New Jersey Annual Conference

532.title: Review of Bishop's Ruling in Annual Conference Session
532.summary: The Judicial Council ruled it had no jurisdiction to review a bishop's parliamentary ruling when the motion to appeal failed to receive the required one-fifth vote of the annual conference.
532.keyHolding: The Judicial Council lacks jurisdiction to review episcopal rulings that are essentially parliamentary in nature and were not properly appealed by the required one-fifth vote of the conference.
532.parties: Wisconsin Annual Conference member who made the motion

533.title: Use of Ministerial Education Fund for Administrative Expense of the Conference Board of Ordained Ministry in Light of Discipline Par. 920.1
533.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that Annual Conferences cannot use Ministerial Education Fund money to pay for administrative expenses of their Board of Ordained Ministry. These administrative costs must come from the regular conference budget instead.
533.keyHolding: Administrative costs of the Board of Ordained Ministry shall be a claim on the conference budget and cannot be paid from the Ministerial Education Fund.
533.outcome: Annual Conference cannot use Ministerial Education Fund for Board of Ordained Ministry administrative expenses

534.title: Eligibility for Election to General and Jurisdictional Conferences of a Ministerial Member of an Annual Conference While Under Suspension
534.summary: A suspended elder cannot be elected as a delegate to General or Jurisdictional Conference because suspension removes the functions of ordained ministry required for such service.
534.keyHolding: Ministers under suspension from the functions of the office of an Elder are not eligible for election to General or Jurisdictional Conference.
534.parties: Thomas Lane Butts (suspended elder) and Alabama-West Florida Conference
534.outcome: Affirmed - suspended elder ineligible for conference delegate election

535.title: Jurisdiction of the Judicial Council to Make a Ruling in the Nature of a Declaratory Decision Upon a Petition From a Division of a General Board
535.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that divisions of general boards do not have authority to petition for declaratory decisions, only full general agencies can make such requests.
535.keyHolding: Under Paragraph 2615, only general agencies, not divisions or committees of general boards, qualify as 'General Conference bodies' authorized to petition the Judicial Council for declaratory decisions.
535.parties: Division of Ordained Ministry of the General Board of Higher Education and Ministry
535.outcome: No Jurisdiction - Division lacks authority to petition for declaratory decisions

536.title: Authority of an Annual Conference to Establish Higher Standards for Admission to Ministerial Membership than Those Prescribed by the Discipline
536.summary: The Judicial Council reconsidered whether annual conferences can add requirements beyond what the Discipline requires for ministerial membership. While they cannot reduce requirements, they may add additional ones if they don't conflict with General Conference legislation.
536.keyHolding: An Annual Conference may not subtract from disciplinary requirements for ministerial membership but may adopt additional requirements that do not conflict with General Conference legislation or the spirit and intent of the Discipline.
536.parties: Judicial Council on its own motion
536.outcome: Reconsidered Decision 513 to clarify that Annual Conferences may add requirements for ministerial membership that don't conflict with General Conference legislation

537.title: Whether "Ministerial Members in Full Connection" and "Traveling Preachers" are Synonymous as Used in Discipline Par. 39
537.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that being a ministerial member in full connection and being a traveling preacher are two separate requirements for election as a delegate to General Conference, not the same thing.
537.keyHolding: The terms "ministerial members in full connection" and "traveling preachers" in Paragraph 39 are separate and distinct prerequisites for delegate eligibility, not synonymous terms.
537.parties: Board of Higher Education and Ministry
537.outcome: Constitutional amendment would be required to make proposed new deacons eligible for delegate election

538.title: A Request From the College of Bishops, Western Jurisdiction, for a Declaratory Decision on Matters Relating to the Proposed Creation of a New Episcopal Area
538.summary: The Western Jurisdiction asked if they could create a sixth episcopal area by dividing one Annual Conference into two, with special arrangements for bishop assignments and delegate representation. The Judicial Council said no, the current Discipline doesn't allow these arrangements without General Conference amendments.
538.keyHolding: Jurisdictional Conferences cannot create new episcopal areas or assign bishops with interim authority outside established disciplinary procedures without General Conference amendments to the Discipline.
538.outcome: Both questions answered negatively - current Discipline does not permit proposed arrangements

539.title: Validity of Delegation by Annual Conference to its Council on Ministries or other Agency of Authority to Make Adjustments in Budget Adopted by Conference, and Right of Conference Treasurers to Make Short-Term Investment of Benevolence Funds
539.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that annual conferences cannot give their agencies power to change how benevolence money is allocated, but treasurers may make short-term investments of these funds.
539.keyHolding: Annual conferences may not delegate authority to change benevolence fund allocations to their agencies, as contributions to benevolences shall not be used for any cause other than that to which they have been given.
539.parties: South Carolina Annual Conference (Bishop Roy C. Clark received written request for ruling)
539.outcome: Partial affirmation - delegation of authority to change allocations not permitted, but short-term investment of benevolence funds allowed under proper circumstances

540.title: Constitutionality of Mandatory Election of Member of Judicial Council from Central Conferences in Par. 2601
540.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that requiring one member to be elected from Central Conferences creates preferential treatment that violates equal access principles in the Constitution.
540.keyHolding: Guaranteeing representation to one group on a limited body creates preferred status that denies equal access to membership for all other groups, violating constitutional principles of equal rights and privileges.
540.parties: General Conference petition with one-fifth of delegates; Commission on Central Conferences as party
540.outcome: Unconstitutional - mandatory Central Conference representation on Judicial Council violates equal access principles

541.title: Changes by a Central Conference of the Number of its Annual Conferences. Unconstitutionality of Portion of Par. 638.11
541.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that Central Conferences have constitutional authority to change the number of Annual Conferences within their bounds without General Conference approval, making the restriction in Par. 638.11 unconstitutional.
541.keyHolding: Central Conferences have unrestricted constitutional authority under Par. 45 to change the number of their Annual Conferences, and the General Conference cannot limit this specific constitutional power.
541.parties: Commission on Central Conference Affairs through General Conference motion
541.outcome: Par. 638.11 declared unconstitutional to the extent it restricts Central Conference authority over number of Annual Conferences

542.title: Whether Ordination and Appointment of Self-avowed and Practicing Homosexuals is Precluded by Amendment of Pars. 404, 414, 420, 423, and 431 of the Discipline
542.summary: The General Conference asked whether adding 'fidelity in marriage and celibacy in singleness' to ordination requirements would automatically prevent ordination of homosexual clergy. The Judicial Council ruled that these words don't create absolute bars and Annual Conferences retain authority to decide if candidates meet qualifications.
542.keyHolding: The addition of 'fidelity in marriage and celibacy in singleness' language does not necessarily preclude ordination or appointment of self-avowed practicing homosexuals, as Annual Conferences retain discretion to evaluate whether candidates meet disciplinary standards.
542.parties: General Conference motion for declaratory decision
542.outcome: Neither ordination nor appointment of self-avowed practicing homosexuals is necessarily precluded by the added language

543.title: A Ruling by Bishop William Boyd Grove on a Request to Require Their Approval for the Reduction of a Line Item of a Program Budget of the Annual Conference
543.summary: A bishop made a ruling regarding whether approval is required to reduce a line item in an annual conference's program budget.
543.keyHolding: The matter was deferred for consideration at a later session without establishing a legal precedent.
543.parties: Request regarding annual conference budget line item reduction

544.title: Constitutionality of Par. 402.2, 1984 Discipline which Prohibits the Ordination and Appointment of Self-avowed Practicing Homosexual Persons
544.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that the General Conference has constitutional authority to prohibit the ordination and appointment of self-avowed practicing homosexual persons as clergy. While Annual Conferences evaluate candidates, they cannot contradict General Conference requirements for ministry.
544.keyHolding: The General Conference has constitutional authority under Paragraph 15 to establish minimum standards for ministry, including the prohibition of ordination and appointment of self-avowed practicing homosexual persons.
544.parties: California-Nevada Annual Conference, Southeastern Jurisdictional Association of Boards of the Ordained Ministry, New York Annual Conference, Good News (a Forum for Scriptural Christianity, Inc.)
544.outcome: Constitutional - General Conference has authority to establish minimum standards for ministry including the prohibition in question

545.title: Constitutionality of Discipline Pars. 920.3 and 1630.2 Relating to the Ministerial Education Fund
545.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that General Conference has constitutional authority to require annual conferences to prioritize the Ministerial Education Fund before funding theological schools.
545.keyHolding: General Conference has full legislative power over connectional enterprises like the Ministerial Education Fund and can mandate its priority status over other theological education funding.

546.title: Meaning of General Conference Action on Recommendations Concerning Inclusive Language
546.summary: The Judicial Council clarified that General Conference approved recommendations about inclusive language but only received a study document called "Words that Hurt and Words that Heal" for study, not as official church policy.
546.keyHolding: General Conference receiving a document for study does not make it official church policy or create a mandate for its implementation as guidelines.
546.parties: Dr. John Walker of the Little Rock Conference
546.outcome: Clarified distinction between adopted recommendations and study materials received by General Conference

547.title: Constitutionality of General Conference Action Declaring Housing for Pastors is Not to be Considered Part of Compensation or Remuneration
547.summary: The General Conference has the constitutional authority to declare that pastor housing is not part of compensation but rather a means provided by the local church for ministry purposes.
547.keyHolding: The General Conference has constitutional authority under Par. 15 to define housing as not being part of ministerial compensation or remuneration.
547.parties: General Conference action referred by motion for declaratory decision; Dr. Donald H. Treese, Rev. Kathy Nickerson of General Board of Higher Education and Ministry, and Rev. Albert Rhodes-Wickett of Pacific and Southwest Annual Conference appeared
547.outcome: Constitutional - General Conference action declaring housing is not compensation is constitutionally valid

548.title: The Constitutionality, Meaning and Effect of 1980 Discipline Par. 649, as to its Fulfillment by the Philippine Central and Annual Conferences, Relating to the Process by which Parts of The United Methodist Church may become Autonomous Methodist Bodies or Affiliated Churches
548.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that the Philippines Central Conference's votes for autonomy were invalid because not all required votes were properly taken and recorded within the authorized 1976-1980 quadrennium, with some votes occurring in 1981.
548.keyHolding: All votes required for a Central Conference to become autonomous must be taken and properly recorded during the quadrennium authorized by the General Conference Enabling Act.
548.parties: United Methodist Youth Fellowship in the Philippines
548.outcome: The 1981 action of the Philippines Annual Conference did not fulfill the directive of the 1976 Enabling Act in a timely fashion - votes were invalid

549.title: The Constitutionality of Discipline Pars. 636.1 and 638.11 Regarding the Authority to Determine Annual Conference Borders Within a Central Conference
549.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that provisions allowing Central Conferences to fix boundaries of Annual Conferences within their territory are constitutional and do not conflict with General Conference authority.
549.keyHolding: Discipline paragraphs 636.1 and 638.11 regarding Central Conference authority to determine Annual Conference boundaries are constitutional.
549.parties: Vileu Schneeberger of Czechoslovakia and Commission on Central Conference affairs
549.outcome: Constitutional - provisions upheld as not violating the Constitution

550.title: Relationship of Committee on Pastor-Parish Relations to Administrative Board
550.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed that Pastor-Parish Relations Committees are not required to be accountable to Administrative Boards in matters of pastoral appointments, though they must follow Administrative Board decisions in areas like budgets and housing.
550.keyHolding: The Pastor-Parish Relations Committee is not amenable to the Administrative Board in the consultation process surrounding ministerial appointments, but serves as an advisory participant in the consultative process.
550.parties: Theo Brannon, Russel Peters and L. W. Brown from the Alabama-West Florida Annual Conference
550.outcome: Affirmed - Pastor-Parish Relations Committee is not amenable to Administrative Board regarding ministerial appointments

551.title: Disciplinary Requirements Concerning Recommendations to Annual Conference by Conference Council on Finance and Administration
551.summary: The Judicial Council reviewed a bishop's ruling that a Conference Council on Finance and Administration violated the Discipline by recommending budget cuts to program agencies without proper consultation with the Conference Council on Ministries.
551.keyHolding: Conference Councils on Finance and Administration must consult with the Council on Ministries and affected program agencies before making recommendations that impact their budgets, even for long-range financial planning.
551.parties: West Virginia Annual Conference requesting review of Bishop William Boyd Grove's ruling
551.outcome: Bishop's ruling affirmed - the Council on Finance and Administration must follow proper consultation procedures

552.title: Ministerial Relationships to Annual Conferences as Defined in Pars. 36, 421, and 422 as Related to Pars. 454.4 and 458 of the 1984 Discipline
552.summary: A minister who voluntarily gives up their credentials to an annual conference must return to that same conference (or its successor) if they want to be readmitted to ministry later.
552.keyHolding: Ministers who surrender credentials must seek readmission from the same Annual Conference to which they surrendered, or its legal successor.
552.outcome: Declaratory decision clarifying that readmission must be sought from the same Annual Conference where credentials were surrendered

553.title: Lay/Clergy Equalization in the Annual Conference as Provided in the Constitution, Par. 35, of the 1984 Discipline
553.summary: The Oregon-Idaho Annual Conference tried to count only clergy who attended conference sessions when equalizing lay and clergy representation, but the Judicial Council ruled this violated the Constitution which requires counting all clergy members.
553.keyHolding: Constitutional lay/clergy equalization in Annual Conference must be based on actual clergy membership, not clergy attendance at conference sessions.
553.parties: Oregon-Idaho Annual Conference (Earl Riddle and David Kinman representing)

554.title: Constitutionality, Meaning and Application or Effect of the Second Sentence of Discipline Par. 425.1 and Whether a Person Must Consent to an Appointment Under Par. 425.1
554.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that ministers from other conferences or Methodist denominations can be appointed to serve in a conference while keeping their home membership, but they must consent to such appointments.
554.keyHolding: Ministers from other Annual Conferences or Methodist denominations may not be appointed under Par. 425.1 without their consent, and this provision does not conflict with other membership categories in the Discipline.
554.outcome: Constitutional - consent required for appointments under Par. 425.1

555.title: Meaning of "Executive Session" of an Annual Conference and Eligibility of those Attending and Participating in Such Sessions
555.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that Annual Conference Executive Sessions must be held to discuss clergy matters and are restricted to ordained ministers in full connection with that conference, though others may be invited without voting rights.
555.keyHolding: Executive Sessions of Annual Conferences are mandatory and must be closed to all except ordained members in full connection within that conference, with limited exceptions by invitation.
555.parties: Memphis Annual Conference, Southern New England Conference, and Southwest Texas Conference
555.outcome: Executive Sessions are mandated and must be closed except to ordained members in full connection, with limited invitation privileges

556.title: Meaning, Application and Effect of Discipline Par. 532.5(b)2 in Relation to the Process of Appointment-making in a Cooperative Parish
556.summary: The West Virginia Annual Conference asked whether bishops must consult with cooperative parish coordinators when making appointments, even in loosely organized parishes where coordinators lack supervisory authority.
556.keyHolding: When making appointments to any type of Cooperative Parish, bishops and cabinets must confer with the coordinator, director, or a representative of the cooperative ministry staff, regardless of the parish's organizational structure.
556.outcome: Decision requires consultation with cooperative parish leadership in all appointment processes, rejecting the conference's argument for exemption based on loose organizational structure

557.title: Precedence of Par. 455.1 or Par. 2623.3(b) in Matters Involving Termination of Ministers
557.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that district superintendents have discretion to choose between two different processes for handling ministerial problems - the administrative reconciliation process or the formal trial process - based on the nature and severity of the situation.
557.keyHolding: District superintendents may choose between administrative reconciliation procedures (¶455.1) and formal trial procedures (¶2623.3(b)) based on the nature of the grievance or accusation and surrounding circumstances.
557.outcome: District superintendents have discretionary authority to determine which process to initiate based on circumstances

558.title: Eligibility of Retired Ministers for Election to Conference Boards and Agencies
558.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that restrictions preventing retired ministers from serving on certain conference boards violated their constitutional rights as full members of Annual Conference.
558.keyHolding: Restrictions on retired ministers' eligibility to serve on conference boards based solely on their retired status constitute unconstitutional discrimination that violates their membership rights.
558.outcome: The restriction in ¶453.6 was declared unconstitutional as discriminatory against retired ministers

559.title: Validity of a Conference Rule Concerning Beginning Date of Service for Quadrennial Agencies and Officers as Relates to Discipline Par. 819.2
559.summary: The South Carolina Annual Conference asked if it could legally have its quadrennial boards and committees begin their terms when they organize, rather than waiting until January 1st. The Judicial Council ruled this was permissible.
559.keyHolding: Annual conferences may establish terms of office for quadrennial agencies that begin with organization before the standard January 1st start date, as long as members serve until successors are elected.

560.title: Bishop's Ruling Regarding the Authority of a Conference Council on Finance and Administration to Rescind an Action of the Full Annual Conference
560.summary: A bishop ruled that a Conference Council on Finance and Administration cannot overturn decisions made by the full Annual Conference. The Judicial Council affirmed this ruling.
560.keyHolding: Only an Annual Conference can rescind its own actions; the Conference Council on Finance and Administration does not have authority to rescind actions of the full Annual Conference.

561.title: Inclusion of Diaconal Ministers and Other Designated Lay Members in Formula for Equalization Under Constitution Par. 35, 1984 Discipline, As Amended
561.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that diaconal ministers and other designated lay members must be counted as lay members when determining if additional lay delegates need to be elected to equalize clergy and lay representation at Annual Conference.
561.keyHolding: All lay members elected to an Annual Conference by virtue of office or special designation, including Diaconal Ministers, cannot be excluded from the count of lay members prior to the process of equalization of ministerial and lay members.
561.outcome: Constitutional interpretation affirmed that diaconal ministers and other designated lay members must be included in lay member count for equalization purposes

562.title: Request for a Declaratory Decision Concerning Housing Allowances for Clergy Couples in Light of ¶ 256.3(f)
562.summary: The California-Pacific Annual Conference cannot require that each minister receive individual housing regardless of their spouse's housing situation. The Discipline's provisions on clergy couple housing take precedence over conference resolutions.
562.keyHolding: Annual conferences cannot adopt legislation that contravenes ¶ 256.3(f) by making individual housing compulsory for each clergy member regardless of spousal housing provisions.
562.parties: California-Pacific Annual Conference members requesting declaratory decision
562.outcome: Conference resolution ruled impermissible as it would contravene Discipline provisions on clergy housing

563.title: Appeal of Robert Wong
563.summary: A minister appealed his conviction for immorality and disobedience, challenging various procedural aspects of his trial, but the Judicial Council upheld the Western Jurisdiction's Court of Appeals decision.
563.keyHolding: The accused is not guaranteed the right to be brought face to face with every witness or to attend every meeting of the Committee on Investigation, and failure to achieve face-to-face meeting with the accuser does not invalidate the investigation.
563.parties: Robert Wong (ministerial member of California-Pacific Conference)
563.outcome: Affirmed - The Western Jurisdiction Court of Appeals ruling sustaining the convictions and penalty was upheld

564.title: The Request of the Western Jurisdictional Court of Appeals as to Whether a Trial Court of an Annual Conference May Issue a Penalty which is a Departure from Discipline ¶2624.1(h)
564.summary: The Western Jurisdictional Court of Appeals tried to ask the Judicial Council for a ruling about trial court penalties, but the Judicial Council said they don't have authority to make such requests.
564.keyHolding: Jurisdictional Courts of Appeals do not have the authority to request Declaratory Judgments from the Judicial Council.

565.title: In Re: Robert Wong
565.summary: The Judicial Council denied a cross-appeal by the church in the Robert Wong case, ruling that no further appeals would be allowed in this matter.
565.keyHolding: The Judicial Council has discretion to deny cross-appeals and limit further appellate proceedings in church trial cases.
565.outcome: Cross-appeal denied, no further appeals allowed

566.title: Jurisdiction of the Judicial Council to Waive Publication Requirements on a Petition from the General Board of Higher Education and Ministry
566.summary: The General Board of Higher Education and Ministry filed a petition too late to meet publication requirements. The Judicial Council refused to waive the publication requirement and postponed the case to October 1986.
566.keyHolding: The Judicial Council will not waive the publication requirement for declaratory decision petitions that are filed too late to meet the thirty-day publication deadline.
566.parties: General Board of Higher Education and Ministry
566.outcome: Petition deferred to October 1986 due to failure to meet publication requirements

567.title: The Interpretation and Application of ¶¶ 813, 1006.15, 814, and 15.14 of the 1984 Discipline Concerning the Process for Election of General Secretaries
567.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that the General Council on Ministries can properly elect general secretaries, but struck down a rule limiting clergy general secretaries to 12-year terms while allowing lay general secretaries unlimited terms.
567.keyHolding: Term limitations that apply only to clergy general secretaries but not lay general secretaries violate constitutional guarantees of equality of status.
567.parties: General Board of Higher Education and Ministry
567.outcome: Election procedures constitutional; clergy term limits unconstitutional

568.title: Whether Ministerial Pension Plan Section 2.1(k) and Comprehensive Protection Plan Section 2.1(g) Violate Discipline 256.3(f)
568.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that pension plan provisions defining compensation differently from Disciplinary standards for ministerial salaries are valid and constitutional.
568.keyHolding: Legislative bodies may define the same word differently when dealing with separate circumstances and different purposes.
568.outcome: Constitutional - pension plan compensation definitions upheld as valid

569.title: Request from the Southern New England Annual Conference for a Ruling on Annual Conference Use of Interest Earned by Ministerial Education Fund Moneys
569.summary: The Southern New England Annual Conference asked the Judicial Council whether it was proper to use interest from ministerial education funds for other purposes, but the Council ruled it had no jurisdiction to answer this question.
569.keyHolding: An annual conference cannot bring matters before the Judicial Council unless they meet specific jurisdictional requirements outlined in the Discipline.

570.title: A Bishop's Ruling on Annual Conference Membership for Annual Conference Chancellors
570.summary: Bishop Ault ruled that an annual conference petition restricting the chancellor's membership and role was out of order because it would interfere with General Conference legislation.
570.keyHolding: Annual conferences cannot restrict General Conference legislation regarding the role of chancellors through local petitions.

571.title: Appeal of John P. Carter and the Cross-Appeal of the Baltimore Annual Conference
571.summary: A clergy member appealed his conviction for disobedience, and the Judicial Council remanded the case because the Court of Appeals made vague statements about racism in the record without providing specific documentation.
571.keyHolding: Courts of Appeals must either specifically document allegations of racism in trial records or expunge such statements from their decisions.
571.parties: Rev. John P. Carter and the Baltimore Annual Conference

572.title: The Effect of the 1984 Disciplinary Requirements on the Right of an Annual Conference to Equate Years of Part-Time Service to Full-Time Service
572.summary: Annual Conferences have the authority to count part-time pastoral service as equivalent to full-time service when considering candidates for associate membership, based on their judgment of the quality and duration of service.
572.keyHolding: An Annual Conference may equate part-time pastoral service to the disciplinary requirement of full-time service for admission to conference membership through factual determination on a case-by-case basis.
572.outcome: Conference authority to equate part-time service affirmed

573.title: Request from an Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision on a Proposed Salary Plan for Ministers
573.summary: The Baltimore Annual Conference asked the Judicial Council to review a proposed clergy salary plan before adopting it. The Judicial Council declined, saying it lacks authority to review proposed conference legislation.
573.keyHolding: The Judicial Council does not have authority to determine the constitutionality of proposed legislation from an Annual Conference.

574.title: A Review of a Ruling by Bishop Roy Santo at the Rocky Mountain Annual Conference Session, June 1986, Concerning the Constitution of a Committee on Investigation
574.summary: The Judicial Council reviewed whether a Committee on Investigation was properly formed at Rocky Mountain Annual Conference. The Council affirmed the bishop's ruling that the committee was correctly constituted despite challenges about some members' prior involvement.
574.keyHolding: A Committee on Investigation is properly constituted when members are selected according to explicit disciplinary provisions, even if some members had formal or informal contacts with the accused that fall short of being parties to prior proceedings.
574.parties: Request for review of Bishop Roy Sano's ruling at Rocky Mountain Annual Conference
574.outcome: Affirmed - Committee on Investigation was properly constituted

575.title: In Re: Remanded Decision of the Northeastern Jurisdictional Court of Appeals in Appeal of John P. Carter and Cross Appeal of the Baltimore Annual Conference
575.summary: The Judicial Council sustained a clergy trial conviction after the jurisdictional appeals court failed to provide documentation for claims of racism in the trial proceedings. The appeals court reduced the suspension from three years to two years and removed the requirement for public apology.
575.keyHolding: Unsupported declarations that racism exists in trial proceedings cannot be considered evidence and must either be documented or expunged from appellate decisions.
575.parties: John P. Carter (accused clergy), Baltimore Annual Conference
575.outcome: Affirmed trial court conviction with modified penalty (reduced suspension period and removed public apology requirement)

576.title: An Appeal From a Bishop's Ruling that Discipline Par. 706 Takes Precedence Over Par. 738, as it Relates to a Conference Commission or Committee on Christian Unity and Interreligious Concerns
576.summary: The Virginia Annual Conference could organize its Christian Unity and Interreligious Concerns work as a division of the Board of Global Ministries rather than as a separate committee, as long as it maintained proper connections with the broader church.
576.keyHolding: Annual Conferences have authority to structure themselves for effective mission in any appropriate mode, provided they maintain connectional relationships between general boards and the conference, district and local church levels.
576.parties: Virginia Annual Conference (via appeal of Bishop Robert M. Blackburn's ruling)
576.outcome: Affirmed - Annual Conference has authority to structure its Christian Unity committee as part of Board of Global Ministries

577.title: Authority of General Board of Pensions to Offer a New Fund for Ministers' Contributions Between Sessions of the General Conference
577.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that the General Board of Pensions cannot create a new social witness fund for ministerial pension investments without General Conference approval.
577.keyHolding: Only the General Conference has authority to create, establish, revise, amend, terminate or continue pension plans and their component funds for The United Methodist Church.
577.parties: New York Annual Conference requesting declaratory decision
577.outcome: General Board of Pensions lacks authority to establish new pension fund without General Conference authorization

578.title: Petition from the Executive Committee of the South Central Jurisdiction for a Declaratory Decision Concerning the Constitutionality, Meaning, Application or Effect of the 1984 Discipline Pars. 509.1(a) and 453.1 as They Affect Mandatory Age Retirement for Bishops and Pastors
578.summary: The South Central Jurisdiction's Executive Committee lacked authority to petition the Judicial Council about mandatory retirement ages for bishops and pastors. The Council noted that different retirement rules for bishops versus other clergy are constitutional.
578.keyHolding: The Executive Committee of a Jurisdictional Conference does not have authority under the Discipline to bring petitions to the Judicial Council regarding mandatory retirement provisions.
578.parties: Executive Committee of the South Central Jurisdiction

579.title: Constitutionality of Certain Provisions of Equitable Salary System Plan Adopted by the South Carolina Annual Conference
