579.summary: The South Carolina Annual Conference asked the Judicial Council to review whether certain provisions in their equitable salary guidelines were constitutional. The Council ruled that conference guidelines cannot deny full members in good standing their guaranteed minimum salary.
579.keyHolding: Annual conferences cannot establish guidelines that would result in full members in good standing receiving less than the established minimum salary.
579.outcome: Sections C, F, K, T, and U of the South Carolina Annual Conference equitable salary guidelines declared null and void as unconstitutional

580.title: In Re: M.A. Kunkle, West Ohio Conference
580.summary: The Judicial Council upheld a jurisdictional court's order for a new trial due to flawed procedures in a clergy misconduct case, but ruled that trials must be held in the conference where the minister holds membership, not where they serve.
580.keyHolding: Annual conferences have constitutional authority to conduct trials of their own ministerial members regardless of where those ministers are serving, and procedurally flawed trials must be remanded for new proceedings.
580.parties: M.A. Kunkle (accused minister) and West Ohio Conference
580.outcome: Modified - upheld order for new trial and benefit payments but rejected jurisdictional court's opinion on proper venue for ministerial trials

581.title: Eligibility of a Minister for Appointment While on Leave of Absence
581.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed a bishop's ruling that ministers on leave of absence cannot receive appointments to local churches, though they may perform limited ministry in the charge where they hold membership.
581.keyHolding: A minister on leave of absence does not remain in full-time itinerant ministry and therefore cannot be appointed to serve a local parish.
581.parties: North Indiana Annual Conference appealing Bishop Leroy C. Hodapp's ruling

582.title: A Review of a Ruling by Bishop David J. Lawson in the Wisconsin Conference on Judicial Council Decisions No. 400 and 521 Regarding the Budgeting Process of an Annual Conference
582.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that annual conference budgets must show specific dollar amounts for all programs from the very beginning of the conference session, not just lump sum reductions to be figured out later.
582.keyHolding: A Conference Council on Finance and Administration must present a budget with specific allocations for each conference benevolence cause at the opening session of Annual Conference, not merely lump sum reductions.
582.parties: Wisconsin Annual Conference seeking review of Bishop David J. Lawson's ruling
582.outcome: Reversed - Bishop's ruling overturned, requiring specific budget allocations at opening session

583.title: Status, Relationship, and Amenability of a Local Deacon or a Local Elder Under Discipline
583.summary: The Judicial Council clarified that local deacons and elders are lay persons who are primarily accountable to their Charge Conference, not clergy members of the Annual Conference. If appointed by an Annual Conference, they are only amenable to that conference for matters related to their specific assignment.
583.keyHolding: Local deacons and elders are lay persons accountable to a Charge Conference, not clergy members of the Annual Conference.
583.outcome: Declaratory decision issued clarifying that local deacons and elders are lay persons accountable to Charge Conference

584.title: Delegation of Power to the Cabinet to Act for the Annual Conference
584.summary: The West Virginia Annual Conference wanted to give its cabinet full authority to act on its behalf between sessions, but the bishop ruled this was not allowed under church law.
584.keyHolding: An Annual Conference may not delegate any authority given to it by the Discipline to another body such as the cabinet.
584.parties: West Virginia Annual Conference Cabinet and Bishop William Boyd Grove
584.outcome: Affirmed - bishop's ruling that the delegation of authority would be improper was upheld

585.title: The Establishment of a Pension Escrow Fund to Divert Funds from the General Board of Pensions
585.summary: Two annual conferences tried to create alternative pension funds because they disagreed with the General Board of Pensions' investment policies regarding South Africa. The Judicial Council ruled that annual conferences do not have authority to establish separate pension programs or divert pension contributions.
585.keyHolding: Annual conferences do not have authority to establish alternative pension plans or divert contributions into escrow funds, as full authority over pension administration rests with the General Board of Pensions.
585.parties: Southern New England Annual Conference, New York Annual Conference, John Collins, Richard S. Parker, James M. Walton-Myers of the General Board of Pensions
585.outcome: Annual conferences' proposed alternative pension plans ruled unconstitutional and beyond their authority

586.title: A Review of a Ruling by Bishop Jesse DeWitt in the Northern Illinois Conference Concerning the Eligibility of a Candidate for Deacon's Orders Who Did Not Receive the Necessary 3/4 Vote by Written Ballot in the District Committee
586.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that once a district committee recommends a candidate for ordination and the Conference Board accepts it, the district cannot later withdraw that recommendation based on procedural irregularities.
586.keyHolding: Once a District Committee on Ministry recommends a candidate to the Conference Board of Ordained Ministry and the Board accepts that recommendation, the district committee may not redetermine the candidate's eligibility.
586.parties: Northern Illinois Conference challenging Bishop Jesse DeWitt's ruling regarding Phyllis Athey's candidacy
586.outcome: Reversed - Bishop's ruling vacated, matter remanded to Annual Conference ministerial members

587.title: Minimum Salary Policies and Procedures in the New Hampshire Conference
587.summary: A clergy couple challenged their Annual Conference's policies that prevented them from receiving the minimum salary despite being full members with full-time appointments. The Judicial Council ruled that conferences cannot adopt policies that prevent full members from receiving established minimum salaries.
587.keyHolding: Annual Conferences cannot establish minimum salary guidelines and then provide means to avoid paying that minimum to ministers in full connection.
587.parties: John A. and Priscilla R. MacDougall
587.outcome: Affirmed - Bishop's ruling that full members are entitled to minimum salary was upheld

588.title: A Review of a Ruling By Bishop David J. Lawson in the Wisconsin Conference Relating to the Constitutionality of the Conference's Ministerial Housing Policy; A Review of a Ruling by Bishop Jack Tuell in the California-Pacific Conference Declaring Constitutional an Action of the Annual Conference Which Sought to Define 'Adequate Housing' as it Relates to Clergy Couples
588.summary: The Judicial Council reviewed two bishops' rulings on clergy housing policies, finding that Wisconsin's housing policy did not actually conflict with church law and overruling Bishop Lawson, while affirming Bishop Tuell's ruling that clergy couples housing policies are constitutional if they provide adequate housing without discrimination.
588.keyHolding: Annual conferences may provide housing or housing allowances to clergy without violating constitutional provisions, and clergy couple housing policies are constitutional as long as they ensure adequate housing based on practical factors rather than marital status discrimination.
588.parties: Wisconsin Annual Conference and California-Pacific Annual Conference
588.outcome: Bishop Lawson overruled regarding Wisconsin housing policy; Bishop Tuell affirmed regarding clergy couples housing policy

589.title: A Request From the West Virginia Annual Conference and the New York Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision on the Constitutionality of the Ruling and Decision of the University Senate of the United Methodist Church as to Morristown College
589.summary: The West Virginia and New York Annual Conferences challenged the University Senate's decision to remove Morristown College, a historically Black Methodist college, from the approved list due to financial problems and academic probation.
589.keyHolding: The case involves a challenge to the University Senate's authority to remove a college from the approved list of United Methodist institutions.
589.parties: West Virginia Annual Conference and New York Annual Conference
589.outcome: Request for declaratory decision on University Senate's removal of Morristown College from approved list

590.title: Delegation of Power to the Conference Council on Finance and Administration or Any Other Conference Agency to Act For the Annual Conference
590.summary: A bishop ruled that annual conferences cannot delegate their authority over budget distribution to their finance committees or other agencies. The Judicial Council affirmed this ruling.
590.keyHolding: The Annual Conference may not delegate any authority given it by the Discipline to boards and agencies.
590.parties: Request made to Bishop James S. Thomas

591.title: Review of a Ruling by Bishop James S. Thomas in the East Ohio Conference Concerning the Adoption by an Annual Conference of a Unified "Administrative Budget" Which Prioritizes Apportionments for Ministerial Support
591.summary: The Judicial Council upheld a bishop's ruling that annual conferences cannot prioritize certain apportionments (like ministerial support) over others when collecting funds from local churches.
591.keyHolding: Annual conferences must apply local church contributions to the specific budgeted funds for which they were designated and cannot establish priority claims for certain apportionment categories.
591.outcome: Affirmed - Bishop's ruling that prioritizing ministerial support apportionments violates the Discipline was upheld

592.title: A Request from the North Carolina Annual Conference for a Decision on the Legality of Action Requiring General and Jurisdictional Conference Delegates to Submit a Record of Their Voting
592.summary: The North Carolina Annual Conference tried to require its General and Jurisdictional Conference delegates to report how they voted on important matters, but the Judicial Council ruled this was not allowed and declared the action invalid.
592.keyHolding: Annual Conferences have no authority to require delegates to General and Jurisdictional Conferences to report their individual voting records.
592.outcome: Unconstitutional - action declared null and void

593.title: Precedence of 810.3 or 1702 as it Relates to Eligibility for Consecutive Quadrennial Membership on General Agencies
593.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that new term limits for general agency service don't invalidate elections that happened before the limits took effect, but do apply to future elections.
593.keyHolding: New legislation limiting consecutive service on general agencies applies only to future elections and does not invalidate or curtail terms from elections held prior to the effective date.
593.outcome: The two board members could continue serving through their elected terms despite new term limits

594.title: Constitutionality of Mandatory Categories of Membership on the Judicial Council
594.summary: The Judicial Council ruled unconstitutional any proposal requiring mandatory categories of membership (such as guaranteed seats for specific groups) on the Judicial Council itself.
594.keyHolding: Mandatory categories of nomination and membership on the Judicial Council are unconstitutional because they create preferred status for some groups while denying access to others.

595.title: Appeal Process As Described in Par. 2625 of the 1984 Discipline
595.summary: The Judicial Council clarified that all clergy, including local pastors and diaconal ministers, have the constitutional right to appeal trial decisions. The church cannot initiate appeals but can respond once an appeal is filed.
595.keyHolding: Paragraph 18 of the Constitution guarantees the right of appeal to all members of the Church, including local pastors, diaconal ministers, and ministerial members of all conferences.
595.outcome: Constitutional - appeal rights confirmed for all clergy

596.title: Request for Ruling in Relation to ¶906.12
596.summary: The General Conference tried to refer six questions about ¶906.12 to the Judicial Council for a declaratory decision, but the vote failed 466-471, which was not a majority as required.
596.keyHolding: A majority vote of the General Conference is required to refer matters for declaratory decision to the Judicial Council, and a failed vote means the Judicial Council has no jurisdiction to hear the case.
596.outcome: No Jurisdiction - matter improperly referred due to failed majority vote

597.title: Right of the General Conference to Direct a Study of Homosexuality to Be Conducted by the General Council on Ministries, and Funded Within the Budget of That Council
597.summary: The General Conference can direct the General Council on Ministries to study homosexuality using church funds because such a study does not promote homosexuality but rather seeks to provide information to help the church resolve differences of opinion.
597.keyHolding: Church funds may be used for studying homosexuality when the purpose is informational rather than promotional, as this does not violate the prohibition against using funds to promote acceptance of homosexuality.
597.outcome: Constitutional - study authorized within budget constraints

598.title: Constitutionality of General Conference Action Authorizing Division of Episcopal Areas When Conferences Exceed Certain Membership
598.summary: The General Conference can constitutionally authorize the division of episcopal areas when annual conferences within them exceed 125,000 members each.
598.keyHolding: The General Conference has constitutional authority under ¶15 to establish formulas for the number of bishops permitted each jurisdiction, including provisions for dividing episcopal areas based on membership thresholds.

599.title: Legality of Proposed Royal Dutch/Shell Boycott
599.summary: The Judicial Council suspended implementation of a proposed boycott of Royal Dutch/Shell because they lacked sufficient information to rule on its legality.
599.keyHolding: The Judicial Council may suspend implementation of General Conference actions when insufficient information exists to determine their legality.

600.title: Legality of Amendment to 805.1(b) Concerning Annual Conference Nominations to Jurisdictional Pool
600.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that a General Conference amendment regarding nominations to jurisdictional pools for general agencies was legal and did not create conflicts with existing rules.
600.keyHolding: The amendment to ¶805.1(b) allowing General Conference delegates to be nominated to jurisdictional pools without category limitations does not create procedural conflicts.

601.title: Constitutionality of Representational Requirements for General Program Board Membership
601.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that requirements guaranteeing specific representation of clergy, laymen, and laywomen on general program boards violate the Constitution, but recommendations for diversity are acceptable.
601.keyHolding: Disciplinary provisions that mandate guaranteed representation of preferred status groups on church boards are unconstitutional under Paragraphs 4 and 15.14.
601.outcome: Mandatory representation requirements ruled unconstitutional; recommendatory language upheld as constitutional

602.title: Authority of General Conference to Define Ministerial Membership in An Annual Conference
602.summary: The General Conference has constitutional authority to define who can be voting members of Annual Conferences. New legislation allowing part-time and student local pastors to vote under certain conditions is constitutional.
602.keyHolding: Paragraph 35 of the Constitution grants authority to the General Conference to define ministerial membership in an Annual Conference.
602.parties: General Conference motion for ruling on constitutionality
602.outcome: Constitutional - General Conference has authority to define ministerial membership including part-time and student local pastors under specified conditions

603.title: Petition From the General Conference Regarding the Constitutionality of Limiting Tenure of Elected General Program Agencies Staff
603.summary: The General Conference asked if it was constitutional to limit elected general program agency staff to 12-year terms. The Judicial Council ruled this limitation is constitutional and applies equally to clergy and lay staff.
603.keyHolding: The General Conference has constitutional authority to limit the tenure of elected general program agency staff when such limitations apply equally to clergy and lay persons.
603.parties: General Conference petition; Odella B. Williamson of the New York Annual Conference appeared at oral hearing

604.title: General Conference Adoption of Boycott of Royal Dutch/Shell Products
604.summary: The Judicial Council ruled it had no authority to review General Conference's decision to boycott Shell Oil products because boycotts are connectional matters within General Conference's power.
604.keyHolding: The Judicial Council lacks jurisdiction over General Conference decisions on substantive connectional matters like boycotts that fall within General Conference's constitutional authority.
604.parties: Ewing Werlein, Jr. (representing Shell Oil Company), John E. Stumbo (representing General Board of Global Ministries), and Leonard D. Slutz (representing General Board of Church and Society)
604.outcome: No Jurisdiction - matter falls within General Conference's constitutional authority over connectional matters

605.title: Constitutionality of Legislation Prohibiting General Board or Agency Employees From Serving on Certain General Conference Legislative Committees
605.summary: The General Conference cannot prohibit paid employees of church boards and agencies from serving on legislative committees, as this would create discrimination based on employment status.
605.keyHolding: Legislation that prohibits paid staff of church agencies from serving on legislative committees violates constitutional equal rights protections by creating discrimination based on employment status.

606.title: Request From the Red Bird Missionary Conference as to Status of Ordained Ministers in Full Connection Under Special Appointment in a Missionary Conference
606.summary: The Red Bird Missionary Conference asked whether 1988 changes to rules about ministers serving in other conferences would affect ministers appointed to missionary conferences. The Judicial Council ruled that these changes only apply to annual conferences, not missionary conferences.
606.keyHolding: General Conference amendments to provisions governing ministers serving other Annual Conferences do not affect the special provisions governing ordained ministers in Missionary Conferences.
606.outcome: Clarified that 1988 General Conference amendments do not affect missionary conference provisions

607.title: Appeal of Ruling by Bishop Felton E. May concerning an Action of the Central Pennsylvania Annual Conference in Discontinuing Probationary Member
607.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed a bishop's ruling that probationary members have no right to appeal when an Annual Conference discontinues their probationary membership on recommendation of the Board of Ordained Ministry.
607.keyHolding: Probationary members are under the complete jurisdiction of the Annual Conference and have no provision for appeal when discontinued upon recommendation of the Board of Ordained Ministry.
607.parties: Douglas Essinger-Hileman (through counsel Larry Selkowitz and Rev. Sandra D. Essinger-Hileman) vs. Central Pennsylvania Annual Conference Board of Ordained Ministry
607.outcome: Affirmed - bishop's ruling upheld that no appeal provision exists for discontinued probationary members

608.title: Review of Ruling by Bishop David J. Lawson Concerning Finance and Budget Plan in the Wisconsin Annual Conference
608.summary: The Judicial Council reversed a bishop's ruling that would have allowed the Wisconsin Annual Conference to use category budgeting for a two-year budget cycle instead of annual line-item budgets.
608.keyHolding: Annual conferences must present and approve budgets annually, not on a two-year basis, as there is no provision in the Discipline for multi-year budgets.
608.outcome: Bishop's ruling reversed - two-year category budgeting not permitted

609.title: Request From the Wyoming Annual Conference on Whether "A Resolution of Reconciliation" Adopted by that Conference is Precluded by Language in the 1988 Discipline
609.summary: The Wyoming Annual Conference asked the Judicial Council to determine if their "Resolution of Reconciliation" regarding homosexuals was allowed under church law. The Judicial Council ruled they had no authority to review actions of Annual Conferences.
609.keyHolding: The Judicial Council does not have jurisdiction to review actions of Annual Conferences, only to interpret provisions of the Discipline.
609.outcome: No Jurisdiction - Judicial Council lacks authority to review Annual Conference actions

610.title: Petition From the Kentucky Annual Conference For a Ruling on the Constitutionality of Par. 510.1
610.summary: The Kentucky Annual Conference challenged disciplinary provisions that deny retired bishops the right to vote, but the Judicial Council ruled these provisions are constitutional.
610.keyHolding: Disciplinary provisions denying retired bishops voting rights are constitutional because the Constitution specifically authorizes General Conference to define the powers, duties, and privileges of the episcopacy.
610.outcome: Constitutional - disciplinary provisions denying retired bishops voting rights upheld

611.title: Petition From the General Board of Higher Education and Ministry for Clarification of Pars. 453 and 2623.1 of the 1988 Discipline and Judicial Council Decision No. 557
611.summary: The General Board of Higher Education and Ministry sought clarification on disciplinary procedures for clergy charges. The Council ruled that the joint review process must be completed before charges can be filed, and district superintendents cannot independently forward charges to investigation committees.
611.keyHolding: District superintendents may not independently forward charges to the Committee on Investigation; charges must go through the Board of Ordained Ministry after completing the joint review process.
611.parties: General Board of Higher Education and Ministry
611.outcome: Clarification provided that district superintendents cannot independently forward charges; joint review process required before Board of Ordained Ministry can file charges; Decision 557 reaffirmed

612.title: Reconsideration of Decision 602
612.summary: The Judicial Council reversed its earlier decision and ruled that making local pastors voting members only when appointed is unconstitutional because it gives bishops, not Annual Conferences, the power to determine ministerial membership.
612.keyHolding: Paragraph 701.1(e) is unconstitutional because it allows bishops to determine Annual Conference ministerial membership through appointments, violating the Annual Conference's exclusive constitutional authority under ¶36 to determine its own ministerial membership.
612.parties: Council of Bishops (Bishop Jack M. Tuell presenting oral argument)

613.title: Request for Declaratory Decision Concerning Legality of General Board of Church and Society Action for an Economic Boycott
613.summary: The Judicial Council declined to rule on whether a General Board of Church and Society economic boycott was legal, finding it lacked jurisdiction to review such actions.
613.keyHolding: The Judicial Council's authority to issue declaratory decisions is limited to rulings on the constitutionality, meaning, application and effect of the Discipline or General Conference legislation.

614.title: Custody and Management of Refund from the Medical Expense Program of the General Board of Pensions
614.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that funds held by a Conference Insurance Committee for employee health benefits are not subject to the investment policies of the Conference Council on Finance and Administration.
614.keyHolding: Employee benefit funds are excluded from the investment authority of Conference Councils on Finance and Administration under Paragraph 709.13 of the Discipline.
614.parties: Little Rock Annual Conference Council on Finance and Administration and Little Rock Annual Conference Insurance Committee
614.outcome: Conference Insurance Committee retains authority over employee benefit funds, which are excluded from Conference Council on Finance and Administration investment policies

615.title: Constitutionality of Discipline Paragraph 627 Requiring the Jurisdictional Conference Journal to Be Printed by The United Methodist Publishing House
615.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that General Conference has constitutional authority to require jurisdictional conferences to have their journals printed by The United Methodist Publishing House.
615.keyHolding: The General Conference has full legislative power over all matters distinctively connectional, including requiring jurisdictional conferences to use The United Methodist Publishing House for printing their journals.

616.title: Review of a Ruling by Bishop R. Kern Eutsler in the Holston Annual Conference Concerning Standing Rules for a Proposed Budget Limitation
616.summary: The Judicial Council upheld a bishop's ruling that an annual conference cannot adopt standing rules requiring automatic budget reductions based solely on membership decline, as such rules conflict with Discipline provisions requiring careful budget studies.
616.keyHolding: Annual conferences may adopt rules for their own governance only if such rules do not conflict with the Discipline, and automatic budget reductions based solely on membership decline are inconsistent with required disciplinary procedures for budget preparation.

617.title: Request from the Tennessee Annual Conference for a Ruling on a Proposed Resolution
617.summary: The Tennessee Annual Conference asked the Judicial Council to rule on a resolution about requiring small church representation in General Conference delegations, but the Council declined because the conference never actually voted on the resolution.
617.keyHolding: The Judicial Council lacks jurisdiction to rule on proposed resolutions that have not been formally adopted or rejected by an Annual Conference.

618.title: Request for a Rehearing of Decision 608
618.summary: The Judicial Council denied a request to reconsider Decision 608 regarding Wisconsin Annual Conference's budget plan. The Council reaffirmed that a two-year budget cycle violates the Discipline.
618.keyHolding: A two-year budgeting cycle for annual conference financial requests is contrary to the Discipline and the Judicial Council will not reverse its prior decision without changed circumstances.

619.title: Appeal from Bishop's Ruling in the Virginia Conference Concerning Board of Ordained Ministry Recommendation to Continue a Ministerial Member on Leave of Absence
619.summary: An appeal from a bishop's ruling in Virginia Conference regarding a Board of Ordained Ministry's recommendation about continuing a minister on leave of absence was deferred for later consideration.
619.keyHolding: Matter was deferred without substantive ruling pending further consideration at Fall 1989 meeting.
619.parties: Appeal from Virginia Conference regarding Board of Ordained Ministry recommendation

620.title: Request for rehearing on Decision 607
620.summary: The Judicial Council denied a request to rehear Decision 607.
620.keyHolding: The Judicial Council denied the request for rehearing of Decision 607.

621.title: Petition to Reconsider Memorandum No. 604
621.summary: The Judicial Council denied a petition to reconsider their previous Memorandum No. 604.
621.keyHolding: The Judicial Council denied the petition for reconsideration of Memorandum No. 604.

622.title: Clarification of Eligibility Requirements for Lay Members of an Annual Conference
622.summary: The constitutional requirements for lay members to serve at Annual Conference cannot be changed by adding extra requirements in other parts of the Discipline.
622.keyHolding: The provisions of ¶35 of the Constitution are the exclusive requirements for election as a lay member to Annual Conference and cannot be modified by additional requirements in other sections of the Discipline.

623.title: Ruling by Bishop William Boyd Grove Regarding Mandatory Categories of Membership for Annual Conference Agencies
623.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed a bishop's ruling that annual conferences cannot require mandatory racial, gender, or other status categories for membership on conference agencies, as such requirements violate the UMC Constitution.
623.keyHolding: Annual conferences may not legislate rules that require racial, gender or other status categories in the membership of their agencies as such requirements are unconstitutional.
623.outcome: Affirmed - mandatory status categories ruled unconstitutional, but recommendations for such categories are permissible

624.title: Request for Clarification For Purchasing Property under ¶2515
624.summary: The Missouri East Annual Conference asked for clarification on procedures for purchasing property, but the Judicial Council found the question was moot since the conference had already completed the purchase.
624.keyHolding: Paragraph 2515 governs the sale or encumbrance of Annual Conference properties but does not provide guidelines for property acquisition.

625.title: Southern Illinois Conference "Statement on Human Sexuality"
625.summary: The Judicial Council declined jurisdiction over a Southern Illinois Conference statement on human sexuality but warned that Annual Conferences cannot impose additional requirements on ordained ministers beyond what General Conference establishes.
625.keyHolding: Annual Conferences lack authority to further define and fix the powers and duties of ordained ministers beyond what General Conference establishes, as this would violate the Constitution and Discipline.

626.title: Ineligibility of Ministerial Members on Leave of Absence for Membership on Conference Agencies
626.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that ordained ministers who are on leave of absence cannot serve on conference boards or committees, and this restriction is constitutional.
626.keyHolding: The General Conference has constitutional authority to define ministerial relationships including restricting ministerial members on leave of absence from serving on conference agencies.
626.outcome: Constitutional - restriction on ministerial members on leave of absence serving on conference agencies upheld

627.title: Request of an Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision as to the Constitutionality of the Filling of a Vacancy on the Judicial Council
627.summary: Two Kansas annual conferences asked the Judicial Council to rule on whether the method used to fill a vacancy on the Judicial Council was constitutional. The Judicial Council ruled it lacked jurisdiction because the matter did not relate to annual conference work.
627.keyHolding: The Judicial Council lacks jurisdiction to issue declaratory decisions on matters that do not relate to Annual Conferences or their work, even if they involve constitutional interpretation of the Discipline.
627.parties: Kansas West and Kansas East Annual Conferences
627.outcome: No jurisdiction - petition dismissed for lack of jurisdiction

628.title: Appeal of Dean T. Tony
628.summary: A pastor appealed his removal from ministry, but the jurisdictional court reduced the penalty without explanation. The Judicial Council reinstated the original penalty because appellate courts must explain changes to trial court penalties.
628.keyHolding: Appellate courts must provide a statement of grounds when changing penalties imposed by trial courts, and failure to do so requires reinstatement of the original penalty.
628.parties: Dean T. Tony v. Virginia Conference
628.outcome: Reversed - trial court penalty of removal from ministry reinstated

629.title: Appeal From the Bishop's Ruling in the Virginia Conference Concerning a Board of Ordained Ministry Recommendation to Continue a Ministerial Member on Leave of Absence
629.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that clergy members must receive 90-day advance notice before being continued on leave of absence, and ordered the Virginia Conference to provide compensation for the affected minister.
629.keyHolding: Par. 450.1 of the 1984 Discipline requires that the Board of Ordained Ministry make its decision on its recommendation to the Annual Conference concerning the ending or continuation of a leave of absence 90 days prior to the Annual Conference session, which at least implies that notification of the recommendation be given at that time.
629.parties: Virginia Annual Conference appealing Bishop Robert Blackburn's ruling
629.outcome: Bishop's decision reversed; Virginia Conference must provide compensation to minister from July 1, 1988 until August 12, 1988

630.title: Appeal of Bishop's Decision in West Ohio Conference Concerning Involuntary Retirement of Ministerial Member
630.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that the West Ohio Annual Conference properly followed church law when it voted to involuntarily retire a clergy member after appropriate procedures and hearings.
630.keyHolding: Annual conferences may place clergy in involuntary retirement through proper procedures under ¶453.3 without formal charges or trial rights when done with appropriate notice and opportunities to be heard.
630.parties: Robert Mussman (involuntarily retired clergy member) vs. West Ohio Annual Conference
630.outcome: Affirmed - the involuntary retirement action was conducted in accordance with the Discipline

631.title: Request From the Central Illinois Conference For a Ruling on the Binding Nature of an Agreement Among Three Conferences in Illinois Concerning Distribution of Assets of the Former Illinois Conference of the Evangelical United Brethren Church
631.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that a 1969 agreement dividing assets from the former EUB Illinois Conference among three UMC conferences is legally binding and can only be changed with all parties' consent.
631.keyHolding: Agreements made during the EUB-Methodist Church merger regarding property distribution are binding contracts that can only be amended with consent of all parties.
631.outcome: Agreement declared binding; distribution formula of 52%-35%-13% among the three Illinois conferences affirmed

632.title: The Difference Between Involuntary Leave of Absence (448.1) and Suspension [2624.1(h)], and on the Constitutionality of 448.1
632.summary: The Judicial Council clarified that involuntary leave of absence is a conference relationship determined by the Annual Conference, while suspension is a punitive sanction imposed by trial courts after conviction of charges.
632.keyHolding: Involuntary leave of absence under ¶448.1 is a non-punitive conference relationship that falls within the Annual Conference's constitutional authority, distinct from suspension which is a trial court sanction.
632.outcome: Constitutional - ¶448.1 upheld as within Annual Conference authority under ¶36

633.title: Constitutionality of ¶¶ 726.5(a), 734.1, 735.1, 737.2, 741.2, 754.1, 2512.1, 2518, 2524, and Any Other Paragraphs of the 1988 Discipline which Mandate Guaranteed Representation of Clergy, Laymen and Laywomen
633.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that church laws requiring guaranteed representation of specific groups (clergy, laymen, laywomen) on boards violate the Constitution, but recommendations for such representation are allowed.
633.keyHolding: Constitutional provisions forbid any legislation which would guarantee a preferred status not extended to others, making mandatory representation requirements unconstitutional.
633.outcome: Mandatory representation requirements declared unconstitutional; recommendations for representation remain constitutional

634.title: Legality of Annual Conference Policy Requiring Approval by Bishop and Cabinet of Clergy Housing Arrangement
634.summary: The North Arkansas Annual Conference can require bishop and cabinet approval for alternative clergy housing arrangements beyond traditional parsonages.
634.keyHolding: Annual Conferences have constitutional authority to establish parsonage standards including requiring approval by the bishop and cabinet for optional clergy housing arrangements.
634.outcome: Annual Conference has authority to establish such requirements

635.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the Wisconsin Annual Conference Concerning Legality of Disbursing Annual Conference Funds to the Wisconsin Chapter, Religious Coalition for Abortion Rights (WRCAR)
635.summary: The Judicial Council reviewed whether the Wisconsin Annual Conference could spend money supporting a religious coalition advocating for abortion rights, and affirmed the bishop's ruling that the conference could consider such funding.
635.keyHolding: Annual conferences have the authority to consider and decide whether to fund organizations related to social issues within the bounds of Disciplinary provisions.
635.parties: Wisconsin Annual Conference members requesting ruling on WRCAR funding

636.title: Authority of Annual Conference to Require Local Church Participation in Conference Property and Liability Insurance Program
636.summary: A lay member challenged the Southern New Jersey Annual Conference's authority to require all local churches to participate in a conference-wide insurance program. The Judicial Council affirmed that Annual Conferences have the authority to require local church participation in conference insurance programs.
636.keyHolding: Annual Conferences have the authority to require local churches to participate in conference-wide property and liability insurance programs due to their ultimate interest in all local church property under the trust clause.
636.parties: Lay member from Southern New Jersey Annual Conference appealing Bishop Neil D. Irons' decision of law
636.outcome: Bishop's decision affirmed - Annual Conference has authority to require local church participation in conference insurance program

637.title: Petition from the Northern New Jersey Annual Conference for a Decision as to the Meaning of Par.505 and its Effect on a Proposed Recommendation to a Special Session of the Northeastern Jurisdictional Conference
637.summary: The Northeastern Jurisdiction created a tenth episcopal area called the Albany area, but the Judicial Council ruled that while this action was generally constitutional, a retired bishop cannot be appointed as a resident bishop in this situation.
637.keyHolding: Jurisdictional conferences may create new episcopal areas, but retired bishops cannot serve as resident bishops under ¶ 510.3 of the Discipline.
637.outcome: Action constitutional except for retired bishop appointment provision

638.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in 1989 Session of the Tennessee Annual Conference As To Authority of Pastor-Parish Relations Committee in Matters of Staff Employment
638.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed a bishop's decision that Pastor-Parish Relations Committees must consult with the pastor before making staff hiring decisions unless specific policies have been adopted by the Administrative Board or Council.
638.keyHolding: Until a local church adopts specific personnel policies, the Pastor-Parish Relations Committee and the pastor have joint authority to hire, evaluate, promote, retire and dismiss non-appointed staff personnel.
638.parties: Reverend Roy West vs. Bishop Ernest W. Newman regarding Tennessee Annual Conference
638.outcome: Bishop's decision affirmed - pastor must be consulted on staff hiring decisions unless specific policies have been adopted

639.title: Petition from the East Ohio Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision on a Proposed Restructure Plan
639.summary: The East Ohio Annual Conference asked the Judicial Council to review their proposed restructure plan, but the Council ruled it lacks jurisdiction since it can only review General Conference actions, not preliminary conference proposals.
639.keyHolding: The Judicial Council does not have authority to render decisions on proposed actions of an Annual Conference, only on acts or legislation of General Conference.

640.title: Request From the East Ohio Annual Conference for a Declaratory Judgment as to Whether an Annual Conference in Structuring Itself in Accordance with 703.1 and 706.1 May Set Aside or Modify or Ignore the Mandatory Language Contained in 707, 715, 722, 726, 728, 729, 730, 731, 732, 733, 734, 735, 737, 738, 739, 740, 741, 742, 743, and 2512 of the 1988 Discipline
640.summary: The East Ohio Annual Conference asked whether they could ignore mandatory structural requirements in the Discipline while restructuring. The Judicial Council ruled that annual conferences must follow all mandatory provisions even when given flexibility to structure themselves.
640.keyHolding: Annual conferences may not set aside, modify, or ignore mandatory language in the Discipline even when given general authority to structure themselves for effective mission.
640.outcome: Annual conferences must comply with all mandatory structural provisions in the Discipline

641.title: Legality of Annual Conference Budget Which Includes Funding for Pension and Benefit Programs and General Church Apportionments in the Same Apportionment with Funding for Conference Administrative and Operating Programs
641.summary: The Yellowstone Annual Conference's budget combined different types of funds into three general sections rather than keeping pension, benefit, and general church funds separate as required by church law.
641.keyHolding: Annual conferences must provide separate identification and handling of pension and benefit funds, Equitable Salary Fund, and general church apportionments as required by the Discipline.
641.outcome: Conference budget plan declared illegal for failing to properly separate required funds

642.title: Petition Regarding Apparent Conflict in General Conference Actions Affecting Language in the Book of Worship
642.summary: The Judicial Council declined to resolve conflicting General Conference petitions about language in the Book of Worship, stating only General Conference has authority over worship language.
642.keyHolding: The Judicial Council cannot determine General Conference intent when conflicting petitions are adopted, and General Conference has sole authority over Book of Worship language.
642.parties: Committee on the Book of Worship
642.outcome: No jurisdiction - Council declined to resolve the conflict

643.title: Petition From the Eastern Pennsylvania Conference for a Declaratory Decision as to the Constitutionality of Paragraph 453.3(b) of the 1988 Discipline
643.summary: The Eastern Pennsylvania Conference asked if the administrative location process violates a minister's constitutional right to trial, and the Judicial Council ruled it does not.
643.keyHolding: The administrative location provisions in Paragraph 453.3(b) of the 1988 Discipline do not violate a minister's constitutional right to trial.
643.parties: Eastern Pennsylvania Conference and Rev. J. Westcoat Sandlin

644.title: Constitutionality of Annual Conference Rule Limiting Tenure of Conference Council on Ministries Clergy Staff but not of Lay Staff
644.summary: The North Carolina Annual Conference asked if they could set different tenure rules for clergy versus lay staff in their Conference Council on Ministries. The Judicial Council said yes, this is allowed under church law.
644.keyHolding: Annual conferences may establish different tenure limitations for clergy and lay staff employees in their Conference Council on Ministries structure under Par. 815(c).
644.outcome: Constitutional - different tenure rules for clergy and lay staff are allowed

645.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the 1989 Session of Florida Annual Conference Concerning Payment of 100% of World Service
645.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed a bishop's ruling that the Florida Annual Conference's policies regarding World Service apportionment payments were lawful and proper.
645.keyHolding: Conference policies regarding World Service apportionment payments that do not achieve 100% payment do not necessarily violate disciplinary provisions.
645.parties: Florida Annual Conference (review of bishop's decision)

646.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the Florida Annual Conference As To Legality of Conference Standing Rules Relating To Allocation of Certain Funds
646.summary: The Florida Annual Conference asked their bishop to rule on whether certain financial standing rules were legal under church law. The Judicial Council affirmed the bishop's decision that the rules complied with the Discipline.
646.keyHolding: Annual conference standing rules relating to financial procedures that comply with the Discipline are legally valid.
646.parties: Florida Annual Conference members questioning the legality of conference standing rules

647.title: Consolidated Petitions for a Declaratory Decision Concerning 709.6, 710.3(a), 710.3(b)(1), 710.3(b)(3), 710.3(d), 715.2(b) and Their Effect on an Annual Conference
647.summary: The Florida Annual Conference can authorize its Council on Finance and Administration to handle budget shortfalls and can use unused Conference Benevolences funds for a reserve fund rather than applying them to World Service.
647.keyHolding: Annual Conferences have authority to manage Conference Benevolences funds separately from World Service funds and may direct unused balances to conference reserve funds.
647.outcome: All four requests for declaratory decisions were granted, affirming the Annual Conference's authority over Conference Benevolences funds

648.title: Meaning, Application, and Effect of the Requirement in ¶456 that a Candidate for Readmission Must Serve at Least One Year as a Local Pastor
648.summary: A minister who has surrendered their credentials must serve at least one year as a local pastor before being readmitted to conference membership, with no exceptions or waivers allowed.
648.keyHolding: The one-year local pastor service requirement for readmission after surrendering ministerial office is mandatory with no disciplinary provision for waiver or alternative fulfillment.
648.outcome: Clarified mandatory nature of one-year local pastor service requirement

649.title: Constitutionality of ¶¶ 737.4(d) and (e) of the 1988 Discipline
649.summary: Annual conferences have the authority to reduce a pastor's pension if their church fails to pay required pension contributions.
649.keyHolding: Annual Conferences have constitutional and legislative authority to reduce a pastor's pension when proportional payment requirements under ¶ 737.4 are not met.
649.parties: College of Bishops of the Southeastern Jurisdiction and Kentucky Annual Conference Board of Pensions

650.title: Legality of Waiving Requirement of Service Under Appointment (¶ 424) Prior to Admission into Full Connection
650.summary: An annual conference cannot waive the requirement that clergy candidates serve two full years under appointment before ordination. The Judicial Council revoked an ordination that violated this rule.
650.keyHolding: The disciplinary requirements for ordination contained in ¶ 424 cannot be waived by an annual conference.
650.parties: Appeal from Louisville Annual Conference ordination decision
650.outcome: Bishop's ruling upheld; ordination revoked; person reverts to probationary membership

651.title: Ruling by Bishop Louis W. Schowengerdt on a Moot and Hypothetical Issue
651.summary: A retired elder asked the presiding bishop to rule on four legal questions, but the bishop correctly refused because the questions were moot and hypothetical rather than based on actual conference actions.
651.keyHolding: Bishops should not rule on moot and hypothetical questions but only on legal matters arising from actual actions taken or proposed by the conference.
651.parties: Hardin L. Adkins, III (retired elder) requesting ruling from Bishop Louis W. Schowengerdt
651.outcome: Bishop's ruling affirmed - properly refused to rule on moot and hypothetical questions

652.title: Interpretation of ¶ 437.2(c) of the 1988 Discipline and Question 69 in The Business of The Annual Conference
652.summary: The Judicial Council clarified that clergy members are limited to a total of eight years of less-than-full-time appointments throughout their entire career, not just eight consecutive years.
652.keyHolding: The eight-year limit for less-than-full-time clergy appointments applies to the overall total of years served in such appointments throughout one's entire clergy career, not just consecutive years.
652.outcome: Clarified that eight-year limit applies to total career years, not consecutive years

653.title: Review of Bishop's Decision Concerning Financial Policies as Related to the Iowa Conference Program of Church Extension and Revitalization
653.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed that the Iowa Annual Conference's plan for starting and supporting new churches was legal under Methodist law.
653.keyHolding: Annual conferences have constitutional authority to structure themselves for effective mission, including developing plans for church extension and revitalization that do not violate the Discipline.

654.title: Return of Credentials or Copies After Surrender of Ministerial Office
654.summary: A bishop ruled that ministers who surrender their credentials cannot get them back or receive copies, and the Judicial Council agreed with this decision.
654.keyHolding: Ministers who surrender their credentials under ¶452.3 are not entitled to receive the credentials or copies because the paragraph makes no provision for their return.
654.parties: Rocky Mountain Annual Conference and Bishop Roy I. Sano

655.title: Appeal of a Decision of the North Central Jurisdictional Court of Appeals Concerning Actions of a Trial Court in the Minnesota Annual Conference
655.summary: The Judicial Council upheld the conviction of a local pastor who was found guilty of sexual harassment and disobedience to church discipline.
655.keyHolding: An appellate court properly applies the two-question test under ¶2625.1(g) to determine whether evidence sustains charges and whether legal errors vitiate the verdict.
655.parties: Gordon Johnson (Local Pastor) v. Minnesota Annual Conference

656.title: Petition for Reconsideration of Decision No. 643
656.summary: The Judicial Council denied a petition requesting reconsideration of an earlier decision (No. 643).
656.keyHolding: The petition for reconsideration was denied without further explanation.

657.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law Concerning Legality of Withholding Portion of Outgoing Pastor's Salary to Pay Costs of Cleaning Parsonage
657.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed a bishop's decision that it is illegal to deduct parsonage cleaning costs from an outgoing pastor's final salary payment.
657.keyHolding: It is illegal to withhold cleaning costs from an outgoing pastor's salary payment to cover parsonage maintenance expenses.
657.outcome: Affirmed bishop's ruling that withholding cleaning costs is illegal

658.title: Eligibility of Part-Time Local Pastors and Student Local Pastors for Election as Lay Delegates to General and Jurisdictional Conferences
658.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that part-time and student local pastors cannot serve as lay delegates to General and Jurisdictional Conferences because they function as clergy, not laity.
658.keyHolding: Local pastors shall not be regarded as laity in Annual Conference relationships and therefore cannot serve as lay delegates.
658.outcome: Part-time and student local pastors ruled ineligible for election as lay delegates

659.title: Legality of Delegating to Districts the Authority to Determine and Apportion Salaries for District Superintendents
659.summary: The Virginia Conference asked if it could delegate authority to districts to set district superintendent salaries. The Judicial Council ruled this delegation was permissible under existing Discipline provisions.
659.keyHolding: Annual Conferences may delegate to districts the authority to determine district superintendent salaries when using conference-established guidelines, as permitted by the phrase 'unless otherwise provided' in ¶710.1(a).
659.outcome: Conference delegation of salary-setting authority to districts ruled consistent with Discipline

660.title: Par. 533.1 as it Relates to the Appointive Process in the Tennessee Conference
660.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that the Tennessee Conference's use of "preference inquiries" sent to pastors and Pastor-Parish Relations Committees is consistent with church law governing pastoral appointments.
660.keyHolding: Preference inquiries used in the appointive process are consultation tools that do not remove the bishop's final authority for making appointments and are consistent with ¶ 533.1 of the Discipline.
660.parties: Tennessee Annual Conference member requesting ruling on standing rules regarding appointive process
660.outcome: Affirmed - preference inquiries are consistent with disciplinary guidelines

661.title: Legality of the Formula and Method by which Ministerial Support Items are Apportioned in the Memphis Conference
661.summary: The Memphis Conference can legally apportion ministerial support items (pensions, equitable salary, district superintendent's fund, episcopal fund) as separate line items, but local churches cannot designate how their payments are distributed among these items.
661.keyHolding: Annual conferences may apportion ministerial support items as separate line items, but local church payments must be distributed proportionally as mandated by the Discipline.
661.outcome: Apportionment method declared legal; local church designation rights denied

662.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law Concerning Question of Conflict Between "New Mission Statement" and Established Standards of Doctrine
662.summary: The Virginia Conference requested a bishop's ruling on whether a proposed mission statement violated church doctrine, but the Judicial Council declined to review it because the bishop's response was an opinion, not a legal decision.
662.keyHolding: The Judicial Council only has authority to review actual decisions of law made during Annual Conference sessions, not episcopal opinions on proposed statements.

663.title: Legality of Certain Wisconsin Conference Budget Procedures
663.summary: The Wisconsin Annual Conference asked whether it was giving up its budget authority by treating Board of Global Ministries items as "line items" rather than informational items. The Judicial Council affirmed the bishop's ruling that the conference retained its proper budget authority.
663.keyHolding: An Annual Conference does not give up its reserved budgetary rights by properly categorizing budget items as operational line items when the budget process follows appropriate procedures through the Council on Finance and Administration.
663.parties: Jerry Eckert appearing at hearing regarding Wisconsin Annual Conference budget procedures

664.title: Restrictions in ¶ 2542 on Use of Proceeds from Mortgage or Sale of Church Property
664.summary: Churches cannot mortgage their buildings or use money from selling church property to pay for current expenses or emergency repairs. The Discipline requires a clear separation between operating funds and capital funds.
664.keyHolding: Paragraph 2542 strictly prohibits the use of mortgage proceeds or principal from property sales for current expenses, including emergency facility repairs.
664.parties: Eastern Pennsylvania Conference requesting ruling on behalf of Bickley Memorial United Methodist Church
664.outcome: Affirmed strict prohibition on using mortgage or sale proceeds for current expenses including emergency repairs

665.title: Par. 906.12 as it Relates to the Decision of the General Commission on Christian Unity and Interreligious Concerns to be a "Reconciling Commission"
665.summary: The Northwest Texas Annual Conference requested that funding be stopped to a commission that declared itself a "Reconciling Commission," but the Judicial Council found no evidence the commission was using funds to promote homosexuality in violation of church law.
665.keyHolding: A general agency declaring itself a "reconciling commission" does not automatically violate the prohibition against using United Methodist funds to promote homosexuality without evidence of actual misuse of funds.
665.parties: Northwest Texas Annual Conference and General Council on Finance and Administration
665.outcome: No evidence found of violation of funding restrictions

666.title: Legality of Selective Adjustments in Apportionments to Local Churches
666.summary: An Annual Conference cannot reduce the total amount of general fund apportionments it receives from the General Conference, but it can create formulas that allow individual churches facing financial hardship to have their apportionments adjusted through a review process.
666.keyHolding: Annual conferences must apportion the full amount of general funds received from the General Conference without reduction, but may develop apportionment formulas that include review procedures for adjusting individual church payments.
666.parties: Maine Conference questioner challenging Bishop F. Herbert Skeete's ruling on apportionment authority
666.outcome: Affirmed - Bishop's ruling upheld that conferences cannot reduce total apportionments but can adjust individual church payments through review processes

667.title: Legality of Administrative Board Action Concerning Designated Gifts
667.summary: A local church's Administrative Board can legally establish policies about what types of designated gifts the church will accept, including refusing gifts that require channeling funds to organizations not approved by the Board.
667.keyHolding: Administrative Boards have the authority to determine policy regarding the receiving of funds donated to or through the church.
667.parties: Lay member of First United Methodist Church, Morehead City, North Carolina challenging Administrative Board policy on designated gifts
667.outcome: Affirmed - Administrative Board's policy on designated gifts upheld as within their authority

668.title: Grievance Procedures in ¶ 453 as Applied to Local Pastors
668.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that local pastors are subject to the same grievance procedures as ordained ministers under church law.
668.keyHolding: The grievance procedures in ¶ 453 apply to local pastors as well as ordained clergy.
668.outcome: Declaratory decision that grievance procedures apply to local pastors

669.title: Petition from the Maine Annual Conference for a Determination as to the Validity of Actions by the General Board of Pensions
669.summary: Maine Annual Conference received wrong information from the pension board about costs, leading to an unexpectedly high bill. The Judicial Council said the parties must work it out themselves rather than go to secular courts.
669.keyHolding: Disputes between church agencies should be settled by the parties themselves rather than through secular courts, and the Judicial Council has jurisdiction to ensure such settlements occur.
669.outcome: Remanded to parties for settlement with retained jurisdiction

670.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the Virginia Conference Concerning Benevolence Funding for the Office of the Virginia United Methodist Foundation
670.summary: The Judicial Council deferred ruling on a bishop's decision about funding for the Virginia United Methodist Foundation, requesting more information before making a determination.
670.keyHolding: The Judicial Council deferred decision pending receipt of additional information necessary to make a proper ruling.

671.title: Whether 1988 General Conference Resolution Entitled "Pay Equity in the USA" Applies to All General Agencies
671.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that a General Conference resolution requiring pay equity monitoring applies to all general agencies, not just those specifically mentioned in a referenced disciplinary paragraph.
671.keyHolding: General Conference resolutions apply broadly to all general agencies unless specific exclusions are explicitly stated in the resolution text.
671.parties: General Council on Finance and Administration seeking clarification against General Board of Pensions and General Board of Publication
671.outcome: Resolution applies to all general agencies as requested by GCFA

672.title: Interpretation of Provision in the 1988 Discipline ¶ 710.3(c) that "[t]he Term 'Conference Benevolences' Shall Not Include Allocations and Expenditures for Other Conference Agencies and Officers Whose Work Is Primarily Administrative."
672.summary: The Virginia Annual Conference could fund their Foundation president's salary from conference benevolences because the position involved stewardship and promotional work, not just administrative duties.
672.keyHolding: Annual Conferences may use conference benevolences to fund foundation presidents whose work includes stewardship, promotion, and development beyond primarily administrative duties.
672.parties: Virginia Annual Conference (review of Bishop Thomas B. Stockton's episcopal decision)
672.outcome: Affirmed - bishop's ruling upheld that foundation president funding from conference benevolences was permissible

673.title: Legality of General Conference Instructions to the General Council on Finance and Administration to Prepare a Proposed Budget Within Specified Limits
673.summary: The General Conference cannot set dollar or percentage limits on budget recommendations from the General Council on Finance and Administration without first changing the Discipline through proper legislative procedures.
673.keyHolding: The General Council on Finance and Administration has plenary authority to set the amount and distribution of all funds in its budget recommendations, and the General Conference cannot impose caps without first amending the Discipline.
673.parties: Jerry Brewster (petitioner), Legislative Committee on Financial Administration, General Council on Finance and Administration
673.outcome: General Conference cannot legally impose budget limits on GCFA without changing the Discipline

674.title: Legality of Mandatory Participation in the Health Care Plan (UMCare)
674.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that General Conference has the authority to require certain clergy and lay employees to participate in the UMCare health insurance plan.
674.keyHolding: General Conference has constitutional authority under Paragraph 15 to mandate participation in health care plans as a distinctively connectional matter.
674.outcome: Constitutional - General Conference has authority to mandate health care plan participation

675.title: Appointive Power of Bishop in Relation to Consultation Process
675.summary: A bishop's authority to make pastoral appointments is not diminished by the required consultation process with committees, as consultation is advisory only.
675.keyHolding: The consultation process required in appointment-making does not conflict with or impair the bishop's ultimate authority to make and fix appointments.
675.outcome: Constitutional - no conflict exists between consultation requirements and episcopal appointment authority

676.title: Amenability of Ministers From Other Denominations Under Appointment in an Annual Conference
676.summary: Ministers from other denominations serving in UMC appointments must follow the same conduct standards and grievance procedures as United Methodist clergy, with the same due process protections.
676.keyHolding: Ministers from other denominations while serving under appointment in an Annual Conference are amenable to the same standards of character and conduct as United Methodist clergy and are subject to the procedures in Par. 453.
676.outcome: Declaratory decision that ministers from other denominations are subject to UMC grievance procedures and standards while under appointment

677.title: Review of Bishop's Decision Concerning Final Approval and Adoption of Sexual Harassment Policy by Task Force
677.summary: The Judicial Council reviewed a bishop's decision about whether an Annual Conference could delegate authority to finalize a sexual harassment policy to a task force. The Council ruled that while conferences can adopt such policies, they cannot delegate the authority to make final changes to task forces.
677.keyHolding: The Annual Conference has authority to adopt a sexual harassment policy but cannot delegate to a task force the right to make changes in that policy, as changes will not be binding until adopted by the Annual Conference itself.
677.parties: Southern New Jersey Annual Conference and Northern New Jersey Conference Task Force
677.outcome: Modified - Conference can adopt policy but cannot delegate final authority to task force

678.title: Authority of Annual Conference to Approve a Candidate Who Has Not Met the Requirements
678.summary: An Annual Conference cannot approve someone as a full-time local pastor if they previously withdrew under charges and lack the required cabinet recommendation for readmission.
678.keyHolding: Cabinet recommendation is required for reinstatement as a ministerial member of an Annual Conference when a candidate has previously withdrawn under charges, and a motion to approve a candidate lacking this requirement is out of order.
678.parties: Western Pennsylvania Conference appealing Bishop George W. Bashore's ruling regarding Chandler D. Wolf
678.outcome: Bishop's ruling affirmed - motion was properly ruled out of order

679.title: Review of Bishop's Ruling in the California-Pacific Conference as to Validity of Proposed Resolution Entitled "Long Term Commitments" in Light of Disciplinary Provisions Regarding Homosexuality
679.summary: The Judicial Council declined to review Bishop Tuell's ruling on a resolution about long-term commitments because it was not a formal decision of law.
679.keyHolding: The Judicial Council lacks jurisdiction to review rulings that are not formal decisions of law.

680.title: Petition for a Judgment on the Legality of Structure Adopted by the North Indiana Conference
680.summary: The North Indiana Conference adopted a new structure that failed to provide for mandatory boards and agencies required by the Discipline. The Judicial Council ruled that while conferences can restructure for effective mission, they cannot ignore mandatory organizational requirements.
680.keyHolding: Annual Conferences must provide for all mandatory boards and agencies specified in the Discipline even when restructuring for effective mission.
680.parties: North Indiana Conference (requesting declaratory decision on their new conference structure)
680.outcome: Conference structure ruled invalid for failing to provide mandatory boards and agencies required by Discipline

681.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the Alabama-West Florida Conference Concerning Custody and Management of Funds Given and Designated for a Specific Conference Agency
681.summary: The Judicial Council reviewed whether conference trustees must follow a 1988 resolution requiring discretionary endowment funds be placed with the United Methodist Foundation when managing estate funds specifically designated for the United Methodist Children's Home. The Council affirmed that trustees have discretion in managing these designated funds and are not mandated to use the Foundation.
681.keyHolding: Conference trustees have discretionary authority over estate funds specifically designated for a particular beneficiary and are not mandated by annual conference resolutions to place such non-discretionary funds with the United Methodist Foundation.
681.parties: Alabama-West Florida Annual Conference Board of Trustees
681.outcome: Affirmed with clarification that trustees have discretion over designated funds

682.title: Various Petitions for Reconsideration of Judicial Council Decision No. 674 and for a Declaratory Decision as to the Legality and Constitutionality of General Conference UMCare Legislation
682.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that the UMCare health plan was unconstitutional because General Conference cannot delegate its legislative authority to the General Board of Pensions to make fundamental decisions about benefits and program structure.
682.keyHolding: General Conference cannot constitutionally delegate its exclusive legislative authority over health care plans to other church bodies.
682.parties: Various Annual Conferences petitioning for reconsideration; Charles Lippse (Holston Conference), David Hardesty Jr. (West Virginia Conference), Renard J. Kolasa (Detroit Conference), and others
682.outcome: UMCare legislation declared unconstitutional due to unauthorized delegation of legislative authority

683.title: Consistency of Support of Religious Coalition for Abortion Rights with Par. 71(g) of the 1988 Discipline
683.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that UMC general boards' membership in the Religious Coalition for Abortion Rights was consistent with the church's Social Principles on abortion.
683.keyHolding: General boards and agencies may support organizations whose positions align with the Social Principles even if those organizations advocate for broader positions than the church officially holds.
683.parties: General Conference referral regarding General Board of Church and Society and Women's Division of General Board of Global Ministries
683.outcome: Constitutional - support of RCAR is consistent with Social Principles

684.title: Legality and Constitutionality of Provision in Calendar Item 1325 (1992 General Conference) that All Clergy Members of an Annual Conference Shall be Included with Voice in the Clergy Session
684.summary: The Austrian Provisional Conference requested a ruling on whether a 1992 General Conference provision requiring all clergy members to have voice in clergy sessions was legal and constitutional. The Judicial Council deferred consideration to their April 1993 meeting.
684.keyHolding: The Judicial Council deferred consideration of the constitutional questions regarding clergy session participation requirements.

685.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the Northern Illinois Conference Concerning Disposition of a Complaint Against a Clergy Member
685.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed a bishop's decision that a clergy complaint was properly referred to the Joint Review Committee instead of the Committee on Investigation.
685.keyHolding: District superintendents have discretion to determine whether a clergy complaint should be referred to the Joint Review Committee or Committee on Investigation based on the nature of the complaint and surrounding circumstances.

686.title: Constitutionality, Meaning, Application and Effect of Par. 705.6 of the 1992 Discipline in Relation to Par. 422 and as Regards the Inclusion of All Clergy Members in Clergy Session
686.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that the 1992 General Conference's decision to include all clergy members (not just those in full connection) in clergy sessions is constitutional and valid.
686.keyHolding: General Conference has the authority to define the composition of clergy sessions, and Par. 705.6's inclusion of all clergy members is constitutional.
686.parties: General Conference (via motion), North Georgia Conference, Austrian Provisional Conference
686.outcome: Constitutional - Par. 705.6 is valid and executive sessions must follow its provisions

687.title: Constitutionality, Meaning, Application and Effect of the Formula in Par. 602 for Representation to the General and Jurisdictional Conferences
687.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that the current formula for determining how many delegates each annual conference sends to General and Jurisdictional Conferences is constitutional and legal.
687.keyHolding: Paragraph 602 of the 1992 Discipline governing delegate representation to General and Jurisdictional Conferences is constitutional as the General Conference has authority to fix the ratio of Annual Conference representation.
687.outcome: Constitutional - upheld the constitutionality and legality of the current delegate representation formula

688.title: Meaning, Application, and Effect of Paragraphs 703.1, 2503, 2542, and 2548 of the 1988 Discipline With Regard to Restrictions on Use of Funds for Church Property
688.summary: The California-Pacific Annual Conference asked for clarification about restrictions on using proceeds from the sale of church property, particularly when churches are discontinued, abandoned, or merged.
688.keyHolding: Church properties that have been abandoned or discontinued shall be administered and disposed of under the authority of the Annual Conference through the Conference Board of Trustees.
688.outcome: Declaratory decision providing guidance on property restrictions and annual conference authority over discontinued church property

689.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the Iowa Conference Interpreting Pars. 448.1 and 448.3 of the 1988 Discipline with regard to Continuing Clergy Member on Leave of Absence
689.summary: The Judicial Council found that a bishop's decisions regarding a clergy member's leave of absence lacked proper due process and were not responsive to the questions asked, remanding the matter back to the Iowa Annual Conference.
689.keyHolding: Due process must be followed in clergy leave of absence proceedings, and bishops' decisions of law must be responsive to the specific questions presented.
689.parties: Concerned Clergy and Iowa Annual Conference regarding W. Michael Biklen
689.outcome: Remanded - Bishop's decisions not affirmed, matter remanded to Iowa Annual Conference to begin procedure over

690.title: Right of Clergy Session to Vote on all Clergy Matters Regardless of Board of Ordained Ministry Recommendation
690.summary: The clergy session can consider and vote on all clergy matters, whether or not the Board of Ordained Ministry recommends them, but must still follow all Discipline requirements.
690.keyHolding: The clergy session is not limited to those matters brought before it by the Board of Ordained Ministry and may consider all clergy business matters, with or without Board recommendation, provided all disciplinary requirements are met.
690.outcome: Clergy session authority affirmed with disciplinary compliance requirement

691.title: Interpretation of Paragraphs 453.5, 454.1(a), 454.1(f), 2622.2, 2622.6 and 2625.1(b) and Their Effect on Grievance Procedures
691.summary: The Judicial Council clarified multiple procedural aspects of clergy discipline and grievances, including that clergy withdrawal is immediately effective, mediators must be neutral and trained, and clergy who withdraw forfeit trial rights.
691.keyHolding: Clergy withdrawal from conference membership is effective immediately upon notification, not upon later conference confirmation.
691.outcome: Declaratory decision answering six questions about clergy withdrawal, mediation requirements, trial rights, due process protections, and statute of limitations

692.title: Constitutionality, Meaning, Application, and Effect of the Action of the 1992 General Conference in Adopting Calendar Item No. 671, Providing that the Bishop of The Methodist Church in Puerto Rico Will Sit With Voice but No Vote in the United Methodist Council of Bishops
692.summary: The General Conference has authority to allow the bishop of the Affiliated Autonomous Methodist Church of Puerto Rico to participate in the UMC Council of Bishops with voice but no vote as an interim measure for mission coordination.
692.keyHolding: The General Conference has constitutional authority to decide all connectional matters affecting work both within and without the United States, including allowing a bishop from an affiliated autonomous church to participate in the Council of Bishops without voting rights.
692.parties: Not specified - appears to be a declaratory decision regarding General Conference action
692.outcome: Constitutional - General Conference has authority to provide for Puerto Rican bishop's participation in Council of Bishops

693.title: Constitutionality of Par. 282 of the 1992 Discipline Providing for the Licensing and Appointment of Lay Preachers
693.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that a new provision allowing district superintendents to appoint "lay preachers" violated the Constitution because only bishops have the authority to make appointments.
693.keyHolding: District superintendents cannot be given appointive authority over clergy as this power is constitutionally reserved to bishops under the general superintendency.

694.title: Annual Conference Actions Concerning Covenant Services and Celebrations in Local Churches of Relationships of Couples Outside the Civil and Religious Rite of Marriage
694.summary: Two annual conferences attempted to authorize clergy to perform covenant services for same-sex couples, but the Judicial Council ruled that conferences cannot create or alter official church rites and rituals.
694.keyHolding: Annual Conferences do not have authority to establish or alter the official rites and rituals of The United Methodist Church.
694.parties: Minnesota Annual Conference and Troy Annual Conference; Reconciling Congregations represented by Laurits Nielsen and Judith Westendorf
694.outcome: Conferences ruled to have no authority to authorize covenant services for same-sex couples

695.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the Florida Conference Concerning Administrative Location Procedures
695.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that the Florida Conference failed to follow proper procedures when placing a pastor on administrative location, requiring fair process and timely hearings before such action can be taken.
695.keyHolding: Administrative location proceedings must follow fair process requirements and provide timely hearings as required by paragraphs 454 and 2622 of the Book of Discipline.
695.outcome: Bishop's decision not affirmed; pastor not legally on administrative location

696.title: The Legality of Holding Membership in Two Denominations Simultaneously
696.summary: A United Methodist minister cannot hold membership in both The United Methodist Church and another denomination simultaneously. When someone joins another church, their UMC membership automatically ends.
696.keyHolding: Joining another denomination constitutes voluntary withdrawal from The United Methodist Church and thereby terminates membership, regardless of whether one is lay or clergy.
696.parties: North Texas Annual Conference regarding William Farmer's dual membership status
