808.outcome: Bishop's decision of law affirmed - annual conference may eliminate honoraria for clergy in conference positions

809.title: Review of Rewritten Clergy Sexual Ethics Policy of the West Ohio Annual Conference
809.summary: The West Ohio Annual Conference revised its clergy sexual ethics policy to comply with church law requiring clergy to maintain confidentiality, including confessional confidences. The bishop's approval of these changes was affirmed.
809.keyHolding: Annual conference policies must comply with Discipline requirements regarding clergy confidentiality, including the absolute protection of confessional confidences.
809.outcome: The bishop's ruling affirming the amended policy was affirmed

810.title: Review of Decision of Law of Bishop Donald A. Ott Relating to Fair Process and Surrender of Ministerial Credentials
810.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed a bishop's ruling that hypothetical questions about fair process violations in a minister's credential surrender cannot be answered through questions of law.
810.keyHolding: Questions of law must relate to specific actions taken by the conference session and cannot be presented in hypothetical form to resolve past procedural issues.
810.parties: Rev. Bobby Dale Whitlock asking questions regarding Merritt Bongard's credential surrender
810.outcome: Affirmed - questions ruled moot and/or improper as hypothetical

811.title: Request from the Minnesota Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision on a Series of Questions Regarding the New Membership Provisions of the 1996 Discipline
811.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that 1996 General Conference legislation creating new 'baptized membership' and 'professing membership' categories was unconstitutional, reverting membership practices back to the 1992 Discipline provisions.
811.keyHolding: The 1996 membership legislation adopted by General Conference based on the Baptismal Study Committee report is unconstitutional and invalid, requiring continuation of the 1992 membership provisions.
811.outcome: 1996 membership legislation declared unconstitutional; 1992 membership provisions remain in effect

812.title: Review of Sexual Ethics Policy and Procedures of the North Georgia Annual Conference
812.summary: The North Georgia Conference's sexual ethics policy was found to violate the Discipline and previous Judicial Council decisions, particularly regarding clergy confidentiality requirements. The policy must be revised before it can take effect.
812.keyHolding: Annual conference sexual ethics policies must comply with Disciplinary requirements regarding clergy confidentiality and cannot expand chargeable offenses beyond those defined in the Discipline.
812.outcome: Remanded for revision to conform with Discipline and Judicial Council decisions before resubmission

813.title: Review of Decision of Law of Bishop Neil L. Irons Relating to the Actions of the Central Pennsylvania Annual Conference in Defeating an Amendment to the Connectional Ministries Budget
813.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed a bishop's ruling about proper budget placement of conference programs, determining that some items belong in the Benevolence Budget while others should remain in the Connectional Ministries Budget.
813.keyHolding: Conference benevolences must include only those allocations directly associated with program, mission, and benevolent causes of annual conference program agencies, not primarily administrative expenses.
813.parties: Central Pennsylvania Annual Conference clergy member challenging budget item placement
813.outcome: Affirmed - bishop's ruling upheld with specific items properly categorized between Benevolence and Connectional Ministries budgets

814.title: Review of a Decision of Law of Bishop Robert E. Fannin Concerning the North Alabama Annual Conference's "Policy Statement and Procedures on Misconduct of a Sexual Nature"
814.summary: The Judicial Council reversed a bishop's ruling that approved North Alabama's sexual misconduct policy, requiring the conference to revise the policy to comply with church law before it can take effect.
814.keyHolding: Annual conference policies on sexual misconduct must comply with established Discipline procedures and cannot expand chargeable offenses or violate fair process requirements.
814.parties: North Alabama Annual Conference member questioning the adopted policy

815.title: Request from the General Board of Discipleship for a Declaratory Decision on the Meaning of the Phrase "Or Other Equivalent Structure" in Par. 630 of the 1996 Discipline
815.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that Annual Conferences must have a board of laity or equivalent structure that performs the required functions - they cannot simply eliminate this mandatory board from their structure.
815.keyHolding: Annual Conferences cannot eliminate the board of laity function but may use alternative structures that are truly equivalent and perform all the same mandatory duties.
815.parties: General Board of Discipleship requested declaratory decision at petition of National Association of Annual Conference Lay Leaders
815.outcome: Declaratory decision issued clarifying that board of laity or equivalent structure is mandatory, not optional

816.title: Review of Decisions of Law of Bishop Hae-Jong Kim in the North Central New York Annual Conference Related to Withdrawal of a Clergy Member Under Complaint
816.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that all actions by the North Central New York Conference regarding a clergy member's withdrawal under complaint were null and void due to unclear facts and improper procedure. The matter was sent back to the Committee on Investigation for proper disciplinary proceedings.
816.keyHolding: When proper disciplinary procedures are not followed in clergy withdrawal under complaint cases, all related conference actions are null and void and the matter must be remanded for proper proceedings.
816.parties: North Central New York Annual Conference members questioning Bishop Hae-Jong Kim's decisions of law
816.outcome: All conference actions declared null and void; matter remanded to Committee on Investigation for proper disciplinary process

817.title: Review of Decision of Law of Bishop Joe A. Wilson in the Central Texas Annual Conference Relating to Fair Process in Surrender of Clergy Credentials
817.summary: The Judicial Council declined to rule on whether fair process was denied to a clergy member who surrendered credentials under threat of judicial process, requesting more evidence from all parties.
817.keyHolding: The Judicial Council will not render decisions on fair process matters without complete evidence and documentation from all parties involved.
817.parties: An elder in the Central Texas Annual Conference questioning Bishop Joe A. Wilson's decision regarding Charles Rice's surrender of credentials
817.outcome: No decision rendered; more evidence requested from bishop, Conference Board of Ordained Ministry, and respondent

818.title: Review of Decision of Law of Bishop Kenneth L. Carder in the Memphis Annual Conference on the Legality of the Conference Practice Imposing a Cap on the Percentage of Change of Apportionments to the Local Church Which May Result in Less than 100% of the Conference Budget Being Apportioned to the Churches of the Conference
818.summary: The Memphis Annual Conference's practice of capping year-to-year apportionment increases to individual churches was ruled illegal when it resulted in less than 100% of required budgets being apportioned. The bishop's ruling against this practice was affirmed.
818.keyHolding: Annual conferences cannot use apportionment caps that reduce General Conference apportionments below required amounts or prevent full apportionment of the conference budget among local churches.
818.parties: Clergy member requesting ruling on Memphis Annual Conference apportionment method
818.outcome: Affirmed - caps are illegal when they reduce required apportionments

819.title: Request from Alaska Missionary Conference for a Declaratory Decision on Qualifications for Lay Members of Annual Conference
819.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that General Conference cannot add qualifications beyond those in the Constitution for lay members of Annual Conference, declaring unconstitutional the requirement that members be from the specific local church for two years.
819.keyHolding: The General Conference cannot add to or modify constitutional qualifications for lay members of Annual Conference through legislative action rather than constitutional amendment.
819.outcome: Unconstitutional - General Conference cannot add qualifications beyond those in Constitution

820.title: Review of Decision of Law of Bishop Joe A. Wilson in the Central Texas Conference Relating to Fair Process in Surrender of Clergy Credentials
820.summary: A bishop correctly ruled that he was not required to answer hypothetical questions about fair process in a clergy member's surrender of credentials. The Judicial Council affirmed that bishops need not respond to hypothetical scenarios.
820.keyHolding: Bishops are not required to answer hypothetical questions posed as requests for decisions of law.
820.parties: Member of Central Texas Annual Conference requesting episcopal ruling

821.title: Review of Decision of Law of Bishop S. Clifton Ives in the West Virginia Annual Conference on a Resolution on Partial-Birth Abortion
821.summary: The Judicial Council reversed a bishop's ruling that allowed an annual conference resolution condemning partial-birth abortion, finding the resolution failed to account for the mother's life and well-being as required by church doctrine.
821.keyHolding: A conference resolution that condemns a specific medical procedure without considering the mother's life and well-being violates the church's balanced position on abortion as stated in ¶ 65(J).
821.parties: Lay member of West Virginia Annual Conference requesting review of Bishop S. Clifton Ives' decision of law

822.title: Request from the North Carolina Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision on Past Service Liability for Pastor's Pensions and Apportionments
822.summary: The North Carolina Annual Conference can create a separate apportionment for past service pension liability and determine how to fund it. However, no budget items can be designated as "prior claims" that get paid before other items in the same category.
822.keyHolding: Annual Conferences have constitutional authority to establish separate apportionments for pension funding, but cannot designate certain budget items as having priority over others in the same funding category.
822.parties: North Carolina Annual Conference (requesting party), William W. Sherman, Jr. (retired clergy member who made the motion)
822.outcome: Annual Conference has authority to create separate pension apportionment but cannot establish priority claims within funding categories

823.title: Review of Decision of Law by Bishop Marion Edwards in the North Carolina Annual Conference on the Authority of the North Carolina Annual Conference to Require a Master of Divinity Degree for Membership in Full Connection and Elder's Orders
823.summary: The North Carolina Annual Conference cannot require all clergy to have a Master of Divinity degree because this eliminates alternative education paths that General Conference has provided for local pastors seeking full connection.
823.keyHolding: An Annual Conference cannot establish requirements that negate or eliminate educational standards and pathways established by General Conference for ordination and full connection.
823.parties: A full-time local pastor in the North Carolina Annual Conference
823.outcome: Bishop's ruling not affirmed - Annual Conference policy declared unconstitutional

824.title: Request for a Declaratory Decision by the California-Pacific Annual Conference to Determine If the Clergy Sexual Ethics Policy Adopted by That Conference in Response to Decision 803 Is in Accordance with the 1996 Discipline and Judicial Council Decision 736
824.summary: The Judicial Council approved California-Pacific Annual Conference's revised clergy sexual ethics policy after requiring specific editorial changes and deletion of one section to ensure compliance with the Discipline.
824.keyHolding: Annual conferences may adopt clergy sexual ethics policies but must comply exactly with Discipline procedures and paragraph numbering without paraphrasing or modifying disciplinary requirements.

825.title: Request from the Norway Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision on Whether an Annual Conference May Meet Every Other Year Rather than Annually
825.summary: The Norway Annual Conference asked if it could meet every other year instead of annually. The Judicial Council ruled that Annual Conferences must meet annually and cannot change their meeting frequency without specific enabling legislation.
825.keyHolding: Annual Conferences must meet annually and have no authority to meet less frequently without specific enabling legislation from General Conference.
825.outcome: Request denied - no authority to meet less than annually

826.title: Appeal From New England Conference Person on Trial and Appeal Procedures
826.summary: A clergy member's appeal was rejected because notice was filed 31 days after the trial ended, missing the required 30-day deadline by one day.
826.keyHolding: The thirty-day deadline for filing notice of appeal after a church trial is absolute and cannot be waived or extended.
826.parties: Rev. Joyce Sheehan (appellant), represented by Sven D. Wiberg
826.outcome: No Jurisdiction - appeal dismissed as untimely

827.title: Request from the Kansas West Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision as to the Constitutionality of the Conference Structure Adopted by the Kansas West Annual Conference at its 1997 Annual Conference Session
827.summary: The Kansas West Annual Conference adopted a new streamlined conference structure, but the Judicial Council ruled it unconstitutional because it violated several requirements including connectional relationships, personnel oversight, and separation of powers.
827.keyHolding: An Annual Conference cannot adopt a restructuring plan that conflicts with General Conference requirements regarding connectional systems, personnel supervision, delegation of legislative authority, and separation of program and financial functions.
827.outcome: Unconstitutional - new structure declared invalid and void

828.title: Request from the General Council on Finance and Administration for Declaratory Decision on the Meaning of the Phrase "Any Official United Methodist Agency" in ¶ 807.5 of the 1996 Discipline in the Context of Who May Use the Official United Methodist Insigne
828.summary: The Judicial Council clarified who can use the official United Methodist Cross and Flame symbol, ruling that only official agencies as defined in the Book of Discipline may use it.
828.keyHolding: The phrase "any official United Methodist agency" in ¶ 807.5 means any organization defined as an agency under ¶¶ 701.1 and 701.2 of the Discipline.
828.parties: General Council on Finance and Administration
828.outcome: Ruled that official United Methodist agencies are limited to those defined under ¶¶ 701.1 and 701.2

829.title: Review of Decision of Law of Bishop Hae Jong Kim in the North Central New York Annual Conference Related to Withdrawal of a Clergy Member Under Complaint
829.summary: When a clergy member under complaint withdraws from The United Methodist Church to join another denomination, they forfeit their right to any further proceedings or appeals within the UMC.
829.keyHolding: Withdrawal from The United Methodist Church forfeits all rights to appeals and proceedings, and bishops cannot render decisions of law regarding former members who have withdrawn.
829.parties: Appeal of Bishop Hae Jong Kim's decision regarding a withdrawn clergy member

830.title: Review of Decisions of Law of Bishop Joel Martinez Relating to Discontinuance of a Probationary Member by Nebraska Annual Conference
830.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed a bishop's refusal to answer questions about administrative procedures in discontinuing a probationary clergy member, ruling that bishops cannot make substantive rulings on administrative actions.
830.keyHolding: Bishops have no authority to make substantive rulings on judicial or administrative actions by properly constituted church bodies.
830.parties: Review of Bishop Joel Martinez's decisions of law regarding Nebraska Annual Conference's discontinuance of Rev. Kenneth A. McQueen, Jr.
830.outcome: Affirmed - Bishop's rulings that administrative questions are not proper questions of law were correct; fair process was followed

831.title: Review of Decision of Law by Bishop C. Joseph Sprague on the Legality of the Interim Plan of Mission and Ministry Adopted by the Northern Illinois Conference in Special Session on November 15, 1997
831.summary: The Judicial Council reversed a bishop's ruling and declared the Northern Illinois Annual Conference's restructuring plan null and void, finding that annual conferences cannot restructure without General Conference authorization.
831.keyHolding: Annual Conferences cannot adopt restructuring plans that usurp General Conference authority over connectional matters or improperly delegate conference authority to committees without General Conference enabling legislation.
831.parties: Northern Illinois Annual Conference member questioning the legality of the restructuring plan
831.outcome: Reversed - restructuring plan declared null and void

832.title: Petition for Reconsideration of Decision 810
832.summary: The Judicial Council denied a request to reconsider its previous Decision 810.
832.keyHolding: The Judicial Council declined to reconsider Decision 810.

833.title: In Re: Ceremonies That Celebrate Homosexual Unions - Chargeable Offense Determination
833.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that the prohibition against conducting ceremonies celebrating homosexual unions in ¶ 65.C constitutes church law that governs clergy conduct, even though it appears in the Social Principles section. Violating this prohibition is a chargeable offense under church law.
833.keyHolding: The prohibition in ¶ 65.C against ceremonies celebrating homosexual unions has the effect of church law and violations constitute chargeable offenses under ¶ 2624.
833.parties: College of Bishops of the South Central Jurisdiction, Illinois Great Rivers Annual Conference, North Alabama Annual Conference, Nebraska Annual Conference
833.outcome: The prohibition against homosexual union ceremonies constitutes enforceable church law and violations are chargeable offenses

834.title: Request from Wisconsin Annual Conference on the Ruling of Bishop Sharon Zimmerman Rader on Whether the Annual Conference May Consider Enactment of a Resolution Prohibiting Homosexual Unions Which Would Have the Effect of Adding to the Discipline
834.summary: The Wisconsin Annual Conference asked the Judicial Council to review a bishop's ruling that blocked consideration of a resolution prohibiting clergy from performing same-sex unions. The Judicial Council found it had no jurisdiction because the bishop made only a parliamentary ruling, not a legal decision.
834.keyHolding: The Judicial Council does not have jurisdiction to review parliamentary rulings that are not decisions of law.

835.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the Louisiana Annual Conference on the Structure of the Annual Conference. Request from the Holston Annual Conference on the Constitutionality of the "Design for Ministry" Restructure Plan
835.summary: The Judicial Council found that both Louisiana and Holston Annual Conferences had proposed restructure plans that failed to meet constitutional and disciplinary requirements for maintaining connectional relationships with general agencies.
835.keyHolding: Annual conferences must maintain connectional relationships with general agencies when restructuring their organization, and structure plans that are vague or eliminate required connections are unconstitutional.
835.parties: Louisiana Annual Conference (Dr. Nancy M. Carruth requesting bishop's decision); Holston Annual Conference
835.outcome: Both conference structure plans were found unconstitutional and remanded for revision

836.title: IN RE: Request From the Minnesota Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision on Whether ¶¶ 358.1b, 2623, and 2626.1 of the 1996 Discipline Violate the Constitution When They Define Judicial Process as Beginning Only with the Referral of a Complaint to the Committee on Investigation
836.summary: The Minnesota Annual Conference asked whether certain disciplinary procedures violated constitutional rights by limiting fair process protections to formal judicial proceedings. The Judicial Council ruled that the supervisory process does not violate constitutional due process rights.
836.keyHolding: The General Conference has constitutional authority to establish both supervisory and judicial processes, and the supervisory process does not deny constitutional rights of fair process or trial.
836.outcome: Constitutional - supervisory process provisions upheld as not violating constitutional due process requirements

837.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the North Texas Annual Conference on the Legality of the Definition of "Self-Avowed Practicing Homosexual" Passed by a Clergy Session, During a Special Session of the North Texas Annual Conference
837.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed a bishop's ruling that a definition of "self-avowed practicing homosexual" must specify to whom the acknowledgment is made, not just what behaviors are included.
837.keyHolding: An adequate definition of "self-avowed practicing homosexual" must identify the persons or groups to whom the self-acknowledgment must be made.
837.parties: North Texas Annual Conference clergy session and Bishop William B. Oden

838.title: Review of the Rewritten Sexual Ethics and Procedure Policy of the North Georgia Annual Conference
838.summary: The Judicial Council reviewed the revised North Georgia Conference policy on sexual misconduct by church professionals and found it compliant with church law after previous corrections were made.
838.keyHolding: The rewritten North Georgia Policy on Sexual Misconduct by Church Professionals conforms to the Discipline and Decision 812 after addressing previously identified deficiencies.
838.outcome: Policy found to be in conformity with Discipline and Decision 812

839.title: Review of Minnesota Annual Conference Sexual Misconduct Policy; Review of the Policy on Sexual Ethics of the Kansas East Annual Conference; Request from the East Ohio Conference for a Declaratory Decision on the Constitutionality of the Sexual Ethics Policy; Review of the Rewritten Sexual Harassment and Misconduct Policy of the North Alabama Annual Conference
839.summary: The Judicial Council found that sexual ethics and misconduct policies from four annual conferences contained constitutional violations and disciplinary deficiencies. All four policies were declared void and remanded for revision.
839.keyHolding: Annual Conference sexual ethics and misconduct policies must comply with the Discipline and may cite but not summarize, paraphrase, or modify disciplinary paragraphs.
839.parties: Minnesota Annual Conference, Kansas East Annual Conference, East Ohio Annual Conference, North Alabama Annual Conference
839.outcome: Remanded - all four policies declared void and remanded for revision

840.title: Request From the East Ohio Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision on the Constitutionality of the Racial Harassment Policy Adopted by the Conference
840.summary: The East Ohio Annual Conference asked if their newly adopted Racial Harassment Policy was constitutional, and the Judicial Council ruled that it was permissible under church law.
840.keyHolding: Annual conferences may adopt racial harassment policies that do not conflict with the Discipline, though definitions not provided for in the Discipline may confuse rather than clarify matters.

841.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the Florida Annual Conference Related to the Requirement That Candidates Must Have Completed One Fourth of Seminary Before January 1, 1997, to Qualify for Conference Relationship
841.summary: The Judicial Council rejected a request to review a bishop's decision because the request was not properly submitted during an annual conference session as required by church law.
841.keyHolding: Bishops' decisions of law can only be reviewed if the original question was properly presented in writing during the regular business of an Annual Conference session.

842.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the Virginia Annual Conference on the Legality of Adding to the Qualifications for Lay Members of General Conference as Outlined in ¶ 34 of the 1996 Discipline
842.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that annual conferences cannot require a $25 fee for delegate nominations, even if paid by districts or agencies, because it adds impermissible qualifications beyond what the Discipline allows.
842.keyHolding: Annual conferences may not add any requirements, including fees regardless of who pays them, beyond the qualifications for General and Jurisdictional Conference delegates specified in ¶ 34 of the Discipline.
842.parties: Rev. James Hundley requesting ruling from Bishop Joe E. Pennell, Jr. in Virginia Annual Conference
842.outcome: Partially Affirmed - fee requirement unconstitutional regardless of payment source

843.title: Request From the General Board of Discipleship on Whether Under ¶ 508 of the 1996 Discipline Enabling Legislation May Be Enacted by a General Conference to Become Effective After the Ratification of a Constitutional Amendment Proposed by the Same General Conference
843.summary: The General Board of Discipleship asked if they could pass enabling legislation for baptism changes before the Constitutional amendment was ratified by Annual Conferences. The Judicial Council said no - the amendment must be ratified first.
843.keyHolding: Enabling legislation cannot be passed by the General Conference until after Constitutional amendments are ratified by Annual Conferences and announced by the Council of Bishops.
843.outcome: Constitutional amendment ratification must precede enabling legislation

844.title: Appeal of Bishop's Decision of Law in the Northern Illinois Annual Conference Relating to the Applicability of ¶ 304.5 of the 1996 Discipline to Diaconal Ministers Making Transition to Permanent Deacons
844.summary: The Council ruled that diaconal ministers seeking ordination as deacons must meet all the same qualification requirements as other ordination candidates, including the prohibition against ordaining self-avowed practicing homosexuals.
844.keyHolding: Paragraph 304 of the Discipline establishing minimum requirements for ordination applies to all candidates for ordained ministry, including consecrated diaconal ministers seeking ordination as deacons.
844.parties: Clergy session of the Northern Illinois Annual Conference
844.outcome: Bishop Joseph C. Sprague's ruling affirmed - ¶304 applies to diaconal ministers seeking ordination as deacons

845.title: In Re: Constitutionality of Prohibition on Ceremonies Celebrating Homosexual Unions
845.summary: Two annual conferences challenged the constitutionality of the 1996 General Conference prohibition on same-sex union ceremonies. The Judicial Council ruled the prohibition is constitutional and does not violate inclusivity provisions.
845.keyHolding: The prohibition on ceremonies celebrating homosexual unions does not violate the constitutional provisions regarding inclusiveness because it does not prevent attendance, participation, or membership in the church.
845.parties: Oregon-Idaho Annual Conference and California-Nevada Annual Conference
845.outcome: Constitutional - prohibition upheld as not violating inclusivity provisions

846.title: Review of Bishop's Decisions of Law in the South Carolina Annual Conference Concerning Matters Related to the Process of Investigation of a Complaint Against a Clergy Member
846.summary: A South Carolina pastor accused of embezzling funds was placed on involuntary leave of absence. When church complaints were dismissed, the bishop made several legal rulings about the disciplinary process.
846.keyHolding: Bishops may rule requests for legal decisions as moot and hypothetical, and are only required to state when questions are improperly posed rather than provide substantive responses.
846.parties: South Carolina Annual Conference clergy member and Bishop J. Lawrence McCleskey
846.outcome: Bishop's decisions affirmed with clarifications about proper responses to improper questions

847.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the Northwest Texas Annual Conference Related to a Resolution Adopted by the Conference Entitled 'A Call to Doctrinal Integrity'
847.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that annual conferences cannot label themselves as unofficial movements like 'Confessing Conference' or 'Reconciling Conference' because it's divisive and conflicts with church doctrine.
847.keyHolding: Annual conferences may not identify themselves with unofficial organizations or movements as such labeling is divisive and subjects official church bodies to potential conflict with the Discipline and doctrines.
847.outcome: Bishop's ruling not affirmed; previous decisions 794 and 665 reversed regarding conference labeling

848.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the Norway Annual Conference on the Legality of the Annual Conference Structure and Related Matters
848.summary: The Judicial Council reviewed Bishop Vaxby's ruling on Norway Annual Conference's restructuring and elimination of certain boards, finding defects in the decision and remanding it back to the conference for correction.
848.keyHolding: Annual conferences cannot restructure under amended paragraph 15.15 of the Constitution without appropriate enabling legislation from General Conference, and may not delegate authority given to them by the Discipline.
848.parties: Ole Einar Anderson, lay member of Norway Annual Conference
848.outcome: Not affirmed and remanded to Norway Annual Conference for correction

849.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the Northern Illinois Annual Conference Relating to Legality of a Special Clergy Session of the Annual Conference
849.summary: The Judicial Council deferred ruling on whether a special clergy session of the Northern Illinois Annual Conference was legal, requesting more documentation before making a decision.
849.keyHolding: The Judicial Council requires adequate documentation before ruling on the legality of annual conference proceedings.

850.title: Request for Reconsideration of Decision 826
850.summary: The Judicial Council denied a request to reconsider their previous Decision 826.
850.keyHolding: The Judicial Council declined to reconsider Decision 826.

851.title: Request for Reconsideration of Decision 830
851.summary: The Judicial Council denied a request to reconsider its previous Decision 830.
851.keyHolding: The Judicial Council has discretion to deny requests for reconsideration of its prior decisions.

852.title: Appeal From the Decision of the Northeastern Jurisdictional Committee on Appeals That It Had No Jurisdiction to Hear an Appeal by a Former Probationary Member From the Western Pennsylvania Annual Conference
852.summary: A probationary member whose membership was discontinued by the Western Pennsylvania Annual Conference appealed to the Jurisdictional Committee, which ruled it had no jurisdiction over supervisory matters, and the Judicial Council affirmed this decision.
852.keyHolding: Jurisdictional Committees on Appeals do not have jurisdiction over supervisory decisions regarding discontinuance of probationary members unless formal charges are filed.
852.parties: Former probationary member from Western Pennsylvania Annual Conference
852.outcome: Affirmed - Jurisdictional Committee properly declined jurisdiction

853.title: Review of Bishop's Decisions of Law in the Northern Illinois Annual Conference On Removal of Descriptive References From Northern Illinois Annual Conference Churches and Official Organizations and On What Is Included in the Term "Official Bodies of the Church."
853.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that a bishop's decisions of law made during a Northern Illinois Annual Conference special session were invalid because the requests were improperly presented and out of order.
853.keyHolding: Bishop's decisions of law are null and void when the underlying requests are improperly presented and procedurally out of order.
853.outcome: Bishop's ruling declared improper and null and void

854.title: Review of the Amended Clergy Sexual Ethics Policy of the California-Pacific Annual Conference
854.summary: The Judicial Council found that the California-Pacific Annual Conference's revised clergy sexual ethics policy complies with church law after multiple rounds of revisions.
854.keyHolding: The revised Clergy Sexual Ethics Policy effectively complies with the Discipline by properly referencing appropriate paragraphs rather than incorporating external resources directly.
854.outcome: Policy found to be in compliance with Discipline

855.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the Northern Illinois Conference Relating to Legality of a Special Clergy Session of the Annual Conference
855.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed that bishops can hold special clergy sessions at different times and places than the regular annual conference, as long as proper consultation occurs and the session's powers are limited to what's stated in the call.
855.keyHolding: A special clergy session of the Annual Conference may be convened by the bishop at a different time and place from the regular session, provided proper consultation occurs and the session has only the powers stated in the call.
855.parties: Full clergy member of the Northern Illinois Annual Conference
855.outcome: Bishop's ruling affirmed - special clergy session was legal

856.title: Request from the Tennessee Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision on the Legality of the Portion of ¶ 2602 of the 1996 Discipline Which States 'That a Member of the Council Whose Seventieth (70th) Birthday Precedes the First Day of the Regular Session of a General Conference Shall Be Released at the Close of That General Conference from Membership or Responsibility in the Council, Regardless of the Date of Expiration of Office.'
856.summary: The Tennessee Annual Conference asked the Judicial Council to rule on age limits for Judicial Council members, but the Judicial Council declined because this matter doesn't relate to annual conference work.
856.keyHolding: Annual conferences may only request declaratory decisions on matters relating to annual conferences or their work, not on general church governance issues.

857.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the California-Nevada Annual Conference Related to Inclusiveness in the Church
857.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed a bishop's ruling that funding Reconciling Congregations programs does not exclude Transforming Congregations from conference life. Annual conferences can choose which ministries to fund without violating inclusiveness requirements.
857.keyHolding: Annual conference funding decisions for particular ministries do not constitute structural exclusion under the constitutional inclusiveness provision when all congregations remain free to participate in conference life.
857.parties: Three members of the California-Nevada Annual Conference
857.outcome: Affirmed - bishop's ruling that conference funding practices do not violate inclusiveness requirements was upheld

858.title: Request from the General Board of Higher Education and Ministry for a Declaratory Decision on the Constitutionality and Application of 714.1 of the 1996 Discipline
858.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that term limits for general program agency staff do not violate constitutional protections against status discrimination, finding that 'membership' rights don't extend to employment matters.
858.keyHolding: Constitutional protections regarding membership rights and privileges do not apply to employment matters, including term limits for agency staff positions.
858.parties: General Board of Higher Education and Ministry

859.title: Petition for Reconsideration of Decision 848
859.summary: The Judicial Council reconsidered its previous decision about the Norway Annual Conference's structure and withdrew Decision 848, finding that the conference was operating within its authority to restructure.
859.keyHolding: Central conferences have authority under ¶¶29.5 and 537.21 to make administrative changes and adaptations to the General Discipline as conditions require.
859.parties: Bishop Hans Vaxby of the Norway Annual Conference
859.outcome: Decision 848 withdrawn and matter referred to Northern Europe Central Conference Judicial Court

860.title: Petition for Reconsideration of Decision 843
860.summary: The Judicial Council denied a petition requesting reconsideration of Decision 843.
860.keyHolding: The Judicial Council denied the petition for reconsideration of Decision 843.

861.title: A Request from the Kansas East Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision on the Constitutionality of the Amended Policy on Sexual Misconduct by Church Professionals and Policy on Sexual Misconduct by Lay Church Professionals
861.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that Kansas East Conference's revised sexual misconduct policies still contained violations of church law and must be revised again before taking effect.
861.keyHolding: Annual conference sexual misconduct policies must conform to the Constitution and Discipline, including proper definitions, confidentiality protections, and adherence to existing disciplinary procedures for different categories of church members.
861.outcome: Remanded for revision - policies declared void and of no effect until properly revised and resubmitted

862.title: Request from the North Carolina Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision on Whether the Requirement That a Local Pastor Be Appointed to a Pastoral Charge (Par. 602 of the 1996 Discipline) by the Bishop to Become a Member of the Annual Conference Violates Section VI, Article II of the Constitution of The United Methodist Church
862.summary: The North Carolina Annual Conference asked whether requiring local pastors to be appointed to a pastoral charge to become conference members violates the Constitution. The Judicial Council ruled this requirement is constitutional.
862.keyHolding: The requirement that local pastors be appointed to a pastoral charge to become annual conference members does not violate the Constitution because the annual conference retains authority to determine membership eligibility based on General Conference standards.
862.outcome: Constitutional - The appointment requirement for local pastor conference membership does not violate the Constitution

863.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the Northern Illinois Annual Conference Related to the Eligibility of a Clergy Member to Be a Delegate to the 2000 General Conference When That Clergy Member's Suspension Following a Trial Is to Begin on July 1, 1999
863.summary: The Judicial Council ruled it had no authority to review a bishop's decision because the request wasn't submitted in writing during a conference session as required by church law.
863.keyHolding: A bishop's decision of law is void and of no effect if not requested in writing during the regular business of a session as required by Paragraph 2613.
863.outcome: No Jurisdiction - Bishop's decision declared void

864.title: Review of Bishop's Ruling in the Western North Carolina Annual Conference on Whether the 1999 Session of the Annual Conference Is Bound by the Rules of Order and Procedure Adopted by a Previous Annual Conference Where the Rules Purport to Set Standing Rules for All Future Annual Conferences
864.summary: The Judicial Council declined to review a bishop's ruling about conference parliamentary procedures, stating they only have authority to review legal decisions, not parliamentary rulings.
864.keyHolding: The Judicial Council lacks jurisdiction to review bishops' rulings on parliamentary procedure as these are not decisions of law under ¶2613.

865.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the Northern Illinois Annual Conference Related to a Resolution Entitled 'On Pastoral Ministry with Homosexual Persons'
865.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed a bishop's ruling that a Northern Illinois Annual Conference resolution acknowledging committed homosexual relationships does not violate church law.
865.keyHolding: A resolution acknowledging commitment between homosexual persons does not contradict the Discipline when it does not call for disobedience to prohibitions on celebrating homosexual unions.
865.parties: Northern Illinois Annual Conference member(s) requesting review of Bishop C. Joseph Sprague's decision of law

866.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the Wisconsin Annual Conference on Whether Mandatory Conference-Wide Insurance Is Legal and Appropriate in Light of ¶2532 of the 1996 Discipline
866.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that annual conferences can require all local churches to participate in a conference-wide insurance plan for property and casualty coverage.
866.keyHolding: Annual conferences have the authority to implement mandatory conference-wide property and casualty insurance plans without violating the Discipline.
866.parties: Wisconsin Annual Conference seeking ruling on insurance plan legality

867.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the West Michigan Annual Conference on Questions of Procedures and Law from a Clergy Member Placed on Administrative Leave
867.summary: A clergy member asked five questions about administrative procedures to the bishop during annual conference. The Judicial Council affirmed the bishop's decision that these questions were administrative matters not appropriate for episcopal ruling.
867.keyHolding: Questions relating to administrative actions by properly constituted bodies are not proper questions of law for substantive answers by a bishop.
867.parties: Clergy member from West Michigan Annual Conference

868.title: Review of the Sexual Harassment Policy of the Minnesota Annual Conference
868.summary: The Judicial Council reviewed Minnesota Annual Conference's Sexual Misconduct Policy and found it compliant with church law because it properly applies only to lay employees and volunteers, not clergy.
868.keyHolding: An annual conference sexual misconduct policy is valid when it properly distinguishes between standards for laity versus clergy and does not contradict existing Disciplinary provisions.

869.title: Request from United Methodist Communications for a Declaratory Decision on Whether Par. 721 of the 1996 Discipline Applies to the Council of Bishops and Official Organizations of Annual Conferences
869.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that Paragraph 721's open meeting requirements do not apply to the Council of Bishops because bishops are not considered "agencies" under the Discipline's administrative structure.
869.keyHolding: Paragraph 721 of the 1996 Discipline, which requires open meetings of church agencies, does not apply to the Council of Bishops because the Council is constitutionally authorized rather than created by General Conference as an "agency."
869.outcome: Council of Bishops is not subject to Paragraph 721's open meeting requirements

870.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the Rocky Mountain Annual Conference Related to a Petition on Inclusiveness of the Church Presented for Adoption by the Annual Conference
870.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed a bishop's ruling that an annual conference resolution to minister with all persons regardless of sexual orientation and other characteristics was proper and did not conflict with church law.
870.keyHolding: A conference resolution committing to ministry with all persons regardless of sexual orientation is in order as it distinguishes between homosexual orientation and practice, and aligns with the church's commitment to minister with all persons.
870.outcome: Bishop's ruling affirmed - resolution declared to be in order

871.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the Northwest Texas Annual Conference Requiring Any Church Adopting an Identification Label to Reverse That Action
871.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that local churches cannot identify themselves with unofficial bodies or movements, reversing a bishop's decision that said annual conferences lack authority to enforce such restrictions on local churches.
871.keyHolding: Local churches may not identify or label themselves as unofficial bodies or movements as such action is divisive and potentially conflicts with United Methodist doctrine and Discipline.
871.parties: Northwest Texas Annual Conference seeking review of Bishop Alfred J. Norris's decision of law
871.outcome: Reversed - Bishop's ruling overturned, establishing that local churches cannot identify with unofficial movements

872.title: Request From the Minnesota Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision on the Constitutionality of Par. 2628.1(j)
872.summary: The Minnesota Annual Conference asked if a rule about correcting errors in church trials was constitutional. The Judicial Council ruled it unconstitutional because it gave bishops and annual conferences powers that belong to other church bodies.
872.keyHolding: Paragraph 2628.1(j) is unconstitutional because it grants bishops and annual conferences powers reserved to other organizational bodies in the Constitution.

873.title: Review of Bishop's Ruling of Law in the Western Pennsylvania Annual Conference on Whether the Conference Structure Is in Compliance with the 1996 Book of Discipline
873.summary: A clergy member asked the bishop to rule on whether the annual conference structure complied with Discipline requirements, but the bishop ruled this was improper since it didn't relate to specific conference business. The Judicial Council affirmed the bishop's ruling.
873.keyHolding: A request for a ruling of law must relate to specific business, consideration, or discussion of an annual conference session to be proper.
873.parties: Clergy member of the Western Pennsylvania Annual Conference
873.outcome: Bishop's ruling that the request for ruling of law was improper is affirmed

874.title: Review of Bishop's Ruling of Law on Whether the General Council on Finance Administration Should Stop All Funds (Salaries) Being Paid to Those United Methodist Bishops Who Voted in Favor of Providing University Benefits for Same-Sex Domestic Partners
874.summary: A lay member asked if bishops' salaries should be stopped for voting to provide same-sex benefits at Emory University. The bishop ruled the question was moot, hypothetical and improper, which the Judicial Council affirmed.
874.keyHolding: Requests for rulings of law that are moot, hypothetical, and do not relate to actions taken or proposed by the annual conference are improper and cannot be decided.
874.parties: Lay member of Alabama-West Florida Annual Conference requesting ruling against Bishop William W. Morris
874.outcome: Affirmed - Bishop's ruling that the request was moot, hypothetical and improper was upheld

875.title: Request from the California-Pacific Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision on the Meaning, Application and Effect of the Amendment to the Constitution Ratified in 1997 Which Says "The Ordained Ministerial Delegates to the General Conference and to the Jurisdictional or Central Conferences Shall Be Elected by and from the Ordained Ministerial Members in Full Connection with the Annual Conference or Provisional Annual Conference."
875.summary: The Judicial Council clarified that only clergy who are both full members of an annual conference AND already ordained can vote for ministerial delegates to General and Jurisdictional conferences.
875.keyHolding: Both the electors and the elected ministerial delegates to General and jurisdictional conferences must be ordained ministerial members in full connection with the annual conference.
875.outcome: Constitutional amendment interpretation clarified - only ordained ministerial members in full connection may vote for ministerial delegates

876.title: Request from the California-Pacific Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision on Whether It Is Legal under the 1996 Discipline for an Annual Conference to Use the "Discernment" Model for Decision-Making
876.summary: The California-Pacific Annual Conference used a non-standard "discernment" voting process that limited amendments and clear yes/no votes, which the Judicial Council ruled violated church law and invalidated decisions made under this process.
876.keyHolding: Annual conferences cannot adopt decision-making procedures that prevent full participation by delegates or deny the total conference membership the right to make final legislative decisions.
876.outcome: Discernment model ruled unconstitutional and all decisions made under it declared null and void

877.title: Request from The South Carolina Annual Conference For A Declaratory Decision On Whether The Language of Par. 323 of the 1996 Discipline Conflicts With The Language of Par. 335.1 (d) And Whether These Paragraphs Are Applicable To The New Deacons in Full Connection As Well As To Elders in Full Connection
877.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that paragraphs about elder appointments to extension ministries do not conflict with ordination requirements and are constitutional even though they don't apply to deacons.
877.keyHolding: Paragraphs 323 and 335.1(d) addressing elder appointments and ordination are not in conflict and are constitutional despite not including deacons in full connection since deacons and elders are different orders addressed separately in the Discipline.
877.outcome: Constitutional - paragraphs are not in conflict and are constitutional

878.title: Review of Structure of Louisiana Annual Conference
878.summary: The Louisiana Annual Conference's revised structure plan was found to still violate church law and was declared null and void until properly corrected. The conference must fix issues with voting authority and membership requirements before resubmitting.
878.keyHolding: Annual conferences cannot vote to approve, disapprove, or modify the Discipline when developing structure plans, and all mandated boards and committees must exist exactly as prescribed in the Discipline.
878.outcome: Remanded - structure plan declared null and void until revised to comply with Discipline requirements

879.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the Rocky Mountain Annual Conference on Legality of Conference Board of Stewards
879.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed a bishop's ruling that a question about the legality of a Conference Board of Stewards was moot because it didn't relate to actual conference business.
879.keyHolding: Bishops may only rule on questions of law that relate to the actual business, consideration, or discussion of the conference session, not on hypothetical matters.
879.parties: Petitioner in Rocky Mountain Annual Conference
879.outcome: Bishop's decision affirmed - question ruled moot and hypothetical

880.title: Petition for Reconsideration of Decision 852
880.summary: The Judicial Council denied a petition asking them to reconsider their previous Decision 852.
880.keyHolding: The Judicial Council denied the petition for reconsideration of Decision 852.

881.title: Petition for Reconsideration of Decision 858
881.summary: The Judicial Council denied a petition to reconsider Decision 858.
881.keyHolding: The Judicial Council denied the petition for reconsideration of Decision 858.

882.title: Review of the Rewritten Policy on Sexual Misconduct by Church Professionals of the North Alabama Annual Conference
882.summary: The Judicial Council approved North Alabama Conference's sexual misconduct policy but required them to modify one section to avoid citing specific paragraph numbers that could change after General Conference.
882.keyHolding: Annual conference policies must reference Discipline provisions generally rather than citing specific paragraph numbers that may change with future revisions.
882.outcome: Modified - policy approved with required revision to remove specific paragraph citations

883.title: Request from the Coordinating Council of the Philippines Central Conference As To Whether Delegates to the Central Conference Must Be Elected by a Simple Majority or May They Be Elected by a Simple Plurality
883.summary: Annual conferences have the authority to determine their own voting procedures for electing delegates to General Conference and central conferences, including whether to use majority or plurality requirements.
883.keyHolding: Annual conferences may determine their own election procedures for delegates as long as constitutional qualifications are met.
883.parties: Coordinating Council of the Philippines Central Conference
883.outcome: Annual conferences have authority to set election procedures including plurality voting

884.title: Request from the General Conference Committee on Correlation and Editorial Revision for a Declaratory Decision on Petitions Relating to Paragraphs 215, 222.1-5, 227.2, 231.1 and .2 of the 1996 Discipline Which Have Been Declared Unconstitutional
884.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that General Conference cannot consider petitions to amend or re-adopt certain membership-related paragraphs from the 1996 Discipline that were previously declared unconstitutional. Any changes would require a constitutional amendment first.
884.keyHolding: Paragraphs of the Discipline that have been declared unconstitutional cannot be amended or re-adopted without constitutional change.
884.parties: General Conference Committee on Correlation and Editorial Revision
884.outcome: Petitions declared out of order and unconstitutional paragraphs cannot be re-adopted without constitutional amendment

885.title: Request from the General Conference Committee on Correlation and Revision for a Declaratory Decision Relating to Petitions Before the General Conference Which Use the Language "Professing Membership."
885.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that the term 'professing member' can be used constitutionally if it is properly defined to require individuals to personally take membership vows as required by the Constitution.
885.keyHolding: The phrase 'professing member' is not inherently unconstitutional but must be defined to require personal taking of membership vows as mandated by Paragraph 4 of the Constitution.
885.parties: General Conference Committee on Correlation and Revision
885.outcome: Constitutional with proper definition requiring personal vow-taking

886.title: Declaratory Decision Regarding Authority of an Annual Conference to Take Actions That Are Unconstitutional or Violate Provisions of the Discipline
886.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that annual conferences cannot ignore or violate provisions of The Book of Discipline, even when they conscientiously disagree with those provisions.
886.keyHolding: Annual conferences have no authority to negate, ignore, or violate provisions of the Discipline, as it is the binding law of the Church that regulates every phase of church life and work.
886.parties: General Conference (on motion of delegate from North Georgia Annual Conference)
886.outcome: Annual conferences cannot supersede or disobey disciplinary provisions based on conscientious disagreement

887.title: Request From the General and Judicial Administration Legislative Committee of the 2000 General Conference for a Declaratory Decision on Whether Lay Persons on the Committee on Investigation Have Voting Rights and Parity With Clergy Members Under Pars. 31, 18, and 56 or Any Other Provision of the Constitution
887.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that lay people serving on committees investigating clergy do not have voting rights equal to clergy members, and any attempt to give them such rights would be unconstitutional.
887.keyHolding: Lay persons on Annual Conference Committees on Investigation do not have constitutional voting rights and parity with clergy members in matters relating to clergy character and conference relations.
887.parties: General and Judicial Administration Legislative Committee of the 2000 General Conference
887.outcome: Unconstitutional - lay voting rights on Committee on Investigation ruled unconstitutional

888.title: Request From General Conference for a Declaratory Decision on the Meaning, Application and Effect of the Adoption of Petition #31789 as It Relates to the Election of a Person to the Judicial Council to Fill the Remaining Four Years of an Existing Eight Year Term
888.summary: General Conference removed the age 70 retirement requirement for Judicial Council members, which eliminated the vacancy that a newly elected member was supposed to fill. This made the election invalid since there was no longer a vacancy.
888.keyHolding: When General Conference removed the mandatory retirement provision that created a vacancy, it simultaneously negated the election held to fill that vacancy since no vacancy existed after the legislative change.
888.outcome: Election negated due to removal of vacancy

889.title: Request from the General Conference for a Declaratory Decision as to Whether a Vote Taken by General Conference on a Legislative Petition is Valid if Only a Portion of That Petition Has Been Printed in the Daily Christian Advocate Advanced Edition and in the Daily Christian Advocate
889.summary: The Judicial Council declined to hear a case about whether incomplete petition information invalidates General Conference votes because fewer than a majority of delegates voted to refer the matter to the Council.
889.keyHolding: Requests for declaratory decisions on non-constitutional matters require a majority vote of General Conference members present and voting for referral to the Judicial Council.
889.parties: General Conference member requesting declaratory decision

890.title: Request from 2000 General Conference for a Declaratory Decision on the Constitutionality of Petition #31143-DI-273-D as Amended by a Legislative Committee for Consideration by the General Conference Relating to Certified Lay Assistant
890.summary: The General Conference asked if a petition creating certified lay assistants would be constitutional. The Judicial Council ruled it unconstitutional because bishops can only appoint ministers, not lay persons, to charges.
890.keyHolding: Under Par. 52 of the Constitution, bishops have authority to appoint only ministers, not lay persons, to charges.
890.outcome: Petition declared unconstitutional - bishops cannot appoint lay persons to charges

891.title: Petition from the 2000 General Conference Regarding the Constitutionality of Petition #30958-FA-823-D Adopted on May 11, 2000, Which Provides that the Salary of a Newly-Elected Bishop Begins at the Time of Consecration as a Bishop
891.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that a General Conference petition setting bishop salaries to begin at consecration is constitutional, as the General Conference has the authority to create support plans for bishops.
891.keyHolding: The General Conference has constitutional authority under Article IV, Paragraph 15 to adopt plans for the support of bishops, including determining when their salaries begin.
891.parties: Delegate from the North Georgia Annual Conference

892.title: Request From the South Carolina Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision on the Constitutionality, Meaning, Application and Effect of ¶ 406.1 of the 1996 Discipline as It Relates to the Current Practice of Nominating Candidates for the Episcopacy
892.summary: The South Carolina Annual Conference challenged the constitutionality of Discipline provisions requiring episcopal nominations to occur immediately before jurisdictional conference, arguing this timing prevented meaningful annual conference input. The Judicial Council ruled the provision constitutional, finding that annual conferences do not have sole authority to nominate bishops.
892.keyHolding: ¶ 406.1 grants annual conferences permissive rather than exclusive authority to nominate episcopal candidates, and jurisdictional delegates may nominate candidates without usurping annual conference authority.

893.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the Northern Illinois Annual Conference Related to the "New Model" for the Structure of the Annual Conference and its Conformity with the 1996 Discipline
893.summary: The Judicial Council rejected a bishop's ruling that approved a new organizational structure for the Northern Illinois Annual Conference, finding the plan was incomplete and required Judicial Council approval before implementation.
893.keyHolding: Annual conferences cannot adopt restructuring plans without completing the full structure and obtaining Judicial Council approval, especially when General Conference enabling legislation is not yet in effect.
893.outcome: Not affirmed - conference must continue under Decision 831 requirements and submit final plan for Judicial Council approval

894.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in Northern Illinois Annual Conference on Whether Establishment of an Implementation Task Force for the "New Model" of Conference Structure Is in Conformity with the 1996 Discipline
894.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed a bishop's ruling that an annual conference has the authority to establish task forces and committees to conduct its business. The specific work of the task force could not yet be evaluated since it was incomplete.
894.keyHolding: Annual conferences have the prerogative to establish committees, teams, and task forces as required to conduct their business.
894.parties: Northern Illinois Annual Conference member requesting bishop's decision of law
894.outcome: Bishop's decision affirmed - annual conference authority to establish implementation task force upheld

895.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the Western New York Annual Conference on Whether a Local Pastor Who is Currently Enrolled in a Seminary Should Be Listed by the Conference Board of Ordained Ministry as a Student Local Pastor or a Part Time Local Pastor
895.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed that seminary students who have appointments and are in process within an annual conference can be classified as part-time local pastors rather than student local pastors, giving them voting rights in annual conference.
895.keyHolding: A seminary student with an appointment who is in process within an annual conference may be listed as a part-time local pastor rather than a student local pastor, thereby gaining voting rights in annual conference.
895.parties: Western New York Annual Conference Board of Ordained Ministry

896.title: Request from the Kansas East Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision on Whether Its Sexual Ethics Policies Conform to the Constitution, Discipline, and Decisions of the Judicial Council
896.summary: The Kansas East Annual Conference successfully revised its sexual ethics policies for church professionals and lay employees after previous versions were found invalid in Decision 861.
896.keyHolding: Annual conference sexual ethics policies must comply with Disciplinary provisions regarding terminology, confidentiality protections, and proper reporting procedures to be valid.
896.outcome: Constitutional - policies found valid after modifications addressing previous deficiencies

897.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the Pacific Northwest Annual Conference on Whether a Motion Entitled "Affirmation of the Goodness of Human Sexuality" Could Be Adopted
897.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that a bishop erred by suspending debate and voting on a resolution about human sexuality when he delayed his legal ruling, stating that conference business should proceed while awaiting the bishop's decision.
897.keyHolding: Annual conference business should not be suspended when a bishop delays ruling on a question of law, and such business should proceed subject to the bishop's eventual ruling.
897.parties: Pacific Northwest Annual Conference clergy member requesting decision of law
897.outcome: Remanded to bishop for ruling by February 1, 2001

898.title: Appeal of Bishop's Decision of Law in the Iowa Annual Conference Ruling Out of Order a Motion to Amend the Rules of Order of the Annual Conference
898.summary: The Judicial Council declined to review a bishop's parliamentary ruling that declared a motion to amend conference rules out of order, stating they have no authority over such parliamentary decisions.
898.keyHolding: The Judicial Council lacks disciplinary authority to review parliamentary rulings made by presiding bishops.
898.parties: Lay member of the Iowa Annual Conference

899.title: Constitutionality, Meaning, Application, or Effect of ¶ 720 of the 1996 Discipline
899.summary: The Alaska Missionary Conference asked whether paragraph 720.1 requiring a calendar year fiscal year applies to all church bodies. The Judicial Council ruled it only applies to agencies created by General Conference, not annual conferences.
899.keyHolding: Paragraph 720.1 requiring calendar year fiscal years applies only to church entities created by General Conference, not to annual conferences or other entities created by the Constitution.
899.outcome: Church entities not created by General Conference are free to establish their own fiscal years

900.title: Consideration of the Amended Structure of the Louisiana Annual Conference as Required by Decision 878
900.summary: The Louisiana Annual Conference's revised structure still didn't comply with church law requirements, so the Judicial Council declared it null and void until properly corrected.
900.keyHolding: Annual conference structures must fully comply with Discipline requirements and cannot vote to approve, disapprove, or modify mandated boards and committees established by the General Conference.
900.outcome: Structure declared null and void and remanded for revision

901.title: Appeal of Bishop's Determination in the West Virginia Annual Conference Stating That a Resolution Presented to the Annual Conference Directing West Virginia Wesleyan College to Rescind its 24 Hour Visitation Policy Was Out of Order
901.summary: The Judicial Council determined it had no jurisdiction over a bishop's parliamentary ruling that declared a resolution about West Virginia Wesleyan College's visitation policy out of order. The Conference mistakenly thought this was a decision of law that could be appealed.
901.keyHolding: The Judicial Council lacks jurisdiction over parliamentary rulings that are not decisions of law.
901.parties: West Virginia Annual Conference members appealing the Bishop's ruling
901.outcome: No Jurisdiction - parliamentary ruling not appealable as decision of law

902.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the California-Nevada Annual Conference Related to ¶ 2628.1(j) of the 1996 Discipline Which Was Declared Unconstitutional by the Judicial Council in Decision 872
902.summary: Bishop Talbert correctly ruled that he lacked authority to review a Committee on Investigation's decision not to try 68 clergy who participated in a same-sex holy union ceremony, because the relevant disciplinary paragraph had been declared unconstitutional.
902.keyHolding: A bishop has no authority to correct investigative proceedings under ¶ 2628.1(j) because that paragraph was declared unconstitutional in Decision 872.
902.parties: Two lay persons from California-Nevada Annual Conference questioning Bishop Talbert's ruling
902.outcome: Affirmed - Bishop correctly ruled he lacked authority under unconstitutional paragraph

903.title: Bishop's Decision of Law in the California-Nevada Annual Conference Related to the Propriety of the Committee on Investigation Inviting Diverse Witnesses from Across the Nation to Speak on Homosexuality and Sexual Orientation Generally Rather than Speaking on the Specific Complaints Against the Participants in the January 16, 1999 Event on Which the Charges Before the Committee Were Based
903.summary: A lay member asked questions about a Committee on Investigation's process during annual conference, but the Judicial Council ruled these weren't proper legal questions requiring a bishop's decision since they didn't relate to conference business.
903.keyHolding: Questions presented as 'questions of law' must relate to the business, consideration or discussion of the conference session to require a bishop's decision of law.
903.parties: Lay member of California-Nevada Annual Conference
903.outcome: Bishop's decisions not affirmed - questions were not proper questions of law

904.title: Ruling From the Judicial Court of the Northern Europe Central Conference in Response to a Request From the Judicial Council in Decision 859 for a Ruling on the Norway Annual Conference Structure
904.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that adaptations by the Northern Europe Central Conference allowing Norway Annual Conference to eliminate its board of laity and combine financial/administrative functions into one Main Board violated the UMC Constitution.
904.keyHolding: Central conferences cannot make adaptations to the Discipline that are contrary to the Constitution of The United Methodist Church or that directly oppose legislation enacted by General Conference.
904.parties: Northern Europe Central Conference and Norway Annual Conference

905.title: Request from the Alaska Missionary Conference for a Declaratory Decision on Whether ¶ 710 Is Constitutional as it Relates to the Requirement That a Lay Member of a General Agency of the United Methodist Church Resign When the Member's Permanent Residence Changes to a Place Outside the Boundaries of the Conference
905.summary: The Alaska Missionary Conference challenged rules requiring lay members of general agencies to resign if they move outside their conference boundaries, arguing this created unfair differences between clergy and lay requirements. The Judicial Council ruled the requirements are constitutional because they appropriately reflect the different ways clergy and lay members relate to annual conferences.
905.keyHolding: Different eligibility requirements for clergy and lay members of general agencies are constitutional when they reflect the different bases for determining annual conference relationships for each group.

906.title: Request from the Holston Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision as to the Meaning of ¶ 420 of the 1992 Discipline Pertaining to the Election of Full-Time Local Pastors to Associate Membership and the Ability to Equate Part-Time Service to Fulfill the Requirement of Full-Time Service
906.summary: The Holston Annual Conference asked for clarification on whether part-time local pastoral service could count toward the full-time service requirement for associate membership. The Judicial Council ruled that only completed part-time service can be equated to full-time service, not future anticipated service.
906.keyHolding: Annual conferences may equate completed part-time local pastoral service to full-time service requirements for associate membership, but cannot equate future anticipated part-time service.
906.outcome: Clarified that only completed part-time service can be equated to full-time service requirements, not future service

907.title: Request From the North Carolina Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision on the Legality of a Resolution on Homosexuality Adopted by the Annual Conference in June 2000
907.summary: The North Carolina Annual Conference asked the Judicial Council to rule on whether their resolution about homosexuality was legal. The Judicial Council declined to rule, saying they don't have authority to review annual conference resolutions.
907.keyHolding: The Judicial Council lacks jurisdiction to render declaratory decisions on annual conference resolutions that do not involve questions of constitutionality, meaning, application, or effect of the Discipline or General Conference legislation.

908.title: Request from the Coordinating Council of the Philippines Central Conference for a Declaratory Decision on the Status of a Member of That Council Who Is Elected to Membership on the Judicial Council
908.summary: A person elected to the Judicial Council cannot serve on any central conference boards or committees and must resign from such positions immediately.
908.keyHolding: Members of the Judicial Council are ineligible to serve on any general, jurisdictional, or central conference board or agency.
908.parties: Coordinating Council of the Philippines Central Conference
908.outcome: Judicial Council member must resign from all central conference positions

909.title: Consideration of the Constitutionality of the New Model Plan of Structure Adopted by the Northern Illinois Annual Conference in November 2000 over Which the Judicial Council Retained Jurisdiction in Decision 893
909.summary: The Judicial Council found that the Northern Illinois Annual Conference's New Model restructuring plan was still incomplete and could not be implemented until the conference properly defines how the new structure will work with existing conference bodies.
909.keyHolding: An annual conference restructuring plan must be complete and properly integrate with existing disciplinary requirements before implementation, and the Judicial Council retains jurisdiction to review such restructuring plans.
909.outcome: Plan found incomplete; conference directed to continue under Decision 831 requirements until proper integration defined

910.title: Reconsideration of Decision 904
910.summary: The Judicial Council withdrew Decision 904, recognizing it had no jurisdiction over matters involving central conference modifications to church structure since those fall under the exclusive jurisdiction of the central conference's judicial court.
910.keyHolding: The Judicial Council lacks jurisdiction over central conference modifications to the Discipline, as such matters fall exclusively under the jurisdiction of the central conference's judicial court.
910.parties: Northern Europe Central Conference and Norway Annual Conference regarding conference structure
910.outcome: Decision 904 withdrawn due to lack of jurisdiction

911.title: Continued Jurisdiction over Ruling of Law by Bishop Elias G. Galvan in the Pacific Northwest Conference as Required by Decision 897
911.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that an annual conference cannot legally offer a resolution on human sexuality even if it claims not to endorse it, because doing so would still violate church law.
911.keyHolding: Annual conferences cannot legally offer resolutions that violate the Discipline even when claiming not to endorse the content, as the act of offering itself constitutes conference action.
911.parties: Clergy member requesting decision of law regarding Report #10 in Pacific Northwest Annual Conference
911.outcome: Bishop's decision not affirmed - resolution violates Discipline and cannot be acted upon

912.title: Petition for Reconsideration of Memorandum 888
912.summary: The Judicial Council denied a petition seeking reconsideration of their earlier Memorandum 888.
912.keyHolding: The petition for reconsideration of Memorandum 888 was denied by the Judicial Council.

913.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the Desert Southwest Annual Conference in Regard to a Resolution Adopted by the Annual Conference Affirming a Resolution of the Western Jurisdictional Conference Entitled "We Will Not Be Silent."
913.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed a bishop's ruling that an annual conference resolution supporting LGBTQ+ inclusion did not violate church law. The resolution affirmed dialogue and ministry with all persons while respecting diverse viewpoints.
913.keyHolding: Annual conference resolutions that affirm ministry with all persons and encourage dialogue on contested issues do not violate the Discipline even when addressing controversial topics like homosexuality.
913.parties: Clergy member requesting ruling on Desert Southwest Annual Conference Resolution 21.20
913.outcome: Affirmed - resolution does not violate Discipline

914.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the West Virginia Annual Conference on Questions Related to a Restructure Plan Adopted by the Annual Conference in its 2001 Session
914.summary: The West Virginia Annual Conference's restructuring plan partially met Discipline requirements but needed more specific details about relationships between groups and funding before full approval.
914.keyHolding: Annual conference restructuring plans must include specific definitions of relationships between organizational bodies, funding methods, and amended standing rules to meet Judicial Council precedent requirements.
914.parties: West Virginia Annual Conference requesting review of bishop's decision of law
914.outcome: Partially affirmed, partially reversed, remanded for revision with retained jurisdiction

915.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the Illinois Great Rivers Annual Conference Related to the Termination of Voluntary Leave of a Clergy Member of the Annual Conference
915.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that a clergy member cannot be forced to continue on voluntary leave of absence against her will and ordered the conference to either end her leave or begin involuntary leave proceedings.
915.keyHolding: A clergy member on voluntary leave of absence who requests in a timely manner the termination of that leave cannot be continued on voluntary leave against their will without following proper disciplinary procedures.
915.parties: Clergy Member Kumji Hwang and Illinois Great Rivers Annual Conference
915.outcome: Bishop's decision reversed in part and affirmed in part; case remanded with orders for equitable compensation and proper leave procedures

916.title: Limited Reconsideration of Decision 909 for Clarification of Whether All Annual Conference Restructure Plans Must Be Postponed Until After the 2004 General Conference Adopts Enabling Legislation for ¶ 15.15 of the Constitution
916.summary: Annual conferences can restructure themselves under existing Discipline paragraphs without waiting for new legislation, as long as they maintain all required connections and follow existing rules.
916.keyHolding: Annual conferences may restructure under ¶ 608 without waiting for enabling legislation for ¶ 15.15, provided they comply with all mandated disciplinary paragraphs and maintain required connections.
916.outcome: Clarified that annual conferences can restructure under existing disciplinary authority without waiting for new enabling legislation

917.title: Request from the California-Pacific Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision on the Appropriateness of a Cabinet Member Participating in the Administrative Process of the Board of Ordained Ministry Under ¶¶ 318.6, 356.3 and 359.3 of the 2000 Discipline
