917.summary: A district superintendent serving on the Board of Ordained Ministry cannot participate in voting or deliberations when the board handles administrative complaints or involuntary actions against clergy because it violates separation of powers principles.
917.keyHolding: District superintendents representing the cabinet on boards of ordained ministry must recuse themselves from participating in administrative processes involving involuntary discontinuation, retirement, or complaints due to separation of powers requirements.
917.outcome: District superintendents prohibited from participating in Board of Ordained Ministry deliberations and votes on specified administrative processes

918.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the Pacific Northwest Annual Conference on the Appropriateness of the Expenditure of Funds for a Special Called Session of the Western Jurisdictional Conference
918.summary: A bishop ruled that a question about spending money for a special jurisdictional conference was premature since no session had been called and no funds approved. The Judicial Council affirmed this decision.
918.keyHolding: A request for ruling on expenditure of funds for a jurisdictional conference session is premature and hypothetical when no special session has been called and no funds have been approved.
918.parties: Member of Pacific Northwest Annual Conference questioning expenditure of funds
918.outcome: Affirmed - question was premature and hypothetical

919.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the South Carolina Annual Conference Related to Compensation and Other Matters Pertaining to a Clergy Member Placed on Involuntary Leave of Absence During a Judicial Process
919.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed a bishop's ruling about compensation for clergy on involuntary leave of absence, finding that the Council on Finance and Administration has no authority to grant such compensation.
919.keyHolding: The Council on Finance and Administration has no authority to grant compensation to clergy members on involuntary leave of absence under ¶351.1.b.
919.parties: Reverend Luonne Abram Rouse (questioner) regarding Reverend Doctor Timothy J. Bowman's compensation

920.title: Request from the Pacific Northwest Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision on the Perceived Conflict Between the Last Sentence of ¶ 325.1 and ¶ 304.3 of the 2000 Discipline
920.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that a clergy woman's statement about living in a partnered homosexual relationship triggers a review process under church law, and that bishops cannot unilaterally refuse appointments but must follow due process procedures.
920.keyHolding: A declaration of living in a partnered homosexual relationship by clergy is sufficient to subject their ministerial membership to review, but bishops must follow due process rather than taking unilateral action regarding appointments.
920.outcome: The Council found no conflict between the paragraphs in question and established procedures for handling such declarations while preserving due process rights

921.title: Request from the California-Pacific Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision on the Meaning of ¶ 633 of the 2000 Discipline Which Is Related to the Administrative Review Committee and Administrative Fair Process Procedures
921.summary: The Judicial Council clarified that administrative review committees only need to review written records for fair process violations, without requiring participation from probationary members or executive committee members in the review process.
921.keyHolding: Administrative review committees are required only to review the written record for fair process violations and are not required to include the probationary member or executive committee in the review process unless a hearing is deemed necessary.
921.outcome: Clarified that administrative review committees need only review written records unless a hearing is necessary

922.title: Review of the Revised Design for Ministry of the Holston Annual Conference as Required by Decision 835
922.summary: The Judicial Council reviewed a revised reorganization plan from the Holston Annual Conference and required three specific changes to comply with Disciplinary requirements before final approval.
922.keyHolding: Annual conference restructuring plans must maintain the specific responsibilities, membership compositions, and accountability structures mandated by the Discipline even when changing organizational names or structures.
922.outcome: Conditional approval requiring three specific revisions to comply with Disciplinary mandates

923.title: Request from the North Georgia Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision on the Legality of the Provision of a New Insurance Program Adopted by the Annual Conference
923.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that North Georgia Annual Conference's mandatory health insurance plan was invalid because it improperly used clergy contributions to fund retiree benefits and failed to follow proper budgetary procedures.
923.keyHolding: Annual conferences have authority to establish mandatory health insurance programs for clergy but cannot use clergy benefits to pay unfunded retiree liability and must follow proper disciplinary procedures for budget presentation.
923.outcome: Plan declared null and void, remanded to conference for compliance with proper procedures

924.title: Request from the Western North Carolina Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision as to the Constitutionality of Portions of ¶ 602.4 of the 2000 Discipline
924.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that requiring certain lay persons to be members of annual conference violates the Constitution. Only a constitutional amendment can mandate these memberships.
924.keyHolding: Disciplinary provisions mandating specific persons as annual conference members beyond those listed in the Constitution are unconstitutional.

925.title: Motion to Appeal Judicial Council Decision 907
925.summary: The North Carolina Annual Conference tried to appeal a Judicial Council decision, but the Judicial Council ruled that its decisions cannot be appealed and are final.
925.keyHolding: All decisions of the Judicial Council are final and there is no disciplinary provision for appealing a Judicial Council decision.
925.outcome: No jurisdiction - Judicial Council decisions cannot be appealed

926.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the North Carolina Annual Conference Related to Resolution of Complaint Filed Against a Clergy Member
926.summary: A retired elder asked the bishop to define terms like 'crime' and 'immorality' and clarify complaint procedures, but the bishop ruled the questions hypothetical since no related matters were before the conference.
926.keyHolding: Bishops are not required to answer hypothetical questions that do not relate to matters actually before the Annual Conference.
926.parties: Elder in full connection (retired) from North Carolina Annual Conference
926.outcome: Affirmed - questions ruled moot and hypothetical

927.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the North Carolina Annual Conference on Whether Funds of Any United Methodist Unit may be Given to any Organization, Institution, Caucus or Group that Promotes the Acceptance of Homosexuality by Allowing any Portion of its Property to be Used to Celebrate Same Sex Unions
927.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed a bishop's ruling that a question about funding organizations that allow same-sex unions on their property was moot and hypothetical because it didn't relate to any actual conference business.
927.keyHolding: Questions of law must be germane to the regular business, considerations or discussions of the Annual Conference and cannot be moot or hypothetical.
927.parties: Retired elder in full connection from North Carolina Annual Conference

928.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the Western Pennsylvania Annual Conference on a Series of Questions Related to the Annual Conference Structure
928.summary: The Judicial Council found that the Western Pennsylvania Annual Conference's structure violated church law and ordered it to return to its previous compliant structure by 2002, while allowing temporary operation under current rules.
928.keyHolding: Annual conference structures must comply with Disciplinary requirements, and conferences cannot operate indefinitely under non-compliant organizational rules.
928.parties: Clergy member of Western Pennsylvania Annual Conference questioning conference structure
928.outcome: Bishop's decisions affirmed in part and reversed in part; conference ordered to revert to compliant structure

929.title: Request from the Commission on General Conference for a Declaratory Decision on the Meaning of 'Any Organization' in 507 of the 2000 Discipline
929.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that the phrase "any organization" in Paragraph 507 includes both official and unofficial United Methodist groups, and the Commission on General Conference cannot restrict petition access to only official organizations.
929.keyHolding: The Commission on General Conference lacks authority to limit "any organization" in ¶507 to only official UMC organizations, as determining petition access is a distinctively connectional matter under General Conference authority.
929.outcome: Commission lacks authority to restrict petition access to official organizations only

930.title: Reconsideration of Decision 920
930.summary: The Judicial Council modified its previous Decision 920 to change mandatory suspension language to permissive language, making clergy suspension discretionary rather than required during certain investigations.
930.keyHolding: The language in ¶ 359.1(c) regarding clergy suspension during investigations is permissive ('may') rather than mandatory ('shall'), requiring modification of Decision 920 to reflect the actual Disciplinary language.
930.outcome: Decision 920 modified to replace mandatory suspension language with permissive language

931.title: Request From the North Central Jurisdiction Commission on Archives and History for a Declaratory Decision on the Necessity of Annual Conference Structures Making Provision for Fulfilling the Requirements of 638 of the 2000 Discipline Concerning Archival and Historical Matters
931.summary: The North Central Jurisdiction Commission on Archives and History requested clarification about whether annual conferences must create structures to meet archival and historical requirements, but withdrew their request before a decision was made.
931.keyHolding: No holding as the request was withdrawn before adjudication.
931.parties: North Central Jurisdiction Commission on Archives and History

932.title: Petition for Limited Reconsideration of Decision 921
932.summary: The Judicial Council denied a request to reconsider its previous Decision 921.
932.keyHolding: The petition for limited reconsideration of Decision 921 was denied without further elaboration.

933.title: Petition for Reconsideration of Decision 919
933.summary: The Judicial Council denied a petition asking them to reconsider their previous Decision 919.
933.keyHolding: The Judicial Council denied the petition for reconsideration of Decision 919.
933.parties: Not specified in the available text

934.title: Petition for Reconsideration of Decision 915
934.summary: The Judicial Council denied a request to reconsider its previous Decision 915.
934.keyHolding: The petition for reconsideration of Decision 915 was denied without further elaboration.

935.title: Review of the Revised Insurance Program of the North Georgia Annual Conference as Required by Decision 923
935.summary: The Judicial Council approved North Georgia Annual Conference's revised clergy insurance plan after finding it properly complied with Disciplinary procedures for budgetary and compensation matters.
935.keyHolding: An annual conference's insurance plan must comply with Disciplinary procedures for budgetary preparation and presentation, and cannot use clergy benefits to fund unfunded retiree medical insurance liability.
935.outcome: Approved - Conference may implement the revised 2002 Plan

936.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the Kansas East Annual Conference on the Portion of the Conference Child Abuse Policy Which Requires Clergy To Report All Cases of Child Abuse Including Information Regarding Such Conduct Received in a Confidential or Confessional Setting
936.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed that a conference policy requiring clergy to report all child abuse cases violated church law because it ignored the requirement that clergy maintain confidential confessions inviolate. The issue became moot when the conference amended its policy to include proper exceptions.
936.keyHolding: Annual conference policies requiring clergy to report child abuse must recognize and except information obtained through confidential confessions, as clergy are charged by ¶ 332.5 to maintain all confidences inviolate.
936.parties: Kansas East Annual Conference seeking review of Bishop's Decision of Law
936.outcome: Bishop's decision affirmed; conference policy violation confirmed but issue rendered moot by subsequent policy amendment

937.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the Wisconsin Annual Conference Related to Licensing and Appointment of a Local Pastor
937.summary: A bishop correctly ruled that questions about local pastor licensing and appointments were hypothetical and not related to actual conference business. The Judicial Council affirmed that bishops are not required to answer moot and hypothetical questions.
937.keyHolding: Bishops are not required to answer moot and hypothetical questions that are not germane to the actual business before the annual conference.
937.parties: Clergy member of Wisconsin Annual Conference
937.outcome: Affirmed - Bishop's ruling that questions were moot and hypothetical was correct

938.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the Baltimore-Washington Annual Conference Related to the Authority of the Clergy Session to Move That a Clergy Person Be Placed on Involuntary Leave of Absence
938.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed a bishop's ruling that a motion to place a clergy member on involuntary leave was out of order because proper fair process procedures had not been followed.
938.keyHolding: A motion to place clergy on involuntary leave of absence cannot be entertained until all provisions of fair process set forth in the Discipline have been followed.
938.parties: Two clergy members of the Baltimore-Washington Annual Conference requesting review of Bishop May's decision of law
938.outcome: Affirmed - Bishop's ruling that the motion was out of order due to lack of fair process was upheld

939.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the Illinois Great Rivers Annual Conference Related to the Legality of a Proposed Amendment to the Illinois Great Rivers Annual Conference Foundation's By-laws Allowing the Foundation to Accept Funds from Non-Methodist Related Entities
939.summary: The Judicial Council declined to review a bishop's decision about whether a conference foundation could accept funds from non-Methodist sources because the request did not meet procedural requirements.
939.keyHolding: The Judicial Council lacks jurisdiction to review matters that do not meet the procedural requirements of ¶2609.6.

940.title: Request from the Illinois Great Rivers Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision on a Perceived Conflict Between ¶¶ 352.1.b and 359.2 of the 2000 Discipline
940.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that there is no conflict between Discipline paragraphs regarding administrative complaints and that the wording 'administrative complaint' must be included in written communications to clergy respondents.
940.keyHolding: An administrative complaint must be written and signed, and the wording 'administrative complaint' must be included in the written communication to the respondent for clarity.
940.outcome: No conflict found between paragraphs; administrative complaint wording requirement clarified

941.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the Illinois Great Rivers Annual Conference Related to a Resolution Establishing a Process of Cabinet Review of Clergy Who Participate in or Allow Events to Be Held in Their Church Buildings That Promote Dialogue on Homosexuality
941.summary: The Judicial Council determined it had no authority to review a bishop's parliamentary ruling that was mistakenly thought to be a decision of law regarding a resolution about dialogue on homosexuality.
941.keyHolding: The Judicial Council lacks disciplinary authority to review parliamentary rulings by presiding bishops, only decisions of law.

942.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the Illinois Great Rivers Annual Conference Relative to the Action Taken by the Board of Ordained Ministry and the Cabinet on the Appointive Status of a Clergy Member of the Annual Conference
942.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that bishops do not have authority to make decisions on matters that are solely judicial or administrative in nature, as these belong to judicial bodies of the church.
942.keyHolding: Bishops lack authority to make substantive rulings on judicial or administrative matters, which must be decided by appropriate judicial or administrative bodies to maintain separation of powers.
942.parties: Illinois Great Rivers Annual Conference clergy member
942.outcome: Bishop's decisions not affirmed due to lack of authority over judicial/administrative matters

943.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the Illinois Great Rivers Annual Conference on a Resolution Requiring That Each Local Church in the Annual Conference Have a Lay Member of the Annual Conference
943.summary: The Judicial Council declined to review a matter from Illinois Great Rivers Annual Conference because it involved parliamentary procedure rather than a bishop's legal ruling.
943.keyHolding: The Judicial Council lacks jurisdiction over parliamentary requests to rule motions out of order, as these are not requests for rulings of law by bishops.

944.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the Pacific Northwest Annual Conference
944.summary: A bishop properly ruled that a question about whether a clergy person could refuse to answer questions during certification review was improper and hypothetical because it related to ongoing judicial proceedings.
944.keyHolding: Bishops must not make rulings on matters that are judicial in nature as this threatens to blur the line between executive authority and judicial process.
944.parties: Lay member of Pacific Northwest Annual Conference requesting decision of law from Bishop Elias G. Galván

945.title: Request from the Kansas West Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision Related to the Equitable Compensation of Women Pastors
945.summary: The Kansas West Annual Conference requested a declaratory decision about equal pay for women pastors, but the Judicial Council ruled it lacked jurisdiction because the request didn't ask about a specific Discipline paragraph.
945.keyHolding: Declaratory decision requests must seek determination of the meaning, application, or effect of a specific paragraph of the Discipline to establish Judicial Council jurisdiction.

946.title: Review of Bishop Decision of Law in the Rocky Mountain Annual Conference on Whether Prohibiting Annual Conference Members from Participating in Legislative Committees to Which They Are Not Assigned Is Constitutional
946.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed a bishop's ruling that annual conference rules limiting voting and motions to assigned committee members are constitutional, since final decisions are made by the full conference in plenary session.
946.keyHolding: Annual conferences may adopt legislative committee procedures that restrict voting and motions to assigned committee members, provided that final legislative decisions are made by the entire conference membership in plenary session.
946.parties: A clergy member of the Rocky Mountain Annual Conference who challenged the legislative committee rules
946.outcome: Affirmed - the bishop's decision that the legislative process was constitutional was upheld

947.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the Rocky Mountain Annual Conference Related to the Necessity of Printing the Entire Budget in the Conference Journal and to the Legality of Certain Processes and Portions of the Annual Conference Budget
947.summary: The Judicial Council reviewed a bishop's decisions about annual conference budget requirements, affirming that conferences are not required to print complete budgets in journals but must properly separate district superintendent compensation items and include all anticipated income.
947.keyHolding: Annual conferences have discretion in determining what reports appear in their journals, including budgets, but must properly categorize budget items and include all anticipated income in budget presentations.
947.parties: Rocky Mountain Annual Conference members who submitted questions of law to Bishop Warner H. Brown, Jr.
947.outcome: Partially affirmed - bishop affirmed on journal printing requirement but not affirmed on budget presentation issues

948.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the Alaska Missionary Conference Related to the Process of Discontinuance of a Local Church
948.summary: A bishop incorrectly refused to answer questions of law about church discontinuance procedures, claiming they were requests for declaratory decisions instead. The Judicial Council ruled the questions were proper and must be answered.
948.keyHolding: Bishops do not have authority to determine whether properly submitted questions are questions of law or requests for declaratory decisions and must answer all properly presented questions of law.
948.parties: Lay member of Alaska Missionary Conference questioning church discontinuance process
948.outcome: Bishop's decision not affirmed; directed to answer the questions and submit to conference journal and Judicial Council

949.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the Northern Illinois Annual Conference Related to the Constitutionality of a Property Action Taken by the Annual Conference
949.summary: A clergy member asked Bishop Sprague to rule on whether an annual conference resolution about campground property was constitutional, but the Judicial Council found this was actually a parliamentary procedure question, not a legal ruling.
949.keyHolding: The Judicial Council has no disciplinary authority to assume jurisdiction over questions of parliamentary procedure addressed to a presiding bishop.
949.parties: Clergy member of Northern Illinois Annual Conference
949.outcome: No Jurisdiction - question was parliamentary procedure, not a legal ruling

950.title: Request from the California-Pacific Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision on Whether it Is Allowable for Bishops and District Superintendents to Be Voting Participants in a Hearing Requested by a Clergy Member Recommended for Involuntary Leave as Described in ¶ 352.1 of the 2000 Discipline
950.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that bishops and district superintendents cannot vote or be present in hearings about placing clergy on involuntary leave of absence because it violates fair process principles.
950.keyHolding: Bishops and district superintendents may not participate as voting members or remain present in involuntary leave of absence hearings as this violates separation of powers and fair process requirements.
950.outcome: Bishops and district superintendents prohibited from participating in involuntary leave hearings; jurisdiction disputed in dissenting opinion

951.title: Review of the Restructure and Related Documents of the West Virginia Annual Conference as Required by Decision 914
951.summary: The Judicial Council reviewed and approved the West Virginia Annual Conference's revised restructure plan after it addressed five specific concerns raised in Decision 914. The conference successfully amended its rules, clarified funding processes, and defined staff roles to comply with church law.
951.keyHolding: The West Virginia Annual Conference restructure plan, as amended, satisfies the requirements of the Discipline and prior Judicial Council decisions regarding conference restructuring.
951.parties: West Virginia Annual Conference member of the Conference Rules Committee requesting episcopal ruling
951.outcome: Affirmed - restructure plan approved as compliant with Discipline requirements after amendments

952.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the Rocky Mountain Annual Conference Related to the Process of Evaluation by the Conference Personnel Committee of the Annual Conference Staffing Plan
952.summary: The Rocky Mountain Annual Conference adopted a petition to have their personnel committee evaluate conference staff positions and performance under the Board of Stewards' direction. The Judicial Council ruled this arrangement was not lawful under church law.
952.keyHolding: A conference personnel committee functioning under ¶611.12 must report directly to the annual conference and cannot be under the direction of another entity like the Board of Stewards.
952.outcome: Bishop's decision of law not affirmed; petition ruled unlawful

953.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the West Virginia Annual Conference Related to the Use by the West Virginia Conference Board of Pensions of Funds Invested with the General Board of Pension and Health Benefits
953.summary: The Judicial Council reviewed a bishop's decision about whether a conference pension board could transfer pension funds to pay health insurance claims, but found the record incomplete and continued the case to gather more documents.
953.keyHolding: The Judicial Council cannot rule on incomplete records and will continue consideration until adequate documentation is provided regarding pension fund transfers.
953.parties: Two retired clergy members of the West Virginia Annual Conference
953.outcome: Bishop not affirmed on Question 1; consideration continued pending additional documentation; no jurisdiction on Question 2 (parliamentary ruling)

954.title: Review of the Revised Sexual Ethics Policy of the East Ohio Annual Conference as Required by Decision 839
954.summary: The Judicial Council rejected East Ohio's sexual ethics policy because required appendices were not included or approved by the conference. The policy must be resubmitted with all related materials properly adopted.
954.keyHolding: A sexual ethics policy cannot be approved by the Judicial Council unless all appendices and directly related materials are adopted by the Annual Conference and included in the submission for review.
954.outcome: Remanded - policy declared void and of no effect until complete submission with all required materials

955.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the East Ohio Annual Conference on the Constitutionality of the 2001 East Ohio Conference Action to Use Interest from Capital Raised to Fund Pre-82 Pension Liability for the Purpose of Partially Funding Health Care Costs And/or Replenishing the Health Care Reserve Account for Conference Claimants
955.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed a bishop's decision that a question about using pension fund interest for health care costs was moot because it didn't cite specific violations of church law.
955.keyHolding: A bishop cannot rule on questions of law that do not cite specific actions violating particular paragraphs of the Discipline.
955.parties: Conference member from East Ohio Annual Conference questioning Bishop Jonathan L. Keaton's decision
955.outcome: Affirmed - Bishop's ruling that question was moot was upheld

956.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the East Ohio Annual Conference on Whether the Resident Bishop and Annual Conference Were in Violation of ¶ 415.6 of the 2000 Discipline When the Words "In the Name of the Triune God" Were Substituted for the Words, "In the Name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit" in the Service of Ordination at the 2001 Session of the East Ohio Annual Conference
956.summary: The Judicial Council ruled it had no jurisdiction to review a question about whether substitute ordination language violated church law because the question was raised at the wrong conference session.
956.keyHolding: The Judicial Council lacks jurisdiction when a question of law is not raised appropriately during the business of the relevant annual conference session where the matter occurred.
956.parties: Member of the 2002 session of the East Ohio Annual Conference

957.title: Review of the Revised Restructure of Western Pennsylvania Annual Conference as Required by Decision 928
957.summary: The Judicial Council approved the Western Pennsylvania Annual Conference's revised organizational structure after the conference made required changes following an earlier ruling.
957.keyHolding: The revised structure and rules of the Western Pennsylvania Annual Conference comply with both the Discipline and Decision 928 requirements.
957.outcome: Revised conference structure approved as compliant with Discipline and previous decision

958.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the Virginia Annual Conference Related to Clergy Retiree Health Plan Eligibility
958.summary: The Judicial Council reviewed a bishop's decision about clergy retiree health plan eligibility in Virginia but deferred their ruling until Spring 2003.
958.keyHolding: The case was deferred without a substantive ruling on clergy retiree health plan eligibility requirements.

959.title: Request from the General Council on Finance and Administration for a Declaratory Decision on the Meaning, Application and Effect of ¶ 405.2 b) and c) Dealing with the Number of Bishops Assigned to Each Jurisdiction
959.summary: The General Council on Finance and Administration requested a declaratory decision about rules governing how many bishops are assigned to each jurisdiction, but the Judicial Council deferred the matter.
959.keyHolding: The Judicial Council deferred consideration of the request regarding bishop assignment rules to jurisdictions until Spring 2003.
959.parties: General Council on Finance and Administration

960.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the West Ohio Annual Conference on the Legality of a Special Clergy Session Held at a Different Time and Place from the Regular Session of the West Ohio Annual Conference
960.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that annual conferences must hold their required clergy session at the same location as the regular conference session, and that special clergy sessions held elsewhere cannot replace this requirement.
960.keyHolding: Annual conferences must hold a clergy session at the site of the regular session of the annual conference as required by ¶365.5, and special clergy sessions held elsewhere cannot substitute for this mandatory requirement.
960.parties: West Ohio Annual Conference clergy member
960.outcome: Modified - Bishop's decision affirmed in part and reversed in part

961.title: Request from the Council of Bishops for a Declaratory Decision on a Proposed Amendment to ¶ 407.3 of the 2000 Discipline Making the Term of the President of the Council of Bishops Four Years and Releasing the President from Residential and Presidential Responsibilities During That Four Year Term
961.summary: The Council of Bishops proposed legislation to allow a bishop to serve as President for four years without residential duties, but this would be unconstitutional without a constitutional amendment.
961.keyHolding: Proposed legislation allowing a bishop to serve as President of the Council of Bishops for four years without residential and presidential responsibilities would violate constitutional requirements in ¶ 47 that bishops have residential and presidential supervision.
961.outcome: Proposed legislation ruled unconstitutional; Decision 843 overruled regarding timing of enabling legislation

962.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the Alaska Missionary Conference Related to the Process of Discontinuance of a Local Church
962.summary: The Judicial Council reviewed questions about church discontinuance procedures in Alaska, affirming that only the annual conference can discontinue a church, not district superintendents or cabinets alone.
962.keyHolding: Only the annual conference itself has authority to discontinue a local church; district superintendents, cabinets, or administrative units lack this authority.
962.parties: Alaska Missionary Conference regarding St. Paul United Methodist Church of Fairbanks, Alaska
962.outcome: Affirmed - Bishop's decisions of law upheld regarding discontinuance procedures and authority

963.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the West Virginia Annual Conference Related to the Use by the West Virginia Conference Board of Pension of Funds Invested with the General Board of Pension and Health Benefits
963.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that the West Virginia Conference could use funds from its general deposit account with the General Board of Pension and Health Benefits to pay health care claims, because this account is separate from the restricted pre-1982 pension account.
963.keyHolding: A conference's deposit account at the General Board of Pension and Health Benefits is not subject to the same restrictions as the pre-1982 past service funding account and may be used to pay health care claims.
963.parties: Two retired clergy members of the West Virginia Annual Conference
963.outcome: Bishop's decision affirmed - conference may use deposit account funds for health care claims

964.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the Virginia Annual Conference Related to Clergy Retiree Health Plan Eligibility
964.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed a bishop's ruling that Virginia Annual Conference's requirements for clergy retiree health benefits do not conflict with United Methodist Church law.
964.keyHolding: Annual conference requirements for clergy retiree health plan eligibility are not in conflict with the provisions of the Book of Discipline regarding clergy retirement.

965.title: Request from the Coordinating Council of the Philippines Central Conference for a Declaratory Decision on the Eligibility of a Member of the Judicial Council to Serve as a Trustee of Wesleyan University-Philippines
965.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that a member can serve as trustee of Wesleyan University-Philippines because the university is not an agency or board of the Central Conference, despite being chartered in the Philippines and having trustees appointed by bishops.
965.keyHolding: A Judicial Council member may serve as trustee of an educational institution that is not a board or agency of a central conference, even if the institution reports to and has trustees appointed by the conference.
965.parties: Coordinating Council of the Philippines Central Conference
965.outcome: Judicial Council member eligible to serve as trustee

966.title: Request from the General Council on Finance and Administration for Declaratory Decision on the Meaning, Application and Effect of ¶¶ 405.2(b) and c) Dealing with the Number of Bishops Assigned to Each Jurisdiction
966.summary: The General Council on Finance and Administration requested a ruling on how to interpret paragraphs about assigning bishops to jurisdictions, but the request was withdrawn.
966.keyHolding: Request for declaratory decision was withdrawn before ruling.
966.parties: General Council on Finance and Administration

967.title: Appeal from the Decision of the Court of Appeals in the Western Jurisdiction in the Matter of the Rev. Karen Dammann
967.summary: The Judicial Council deferred consideration of an appeal from the Western Jurisdiction regarding Rev. Karen Dammann until October 2003.
967.keyHolding: The Judicial Council deferred review of the Western Jurisdiction's decision in the Rev. Karen Dammann matter.
967.parties: Appeal from Western Jurisdiction Court of Appeals regarding Rev. Karen Dammann

968.title: In Re: Request From The Kansas West Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision on the Meaning, Application, and Effect of ¶¶ 246.12, 331, 621, 622 and 623 of the 2000 Discipline as Related to Equitable Compensation of Women Pastors
968.summary: The Kansas West Annual Conference wanted to provide $50,000 in lump sum payments to female pastors who experienced gender pay inequity. The Judicial Council ruled that addressing gender pay gaps is allowed, but the specific method of distribution based only on years of service was unlawful.
968.keyHolding: Annual conferences may develop remedies for gender-based clergy compensation inequity, but any remedy must consider individual pastor performance and not conflict with Disciplinary provisions regarding local church responsibility for setting compensation.
968.outcome: Conference directed to amend implementation method and resubmit for approval; Judicial Council retains jurisdiction

969.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the South Carolina Annual Conference on the Applicability of ¶604.14 of the 2000 Discipline Concerning Open Meetings to the Clergy Session of the Annual Conference
969.summary: A lay member asked whether open meeting rules apply to clergy sessions, but the bishop correctly ruled this was an improper request because it wasn't connected to specific conference business being discussed.
969.keyHolding: Questions of law must be germane to regular business of the annual conference and connected to specific action taken during deliberation of a matter.
969.parties: Lay member of South Carolina Annual Conference vs. Bishop J. Lawrence McCleskey

970.title: Review of the Bishop's Decision of Law in the Illinois Great Rivers Annual Conference on the Constitutionality of the Conference Housing Policy Adopted at its June 2003 Session
970.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed a bishop's ruling that an annual conference's housing policy for clergy couples does not violate the constitutional requirement of inclusivity, since it provides housing for all appointed staff regardless of marital status.
970.keyHolding: A conference housing policy that provides housing for each appointed staff person irrespective of marital status does not violate the constitutional inclusivity requirements of Article IV.
970.parties: Clergy member requesting decision of law regarding Illinois Great Rivers Annual Conference housing policy

971.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the West Michigan Annual Conference Related to the Authority of the Bishop to Replace or Renominate Members on the Annual Conference Board of Ordained Ministry
971.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that a bishop cannot remove or decline to renominate members of the Board of Ordained Ministry during their elected term, even if they are under clergy suspension. Rev. Ventura retained his position on the board despite being suspended from ministerial duties.
971.keyHolding: Bishops have no authority to remove members of the Board of Ordained Ministry during their elected terms; their only authority is to nominate members after proper consultation.
971.parties: West Michigan Annual Conference clergy and lay members questioning Bishop Linda Lee's decision regarding Rev. Oscar Ventura
971.outcome: Reversed - Bishop's decision found to be in error; Rev. Ventura remains on the Board of Ordained Ministry

972.title: Request from the California-Pacific Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision on the Meaning, Application and Effect of ¶ 359 As Related to the Right of Persons To Be Accompanied by Another Person to Any Hearings
972.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that clergy members facing administrative complaints or judicial proceedings have the right to choose their advocate and change advocates when circumstances require it, while maintaining confidentiality requirements.
972.keyHolding: A respondent in administrative or judicial proceedings has the right to select and change their advocate when warranted, subject to confidentiality requirements and without impeding the orderly process.
972.outcome: Clergy have the right to select and change advocates in administrative and judicial proceedings while maintaining confidentiality

973.title: Request from the California-Pacific Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision on the Meaning, Application and Effect of ¶¶ 352 and 359 of the 2000 Discipline as Related to an Involuntary Leave of Absence and an Administrative Complaint
973.summary: The Judicial Council clarified that when district superintendents request to place a clergy member on involuntary leave of absence, this does not constitute filing a formal administrative complaint under church law.
973.keyHolding: A written request by district superintendents for involuntary leave of absence under ¶ 352.1b is not the same as filing an administrative complaint under ¶ 359.1.
973.outcome: Request granted - distinguished involuntary leave procedures from administrative complaint procedures

974.title: Request from the California-Pacific Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision on the Meaning, Application and Effect of ¶ 359.2 Concerning Access to Written Complaints and Supporting Documents at the Initiation of the Supervisory Process
974.summary: A clergy member facing a complaint has the right to receive and keep copies of the written complaint and all supporting documents from the very beginning of the supervisory process. While confidentiality is important, it cannot be used to prevent the accused clergy from accessing these materials.
974.keyHolding: At the initiation of the supervisory process, respondents have the right not only to examine but to possess the written complaint and any supporting material accompanying it.
974.outcome: Declared that respondents have the right to possess written complaints and supporting documents at the initiation of the supervisory process

975.title: Review of the East Ohio Sexual Ethics Policy as Required by Memorandum 954
975.summary: The Judicial Council reviewed and approved the East Ohio Annual Conference's Sexual Ethics Policy for Clergy, finding it complies with church law and constitutional requirements.
975.keyHolding: The East Ohio Annual Conference Sexual Ethics Policy for Clergy is in compliance with the Constitution, Discipline, and Judicial Council decisions and may be implemented.
975.outcome: Policy approved as constitutional and compliant with church law

976.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the East Ohio Annual Conference on Whether the Annual Conference Had the Authority to Redesignate Certain Funds to Support the Conference's Health Care Benefit Plan
976.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that East Ohio Annual Conference could rename its pension reserve account to include health care, but must honor donor intent from a 1988-92 fundraising campaign by using those funds for pre-1982 clergy pension obligations.
976.keyHolding: Annual conferences have authority to redesignate funds under ¶604.1, but must respect donor intent and use capital campaign funds for their stated purpose of addressing pre-1982 pension obligations.
976.parties: Clergy member of East Ohio Annual Conference requesting episcopal decision of law
976.outcome: Partially affirmed - redesignation authority confirmed but health care allocation restricted by donor intent

977.title: Request From The East Ohio Annual Conference For A Declaratory Decision On The Meaning, Application And Effect Of ¶ 315.6 Of The 2000 Discipline And Whether The Entire Educational Requirements For Election To Probationary Membership And Commissioning Are Set Forth In That Paragraph
977.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that local pastors age 40 or older can become probationary members and be commissioned without a bachelor's degree if they complete the specific requirements in ¶ 315.6, including Course of Study and Advanced Course of Study.
977.keyHolding: Paragraph 315.6 provides an alternative educational pathway for local pastors seeking probationary membership and commissioning that does not require completion of a bachelor's degree.
977.outcome: The Judicial Council clarified that ¶ 315.6 sets forth complete educational requirements for local pastors seeking probationary membership without requiring a bachelor's degree

978.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the New England Annual Conference on Whether it Is Proper for the Annual Conference to Provide Funds "for a Ministry Directed Specifically Towards Gays, Lesbians, Bisexuals and Transsexuals, Such as the Cambridge Welcoming Ministries."
978.summary: A local church asked whether the annual conference could fund ministry to LGBTQ persons, but the Judicial Council affirmed the bishop's ruling that the question was moot since no such funding was planned or before the conference.
978.keyHolding: Questions of law that do not relate to business before the annual conference session are considered moot and hypothetical, and no ruling need be made.
978.parties: The Visioning and Administrative Board of Houlton United Methodist Church
978.outcome: Affirmed - Bishop's decision that question was moot and hypothetical upheld

979.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the Western New York Annual Conference Related to a Motion Made During the 2002 Session of the Annual Conference and the Reasons for That Motion Not Being Ruled out of Order
979.summary: The Judicial Council declined to rule on a bishop's decision regarding parliamentary procedure at an annual conference session, finding it lacked jurisdiction over such matters.
979.keyHolding: The Judicial Council lacks jurisdiction to review questions of parliamentary procedure that do not meet the requirements of ¶ 2607.6.
979.outcome: No Jurisdiction - Judicial Council declined to rule due to lack of jurisdiction over parliamentary procedure matters

980.title: In Re: The Rev. Karen Dammann
980.summary: The Judicial Council reversed a decision not to bring charges against Rev. Karen Dammann after she admitted to being in a same-sex relationship, ruling that committees must enforce church law even when they disagree with it.
980.keyHolding: When agreed facts establish conduct that the Discipline declares incompatible with Christian teaching, committees must certify charges regardless of their personal views on the law.
980.parties: Bishop Elias G. Galvan v. Rev. Karen T. Dammann
980.outcome: Reversed and remanded with specific directions for new hearing and committee composition requirements

981.title: Request from the California-Pacific Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision on Whether or Not a Local Pastor Has the Right to a Trial When the Pastor Receives in Notice in Writing That He or She Is Being Discontinued from Appointment for Allegedly Violating Specifically One or More of the Chargeable Offenses Listed in ¶2702.1 of the 2000 Discipline
981.summary: The California-Pacific Annual Conference asked whether local pastors have the right to a trial when they are discontinued from appointment for allegedly committing chargeable offenses. The Judicial Council deferred this decision to Spring 2004.
981.keyHolding: This case was deferred and no legal principle was established at this time.

982.title: Request from the California-Pacific Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision on the Meaning, Application, and Effect of ¶¶ 346 and 359.1 of the 2000 Discipline as to Whether a Local Pastor Has the Right to Trial after Being Discontinued from Appointment
982.summary: The Judicial Council clarified that local pastors have the right to trial when accused of chargeable offenses, even if their appointment is terminated, but only if the termination notice clearly identifies itself as a formal complaint with proper signatures and procedures.
982.keyHolding: The termination of an appointment does not negate a local pastor's right to trial when accused of chargeable offenses, provided the accusation follows proper complaint procedures.
982.outcome: Clarified that local pastors retain trial rights when properly accused of chargeable offenses, regardless of appointment termination

983.title: Review of Revised Structure of the Louisiana Annual Conference as Required by Decision 900
983.summary: The Louisiana Annual Conference's structure and rules were found to still be invalid because they didn't properly follow requirements in the Book of Discipline, despite multiple attempts to fix the problems.
983.keyHolding: Annual conference structures must comply exactly with Disciplinary requirements and cannot selectively paraphrase or modify mandatory language from the Discipline.
983.outcome: Remanded - structure declared null and void until deficiencies are corrected

984.title: IN RE: Declaratory Decision Regarding the Meaning, Application or Effect of 304.3 and 2702.1(b) of the 2000 Discipline
984.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that the statement in ¶304.3 declaring homosexuality incompatible with Christian teaching is an official church declaration that makes the practice of homosexuality a chargeable offense under church law.
984.keyHolding: The General Conference's statement in ¶304.3 that homosexuality is incompatible with Christian teaching constitutes an official church declaration that makes homosexual practice a chargeable offense under ¶2702.1(b).
984.outcome: Declaratory decision affirming that homosexual practice is a chargeable offense under church law

985.title: Request for a Declaratory Decision from the General Conference Regarding the Application of the Discipline to Actions of an Annual Conference in a Church Trial and the Meaning, Application or Effect of 304.3 of the Discipline to the Findings of the Trial Court
985.summary: The Judicial Council ruled it cannot review trial court findings in clergy cases, but affirmed that bishops cannot appoint clergy found by trial courts to be self-avowed practicing homosexuals.
985.keyHolding: A bishop may not appoint a clergy person who has been found by a trial court to be a self-avowed, practicing homosexual, though it is up to the trial court to make that determination.
985.outcome: No jurisdiction to review trial court findings; bishops prohibited from appointing clergy found to be self-avowed practicing homosexuals

986.title: Request from the General Conference for a Declaratory Decision Concerning Pastoral Leadership in Paying Apportionments as a Chargeable Offense under ¶ 2702
986.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that pastors cannot be charged with an offense simply for being unwilling to lead their church to pay apportionments in full, since pastors share this responsibility with many other lay and clergy leaders.
986.keyHolding: A pastor's unwillingness to lead a local church toward full payment of apportionments does not constitute a chargeable offense under ¶ 2702 because pastors do not carry this responsibility alone and should only be held accountable for their own personal actions.
986.outcome: Pastor unwillingness to lead apportionment payment is not a chargeable offense

987.title: Request from the Western Michigan Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision on the Meaning, Application and Effect of the Discipline to the Addition of Domestic Partner Benefits to the Conference Health Benefits Policy
987.summary: The Western Michigan Annual Conference requested a declaratory decision about adding domestic partner benefits to their health benefits policy. The Judicial Council ruled it had no jurisdiction because the request did not cite specific Discipline paragraphs as required.
987.keyHolding: The Judicial Council lacks jurisdiction over declaratory decision requests that do not seek determination of the meaning, application or effect of any specific paragraph of the Discipline as required under ¶ 2610.
987.outcome: No jurisdiction - request did not cite specific Discipline paragraphs

988.title: Review of Kansas West Annual Conference Equitable Compensation Plan for Women Clergy as Required by Decision 968
988.summary: The Judicial Council approved Kansas West Annual Conference's revised plan to address gender-based pay inequities for women clergy through a case-by-case review process.
988.keyHolding: A plan to remedy gender inequity in clergy compensation is permissible if its method of implementation does not result in further discrimination on the basis of gender.
988.outcome: Plan approved as compliant with Decision 968 requirements

989.title: Request from the 2004 General Conference for a Declaratory Decision on the Constitutionality of Calendar Item 1017, as Adopted, with respect to the Lay Membership of Annual Conferences
989.summary: The 2004 General Conference tried to add conference scouting coordinators as lay members of annual conferences, but this violated constitutional requirements for annual conference membership.
989.keyHolding: General Conference cannot add new categories of ex-officio lay members to annual conferences beyond those specified in the Constitution.
989.outcome: Calendar Item 1017 declared unconstitutional and null and void

990.title: Request from the 2004 General Conference for a Declaratory Decision on the Meaning, Application, and Effect of the Provisions of ¶ 705.3(j) of the Discipline with Respect to the Membership of the Connectional Table
990.summary: The General Conference asked whether rules for general agency membership applied to the new Connectional Table. The Judicial Council ruled that since the Connectional Table was intentionally created as a different type of entity rather than a general agency, those membership rules don't apply.
990.keyHolding: The Connectional Table is not a general agency, so general agency membership provisions do not apply to it, though its membership must still comply with constitutional requirements.
990.outcome: Provisions of ¶705.3(j) do not apply to Connectional Table, but membership must be constitutional

991.title: Request from the 2004 General Conference for a Declaratory Decision on Whether Calendar Item 1498, as Adopted, Violates any Disciplinary Provision with Respect to Racial Ethnic Caucus Membership at Connectional Table
991.summary: The General Conference asked if allowing racial ethnic caucuses to nominate members to the new Connectional Table violated church law. The Judicial Council ruled it does not violate any rules and is constitutional.
991.keyHolding: Legislation providing for nomination of Connectional Table members from racial ethnic caucuses does not violate disciplinary provisions and is constitutional because the Connectional Table is not a general program board subject to the restrictions in Decision 601.
991.outcome: Constitutional - racial ethnic caucus nominations to Connectional Table permitted

992.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the North Central New York Annual Conference Concerning Approval of a Candidate for Commissioning as Probationary Member by the Clergy Session
992.summary: The Judicial Council declined to review a bishop's decision about approving a candidate for commissioning, saying it was a parliamentary matter for the annual conference to handle.
992.keyHolding: The Judicial Council lacks jurisdiction over parliamentary rulings, which are the prerogative of the presiding officer and appealable to the annual conference.
992.parties: North Central New York Annual Conference

993.title: Request from the 2004 General Conference for a Declaratory Decision on the Constitutionality of Calendar Item 1167, as Adopted, with Respect to Lay Membership on the Committee on Investigation
993.summary: The General Conference asked whether lay members could serve with voting rights on committees that investigate clergy misconduct. The Judicial Council ruled this unconstitutional, saying only clergy can vote on matters involving clergy character and relationships.
993.keyHolding: Lay professing members cannot serve with voice and vote on committees on investigation of clergy members because such matters are restricted to clergy under Paragraph 31 of the Constitution.
993.outcome: Calendar Item 1167 declared unconstitutional - lay members cannot serve on committees on investigation

994.title: Request from the Virginia Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision on the Meaning, Application, and Effect of the 2000 Discipline and Specifically ¶ 608 thereof, to "Equipping the Church: An Organizational Plan for the Virginia Conference of The United Methodist Church," as Adopted
994.summary: The Virginia Annual Conference asked the Judicial Council to determine if their new organizational plan was legal under church law. The Judicial Council ruled that the plan was consistent with Discipline requirements.
994.keyHolding: The Virginia Conference Organizational Plan is consistent with ¶ 608 of the 2000 Discipline regarding annual conference restructuring authority.

995.title: Request from the Virginia Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision on the Meaning, Application and Effect of ¶ 352.1(b) [Involuntary Leave of Absence] and ¶ 356.2 [Voluntary Retirement] of the 2000 Discipline Where a Clergy Member Requested Voluntary Retirement, But was Placed On Involuntary Leave of Absence by the Clergy Session
995.summary: The Judicial Council reversed a Virginia Annual Conference decision to place a clergy member on involuntary leave of absence instead of granting his requested voluntary retirement, finding multiple procedural violations and ordering his reinstatement with back pay.
995.keyHolding: Fair process can never be presumed but must be clearly demonstrated at each stage of proceedings, especially proceedings that contemplate an involuntary consequence.
995.outcome: Reversed and remanded with directions to reinstate clergy member with full benefits retroactive to June 14, 2004

996.title: Request from the Illinois Great Rivers Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision on the Authority of a Bishop to Overrule the Judicial Council and Deny an Individual's Request for Jury Trial
996.summary: An annual conference asked whether a bishop could overrule a Judicial Council decision about someone's right to a trial, but the Judicial Council said the question was too hypothetical and didn't provide specific facts or cite specific Discipline paragraphs.
996.keyHolding: The Judicial Council lacks jurisdiction over requests for declaratory decisions that are abstract, hypothetical, and fail to cite specific disciplinary provisions or factual allegations.

997.title: Request from the Wisconsin Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision on the Constitutionality of ¶ 346.1 of the 2000 Discipline Concerning Discontinuance of Local Pastors
997.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that bishops have constitutional authority to discontinue local pastors without trial procedures, as long as there are no pending charges against them.
997.keyHolding: A bishop's authority to discontinue a local pastor under ¶ 346.1 without trial procedures is constitutional when no charges are pending under ¶ 2702.
997.outcome: Constitutional - bishop's authority to discontinue local pastors upheld

998.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the North Georgia Annual Conference Concerning the Propriety of a Resolution Entitled "A Resolution From The South Georgia Annual Conference – Support for a Marriage Amendment to the Georgia Constitution" under the Discipline
998.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed a bishop's ruling that annual conference resolutions supporting a Georgia constitutional amendment defining marriage as between one man and one woman did not violate church law protecting homosexual persons' basic rights.
998.keyHolding: Annual conference resolutions supporting state constitutional amendments defining marriage as between one man and one woman do not violate Discipline provisions protecting basic human rights and civil liberties of homosexual persons.
998.parties: Member of North Georgia Annual Conference requesting ruling on resolution legality

999.title: Appeal of Board of Missions and Church Extension on Question of Responsibility of Pension of D. W. Nichols, et al.
999.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that the Southern California-Arizona Conference is not responsible for pension payments to retired ministers for years they served in Mission Conferences abroad, only for service within the United States conference.
999.keyHolding: Annual Conferences are only responsible for pension payments covering years of service performed within their own conference or its predecessor, not for service in Mission Conferences.
999.parties: Board of Missions and Church Extension
999.outcome: Board of Missions and Church Extension appeal upheld; Southern California-Arizona Conference not liable for mission service pension costs

1000.title: Request for a Declaratory Decision by the Northern Illinois Annual Conference for Review of its Revised Plan of Structure and as Required by Decision 909
1000.summary: The Northern Illinois Annual Conference's revised organizational structure was approved as compliant with church law after previous restructuring attempts had been rejected.
1000.keyHolding: An annual conference's revised plan of structure that establishes a Conference Council on Ministries and Director of Connectional Ministries in compliance with ¶607 and ¶608.1 of the Discipline meets constitutional requirements.
1000.outcome: Constitutional - revised plan approved for implementation

1001.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the New York Annual Conference Concerning Whether an Elder's Request for Trial Can be Denied Where the Bishop Determines that a Complaint Will be Handled Administratively
1001.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that a bishop's decision about whether clergy trial rights are satisfied by administrative processes was void because the legal question wasn't related to actual conference business.
1001.keyHolding: Questions of law must be germane to the regular business of the Annual Conference and cannot be moot or hypothetical.
1001.parties: Two elders in full connection from New York Annual Conference
1001.outcome: Bishop's decision declared void - question was moot and hypothetical

1002.title: Request from the 2004 General Conference for a Declaratory Decision on the Meaning, Application, and Effect of ¶102 of the Discipline to Calendar Item 1514, as Adopted, with Respect to the Doctrinal Standards of The United Methodist Church
1002.summary: The General Conference asked whether a resolution affirming commitment to basic Christian doctrines violated church law. The Judicial Council ruled the resolution violated constitutional restrictions and was null and void.
1002.keyHolding: Resolutions that attempt to alter or expand doctrinal standards beyond constitutional limits violate the Restrictive Rules and are improperly before General Conference.
1002.outcome: Calendar Item 1514 declared null and void as violating Restrictive Rules I, II, and V

1003.title: Request from the 2004 General Conference for a Declaratory Decision on the Legality and Constitutionality of Petition 40325, as Adopted, Dealing with the General Board of Pensions and Health Benefits
1003.summary: The 2004 General Conference asked the Judicial Council to determine if legislation about the General Board of Pensions and Health Benefits was legal and constitutional.
1003.keyHolding: The document provides only procedural information about oral hearings without stating the actual legal holding or decision.
1003.outcome: Outcome not specified in provided text

1004.title: Request from the Illinois Great Rivers Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision on the Legality under the 2000 Discipline of a Resolution Expressing Appreciation of the Girl Scouts of the USA
1004.summary: The Illinois Great Rivers Annual Conference asked the Judicial Council to review a resolution appreciating Girl Scouts USA, but the Council declined because the request didn't cite specific Discipline paragraphs as required.
1004.keyHolding: Declaratory decision requests must cite specific paragraphs of the Discipline to be reviewed, which is an essential jurisdictional requirement.

1005.title: Request from the Alaska Missionary Conference for a Declaratory Decision on the Constitutionality of 2004 General Conference Calendar Item 1017
1005.summary: The Alaska Missionary Conference asked whether adding a conference scouting coordinator to annual conference membership was constitutional. The Judicial Council noted this question had already been answered in Decision 989.
1005.keyHolding: The constitutionality question regarding adding conference scouting coordinator to annual conference membership was already resolved in Decision 989.

1006.title: Reconsideration of Decision 993
1006.summary: The Judicial Council reconsidered its previous decision that struck down parts of General Conference legislation, clarifying how church trial committees should be composed when the unconstitutional portions are removed.
1006.keyHolding: When the Judicial Council holds General Conference legislation amending the Book of Discipline to be unconstitutional, the language reverts to its prior form with respect to the portion held unconstitutional.
1006.parties: Judicial Council on its own motion
1006.outcome: Clarified the composition of committees on investigation after removing unconstitutional provisions

1007.title: Request from the Northern Illinois Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision on the Meaning, Application and Effect of ¶¶ 715 and 2532.6 of the 2000 Discipline with Respect to Disabled-Accessibility in Local Church and District Office Facilities
1007.summary: The Northern Illinois Annual Conference requested a ruling on disabled-accessibility requirements for church facilities, but the Judicial Council declined to hear the case because it couldn't determine if the request was properly authorized during a special session.
1007.keyHolding: The powers of a special session of an annual conference are limited to the powers specified in the call for that special session.
1007.outcome: No Jurisdiction - declined due to insufficient record of proper authorization

1008.title: Request from the 2004 General Conference for a Declaratory Decision on the Legality and Constitutionality of Petition 40325 (Calendar Item 1031), as Adopted, Dealing with the General Board of Pension and Health Benefits
1008.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that most provisions of the new Clergy Retirement Security Program (CRSP) pension plan are constitutional, but one section improperly delegates General Conference authority to the pension board.
1008.keyHolding: While most of the CRSP pension plan provisions are constitutional, Section A5.1(b)(iii) unconstitutionally delegates General Conference legislative authority to the General Board of Pension and Health Benefits.
1008.parties: 2004 General Conference requesting declaratory decision regarding General Board of Pension and Health Benefits
1008.outcome: Mostly constitutional - CRSP implementation approved except for one section found to be unconstitutional delegation

1009.title: Request from the Illinois Great Rivers Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision on the Meaning, Application and Effect of ¶¶ 31 and 605.6 of the 2000 Discipline with Respect to the Phrase "Conference Relations of Clergy" and the Authority of an Annual Conference Clergy Session to Create Programs, Study Teams and Task Forces on Matters Pertaining to the Maintenance, Enhancement, and Support of the Conference Relations of Clergy
1009.summary: The Judicial Council ruled that only the full annual conference, not just the clergy session meeting in executive session, has authority to create programs and task forces related to clergy conference relations.
1009.keyHolding: The executive session of clergy members in full connection cannot create programs, study teams, and task forces on matters pertaining to the maintenance, enhancement, and support of the conference relations of clergy - such action can only be taken by the plenary session of the annual conference.
1009.outcome: Executive session authority limited; only full annual conference can create such programs

1010.title: Request from the California-Pacific Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision on the Constitutionality, Meaning, Application, and Effect of ¶ 359.3c(2) of the 2000 Discipline Concerning Administrative Location
1010.summary: The Judicial Council reversed a California-Pacific Annual Conference decision to place a clergy member on administrative location because the hearing process violated fair process requirements by allowing bishops and district superintendents to participate.
1010.keyHolding: Bishops and district superintendents cannot participate as voting members in administrative location hearings as this violates fair process requirements under the Discipline.
1010.parties: California-Pacific Annual Conference and a clergy member in full connection
1010.outcome: Administrative location decision reversed; clergy member reinstated with full retroactive benefits

1011.title: Request from the California-Pacific Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision on the Meaning, Application and Effect of ¶ 633 of the 2000 Discipline Concerning the Responsibilities of the Administrative Review Committee
1011.summary: The Judicial Council clarified that administrative review committees can only check whether proper procedures were followed in disciplinary actions, not judge the merits of decisions or determine if processes are constitutional.
1011.keyHolding: Administrative review committees are limited to ensuring procedural compliance with the Discipline and cannot review substantive merits of decisions or determine constitutionality of processes.
1011.outcome: Clarified scope of administrative review committee authority as procedural only

1012.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the California-Pacific Annual Conference Concerning Legality of Incapacity Leave of a Clergy Member
1012.summary: The Judicial Council affirmed a bishop's ruling that a clergy member was legally placed on incapacity leave and remained legally on such leave until 2004.
1012.keyHolding: Incapacity leave properly granted under ¶355 procedures remains valid until the clergy member provides medical evidence of recovery and receives a new appointment from the bishop.
1012.parties: Elder requesting bishop's decision of law regarding Rev. Ana Maria Dominguez's incapacity leave
1012.outcome: Bishop's decision of law affirmed - incapacity leave was legal throughout the questioned period

1013.title: Request from the California-Pacific Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision on the Meaning, Application and Effect of ¶¶ 612 and 623 of the 2000 Discipline Concerning Minimum Base Compensation and Base Compensation Supplements for Clergy Support
1013.summary: Annual conference finance councils must consult in good faith with equitable compensation commissions when preparing clergy support budgets, and conferences must provide adequate funding for minimum clergy compensation.
1013.keyHolding: The conference council on finance and administration must consult with the conference commission on equitable compensation before recommending clergy support budgets, and the annual conference has sole responsibility to adopt budgets that support minimum base compensation requirements.
1013.outcome: Conference finance councils must consult with equitable compensation commissions and conferences must adequately fund minimum clergy compensation

1014.title: Request from Kansas East Conference for a Declaratory Decision on the Meaning, Application, and Effect of ¶¶ 246.12 and 333 of the 2000 Discipline to a Requirement that Full-Time Clergy Contribute to the Cost of Health Insurance
1014.summary: The Kansas East Annual Conference asked whether it could require full-time clergy to contribute 4% of their salary toward health insurance costs. The Judicial Council ruled this was permissible under church law.
1014.keyHolding: Annual conferences may require clergy to contribute to health insurance costs without violating provisions regarding compensation setting or equitable salaries.
1014.outcome: Constitutional - health insurance contribution policy permitted

1015.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the Rocky Mountain Annual Conference Concerning Structure Modification for the Rocky Mountain Annual Conference
1015.summary: The Judicial Council found that a bishop's decision about conference restructuring was properly requested, but incomplete documentation prevented a full review, so the matter was sent back for more information.
1015.keyHolding: Questions of law about conference structure are properly raised when restructuring legislation is pending before the Annual Conference, and the Judicial Council has jurisdiction to review such decisions of law.
1015.parties: Rocky Mountain Annual Conference members requesting decision of law
1015.outcome: Remanded with instructions to submit complete documentation by July 15, 2005

1016.title: Appeal of Rev. Ngoy Daniel Mulunda Nyanga Concerning Actions of the West Congo Annual Conference and the Central Congo Central Conference
1016.summary: A clergy member appealed decisions made by conferences in the Congo, but withdrew the appeal before the Judicial Council could make a decision.
1016.keyHolding: Appeal was withdrawn before judicial determination.

1017.title: Petition for Reconsideration of Decision 997
1017.summary: The Judicial Council refused to reconsider an earlier decision (Decision 997), effectively letting that previous ruling stand.
1017.keyHolding: The Judicial Council denied the petition for reconsideration without providing additional reasoning.

1018.title: Petition for Reconsideration of Memorandum 1001
1018.summary: The Judicial Council denied a request to reconsider their previous Memorandum 1001.
1018.keyHolding: The Judicial Council denied the petition for reconsideration of Memorandum 1001.

1019.title: Request from the Tennessee Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision on the Meaning, Application and Effect of ¶¶ 705.5(e), 705.6(a) and 706.1 of the 2004 Discipline with Respect to the Allocation by the Secretary of the General Conference of Additional (At-Large) Members of the General Program Boards and General Agencies
1019.summary: The Tennessee Annual Conference asked the Judicial Council to clarify rules about how additional members are allocated to church boards and agencies, but the Council ruled it had no authority to decide this matter.
1019.keyHolding: The Judicial Council lacks jurisdiction under ¶2610 to issue declaratory decisions on matters that do not relate to annual conference work.

1020.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the California-Nevada Annual Conference Related to the Adoption by the Annual Conference of a Definition for "Status" and the Refusal to Adopt a Definition for "Practicing" with Respect to the Enforceability of ¶ 304.3 of the 2004 Discipline in the Annual Conference
1020.summary: The California-Nevada Annual Conference defined "status" to include sexual orientation and refused to define "practicing homosexual." The Judicial Council ruled that neither action affects the enforceability of clergy ordination standards in ¶ 304.3.
1020.keyHolding: Annual conference definitions or refusals to define terms do not void, violate, or pre-empt the enforceability of ¶ 304.3 of the Discipline regarding clergy ordination standards.
1020.parties: Member of California-Nevada Annual Conference requesting ruling from Bishop Beverly J. Shamana
1020.outcome: Affirmed - Bishop's decisions of law were upheld on all questions

1021.title: Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the Pacific Northwest Annual Conference Related to the Adoption of a Petition Entitled "Affirming Our Unity Amongst Diversity Of Opinion."
1021.summary: The Judicial Council partially reversed a bishop's decision that refused to answer legal questions about an annual conference petition affirming unity amid diversity of opinion on faith matters. The Council found the petition was a valid historical statement that didn't violate church law.
1021.keyHolding: An annual conference petition making historical statements about diversity of opinion in the Christian community does not violate church law and bishops must address properly framed questions of law rather than dismissing them as theological interpretation.
1021.parties: Pacific Northwest Annual Conference clergy member questioning adopted petition
1021.outcome: Partially Reversed - bishop must address legal questions but petition itself upheld as lawful

1022.title: Revised Structure of the Louisiana Annual Conference as Required by Decision 983
1022.summary: The Judicial Council approved the Louisiana Annual Conference's revised structure after multiple prior rejections, finding it now complies with church law.
1022.keyHolding: The Louisiana Annual Conference Structure and Rules now conform with the 2000 Discipline and Judicial Council decisions after required revisions.

1023.title: Continuation of Review of Bishop's Decision of Law in the Rocky Mountain Annual Conference Concerning Structure Modification for the Rocky Mountain Annual Conference as Required by Decision 1015
1023.summary: The Rocky Mountain Annual Conference proposed a new organizational structure that included a Board of Stewards with broad powers, but the Judicial Council ruled it violated church law and declared it invalid.
1023.keyHolding: Annual conference structural plans must comply with the Discipline and Judicial Council decisions, and annual conferences cannot delegate their authority to other bodies.
1023.outcome: The proposed structural plan was declared null, void, and of no effect for violating the Discipline

1024.title: Request from the Minnesota Annual Conference for a Declaratory Decision on the Meaning, Application and Effect of ¶ 606.9(b) of the 2004 Discipline with Respect to the Maintenance by Annual Conference Officers of a Supervisory File Not Accessible or Reviewable by the Individual in Whose Name the File is Kept
1024.summary: The Minnesota Annual Conference asked whether annual conference officers can maintain supervisory files that clergy cannot access, even when referenced in their personnel files. The Judicial Council ruled that ¶606.9(b) only covers personnel records which must be accessible to individuals, not supervisory records.
1024.keyHolding: Paragraph 606.9(b) provides access rights only to personnel records maintained by annual conferences, and makes no reference to supervisory records which are governed by different provisions.
1024.outcome: Personnel records under ¶606.9(b) must be accessible to individuals; supervisory records are governed by separate provisions

1025.title: Request from the Northern Illinois Annual Conference for Declaratory Decision on the Meaning, Application and Effect of ¶¶ 715 and 2532.6 of the 2004 Discipline with Respect to Disabled-Accessibility in Local Church and District Office Facilities
1025.summary: The Judicial Council ruled on accessibility requirements for UMC facilities and communications, clarifying that bishops (not district superintendents) assign responsibility for accessibility audits, and that accessibility notices must appear on all publicity for events held in non-accessible facilities.
